meetings.title: Durham City Council Nov 18, 2019 (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: With Council Member Vernetta Alston granted an excused absence (6-0), the Durham City Council on November 18, 2019 approved 6-0 the consent agenda (excluding Item 33) and heard Police Chief Cerelyn Davis's Third Quarter Crime Report (Item 19), where Latinx advocates pressed for lifting U-visa time restrictions and Mayor Schewel committed to action within two weeks. Council voted unanimously 6-0 to designate both Mutual Plaza (Item 20) and the W.C. and Mary Hinton Lyon House (Item 21) as local historic landmarks, and voted 6-0 to approve the Bethpage Office FLUM amendment and rezoning (Item 22) despite Council Member Charlie Reece's reluctance regarding the lack of a development plan. Council also approved 6-0 UDO text amendments for FEMA flood map updates (Item 23) and Omnibus 13 (Item 24), rezoned 1107 Chalk Level Road for 97 townhomes 6-0 (Item 25) while expressing disappointment that neighborhood negotiations removed an affordable housing density bonus, held the FY 2020-2025 Consolidated Plan needs hearing (Item 26), continued the Urban Avenue street closing (Item 27) to December 16, and approved Mayor's Hispanic/Latino Committee appointments 6-0 (Item 33).

agenda_items.title: Neighbor Spotlight, History Moment, Reduce Violence Proclamation, and Council Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Javiera Caballero presented the October Neighbor Spotlight to Anne Drennan for the HELP medical equipment loan program, public historian Eddie Davis delivered a History Moment honoring educator Dr. John Harding Lucas Sr., and Council Member Mark-Anthony Middleton read a Reduce Violence Everywhere proclamation accepted by Wanda Boone of Together for Resilient Youth. During announcements, Middleton urged city attention to historic Geer Cemetery upkeep, and City Manager Bonfield highlighted Durham staff panels and awards at the National League of Cities conference.

agenda_items.title: Excused Absences and Consent Agenda (Items 1-18, Pulling Item 33)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted 6-0 to grant excused absences to Vernetta Alston for November 18 and to Mayor Schewel for the December 5 work session. After resident Victoria Peterson pulled Item 33 (Mayor's Hispanic/Latino Committee appointments), council approved Consent Agenda Items 1-18 by a 6-0 vote, including the FY 2020-21 budget schedule, CDBG/HOME/HOPWA consolidated plan consultant, Laurel Oaks and Ross Road housing rehabilitations, Veranda at Whitted School ILA, DCLT loan amendment, Durham County Transit Plan grant, Jordan Lake water storage, Cedar Grove shared economic prosperity contract, and a Police Mobile Command Center.

agenda_items.title: 2019 Third Quarter Crime Report and Public Comment on U-Visas and Gun Violence
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Police Chief Cerelyn Davis reported 32 homicides in the first nine months of 2019 (up from 24 in 2018), a 17% increase in shootings, an 18% decline in sexual assaults, three-year lows in robberies and burglaries, a 5.92-minute average priority-one response time, 97% sworn staffing, and 157 U-visa requests processed YTD (57% approved in Q3). Public speakers voiced conflicting concerns over firearm seizures and stops, funding police hiring and ShotSpotter, and disappointment that DPD had not lifted U-visa time restrictions after six months; Mayor Schewel committed to working with the City Manager and Chief to lift the U-visa limitations within two weeks.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Mutual Plaza Local Historic Landmark Designation (411 W. Chapel Hill St.)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Carla Rosenberg presented the Mutual Plaza landmark request for 1.65 acres covering New Lots 1 and 2 (leaving vacant New Lot 3 undesignated), noting 6-0 Historic Preservation Commission and SHPO support and an estimated $137,000 annual 50% property tax deferral. Council members praised the building's civil rights and Black economic legacy, noted the importance of applying landmark status judiciously, and voted 6-0 to adopt the designation ordinance.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: W.C. and Mary Hinton Lyon House Local Historic Landmark Designation (2423 W. Club Blvd.)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Carla Rosenberg presented the landmark request for the 0.54-acre Prairie/Maya-style W.C. and Mary Hinton Lyon House, submitted by Cynthia de Miranda. Council Member Middleton questioned how council evaluates residential landmarks relative to iconic sites like Mutual Plaza, and de Miranda explained only two examples of the style remain in Durham and the house anchors Club Boulevard's development history. Council voted 6-0 to approve the landmark designation.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Bethpage Office FLUM Amendment and Zoning Map Change (A1800009 / Z1800033)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Emily Struthers presented Tri-Properties' request (represented by Nil Ghosh) to change 23.66 acres at 5621 Chin Page and 3824 Page Road from Industrial Light to Office and Institutional without a development plan, moving the Future Land Use Map from industrial to office/low-medium density residential. While Council Member Charlie Reece expressed strong reservations about approving a rezoning without a development plan, he voted yes alongside colleagues because neighboring Creekside HOA supported removing industrial entitlements. All three required motions passed 6-0.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 6-0 (FLUM Resolution, Consistency Statement, Zoning Ordinance)

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Amendment TC1900003 (FEMA FIRM Flood Insurance Rate Map Updates)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Michael Stock presented technical UDO revisions adopting updated FEMA Flood Insurance Rate Map panels ahead of a December 6, 2019 deadline to maintain National Flood Insurance Program eligibility, already approved by the Board of County Commissioners on October 28 and Planning Commission 12-0. Resident Helen Plass urged stronger urban forest and stormwater protections around flood zones; council approved the consistency statement and text amendment 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Amendment TC1900001 (Omnibus 13)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Michael Stock presented Omnibus 13 technical and minor policy UDO updates, including EAR, domestic chickens, solar access, excluding ADUs from density calculations, Planning Director authority to suspend UDO rules during declared emergencies, and requiring sidewalks on both sides of suburban-tier streets. Residents Helen Plass and Mimi Kessler objected to electronic notice, excluding ADUs from density, and staff emergency suspension powers, while staff clarified emergency suspension requires a formal mayoral or BOCC state-of-emergency declaration and council praised the new suburban sidewalk mandate. Both motions passed 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Zoning Map Change — 1107 Chalk Level Road
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jamie Sunyak presented Eagle Point Properties' request (represented by Mike Tarrant of Stewart Inc.) to rezone 12.17 acres from RS-10 to RS-M for up to 97 for-sale townhomes (with 80% capped at 1,500 sq. ft.), a bus pull-out/shelter, and sidewalk gap construction, reduced from 192 apartments after neighborhood meetings. Mayor Pro Tem Johnson and Mayor Schewel supported the project 6-0 while lamenting that neighborhood negotiations had eliminated Durham's first proposed use of the affordable housing density bonus.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: FY 2020-2025 Consolidated Plan Needs Public Hearing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Wilma Conyers of Community Development outlined the HUD consolidated plan timeline and projected FY 2021 entitlement allocations ($1.9M CDBG, $1M HOME, $160k ESG, $429k HOPWA). Resident Victoria Peterson urged coordinating federal funds with the $95 million affordable housing bond to train and hire local workers; no council vote was required.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Urban Avenue Street Closing and Development Agreement (949 Washington St.)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Director Patrick Young requested continuing the Urban Avenue street closing and Brame Specialty building development agreement due to late applicant easement changes. Mayor Schewel opened the hearing and continued it to December 16, 2019 without objection.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 33: Mayor's Hispanic/Latino Committee Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resident Victoria Peterson challenged the committee's racial diversity and questioned whether leadership appointees were U.S. citizens. Mayor Schewel affirmed that Durham welcomes all residents on boards and commissions regardless of documentation status, Council Member Freeman noted a committee of Black and Hispanic residents advanced racial equity, and council approved the appointments 6-0.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel presided over the November 7, 2019 work session, opening with six members present (Council Member DeDreana Freeman arrived later after a school obligation) and approving excused absences for Schewel's November 21 absence (6-0) as well as the City Manager's priority items (6-0). Water Management officials presented the state's best-tasting drinking water award for the Williams Water Treatment Plant, and Council Member Mark-Anthony Middleton shared remarks honoring his older brother who passed away earlier that morning. Council discussed equitable community engagement constraints versus rapid neighborhood gentrification, reviewed Item 3 on Council intern hiring, HR drug-testing policies, and ban-the-box principles, and resolved a ballot review via a hand vote between Suhayon Paro Castillo Lopez and Vicki Muniz Quinones. All formal procedural motions passed unanimously, ending with a 7-0 vote to settle the agenda and schedule a December 5 Community Conversations discussion.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, Community Conversations Scheduling, and Excused Absences
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel opened the meeting with six members present (DeDreana Freeman joined later). Mayor Pro Tempore Jillian Johnson requested a Council discussion on Community Conversations (scheduled for December 5 due to November 21 absences), Council granted Schewel an excused absence for November 21 (6-0) while noting Freeman and Mark-Anthony Middleton would attend the National League of Cities, and Middleton honored NCCU Homecoming and the passing of his brother.

agenda_items.title: Water Plant Award Recognition and City Manager's Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Water Management staff Vicki Westbrook, Bobby Weisen, and Daryl Kennedy presented the plaque won by the Williams Water Treatment Plant for the best-tasting drinking water in North Carolina. Council then unanimously approved (6-0) the City Manager's priority items adding attachments to Item 4 (Chrysalis Research) and Items 31–32 and adding supplemental Item 33 (Mayor's Hispanic/Latino Committee).

agenda_items.title: Administrative Consent Agenda Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed consent items including the FY2021 budget development schedule (Item 2), Reinvestment Partners rehabilitation at 2816 Ross Rd (Item 6, pulled), the Whitted School affordable housing ILA with Durham County (Item 7, praised by Council), Triangle Land Conservancy watershed land acquisition (Item 11), Cedar Grove Institute Shared Economic Prosperity plan (Item 13, pulled), and the Police Mobile Command Center (Item 15, pulled).

agenda_items.title: Equitable Community Engagement and Gentrification Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members reflected on limitations of conducting community engagement after an agreement is already negotiated versus proactive engagement on upcoming trail projects. Mayor Schewel noted that data showed the area was gentrifying rapidly regardless of individual projects or trails, while members urged cross-departmental coordination across Planning and General Services.

agenda_items.title: Review and Discuss Council Intern Hiring and Onboarding
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council discussed how Council interns are classified as part-time city employees rather than stipend recipients, HR posting and risk-management/drug-testing policies (with one member voicing support for ban-the-box and no objection to drug testing while retaining authority to choose their own intern), and DeDreana Freeman described hosting a school-paid intern from Amherst alongside an Elon intern.

agenda_items.title: Board/Commission Ballot Recount, Hand Vote, and Settling the Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After DeDreana Freeman and staff raised a question regarding an amended ballot by Mark-Anthony Middleton, Council held a hand vote between Suhayon Paro Castillo Lopez (3 hands) and Vicki Muniz Quinones (remainder truncated in digest). Council also amended Item 33 wording and unanimously settled the agenda (Consent 1–18 and 33 as amended; GBA 19; GBA public hearings 20–27; Dec 5 Community Conversations discussion).
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 7-0 (agenda settled); hand vote inconclusive in digest

meetings.title: Durham City Council Nov 4, 2019 (with closed captions)
meetings.executive_summary: With Council Member Mark-Anthony Middleton granted an excused absence due to a family health emergency (6-0), the Durham City Council on November 4, 2019 approved excused absences for Middleton and DeDreana Freeman for the November 21 work session (6-0), passed the consent agenda (excluding pulled Items 3 and 21) by a 6-0 vote, and unanimously voted 6-0 across three motions to rezone 12 GoTriangle parcels at 4809 Farrington Road from Light Industrial back to Residential Suburban Multifamily following cancellation of the Durham-Orange Light Rail project. Council held Item 3 (Mayor's Hispanic/Latino Committee appointments) until the November 7 work session without a vote. The majority of the meeting centered on Item 21, the disposition and redevelopment of the former police headquarters at 505 West Chapel Hill Street, where community speakers debated Akridge and New South Ventures' 33% Black ownership stake and higher purchase price against The Fallon Company and WinnCompanies' staff-recommended proposal featuring upfront payment, 4% LIHTC scattered-site affordable housing, and larger commercial office space; council ultimately voted unanimously 6-0 to authorize the City Manager to negotiate a development agreement with The Fallon Company.

agenda_items.title: Excused Absences, Duke Energy Storm Resiliency Grant, History Moment, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council granted Council Member Mark-Anthony Middleton an excused absence (6-0) due to a family health emergency, accepted a Duke Energy Storm Resiliency Grant for Fire Department swift-water rescue equipment, and heard a History Moment by Eddie Davis honoring Governor William B. Umstead with remarks from his daughter Merle Umstead Ritchie. Council also approved 6-0 excused absences for Council Members Freeman and Middleton for the November 21 work session, heard election reminders ahead of the November 5 municipal election and $95 million housing bond vote, and heard Freeman urge collaboration on youth violence prevention.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Items 3 and 21)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Schewel read the consent agenda, with Council Member Freeman pulling Item 3 (Mayor's Hispanic/Latino Committee appointments) and Item 21 (505 West Chapel Hill Street redevelopment) pulled for full discussion. The remaining consent items—including the Triangle Bikeway Implementation Study ILA with Raleigh, water/sewer rehabilitation contracts, condemnation actions, Youth Work Internship Program ILA, National Sexual Assault Kit Initiative grant, Carver Street Extension inspection amendment, and fiber optic network electronics—passed 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Consolidated FLUM Amendment and Zoning Map Change — 4809 Farrington Road
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jamie Sunyak presented a city-initiated proposal to amend the Future Land Use Map from industrial to low-medium density residential and rezone 12 GoTriangle parcels totaling 23.418 acres on Farrington Road from Light Industrial (previously designated for a light rail operations facility) to RS-M after GoTriangle discontinued the light rail project, noting 12-0 Planning Commission approval. Neighboring residents Ruth Ann McKinney and Philip Post spoke in support of preserving the I-40 tree buffer and watershed protections; council unanimously approved all three required motions 6-0.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 6-0 (FLUM Resolution, Consistency Statement, Zoning Ordinance)

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 3: Mayor's Hispanic/Latino Committee Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Freeman noted that absent Council Member Middleton had indicated a vote tally mix-up and wished to review the appointments before voting. Without objection, Mayor Schewel held Item 3 until the Thursday work session.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Held until Thursday work session (No formal vote)

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 21: Future Disposition and Redevelopment of 505 West Chapel Hill Street
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Project Manager Stacy Poston presented General Services' recommendation to negotiate a development agreement with The Fallon Company (partnered with WinnCompanies, James Rogers, and Dr. Henry McCoy) over finalist Akridge (partnered with New South Ventures). Akridge representatives (Matt Klein, Ken Spaulding, Carl Webb, and Zena Howard) and supporters stressed their $2 million higher offer, single-phase conventional financing, and 33% local Black equity ownership through NSV Development, while Fallon/Winn speakers (Sherrod Banks, Joe Fallon, Gilbert Winn, Shawnie Wilcox, and former Mayor Bill Bell) and staff highlighted upfront cash payment (95% at execution), 4% LIHTC scattered-site affordable housing in perpetuity, and major downtown office capacity. While expressing regret over Fallon's unspecified minority equity percentage and commending Akridge's local equity partnership, all six present council members praised staff's thorough evaluation and voted 6-0 to select The Fallon Company.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel presided over the October 24, 2019 work session with all seven council members seated, unanimously approving (7-0) the City Manager's priority items including a closed session request under NCGS 143-318.11(a)(6). During Citizens Matters, local artists Marshall Botvinnik and Alyssa Noble (Durham Independent Dance Artists) proposed an $800,000 municipal arts grant program, which Mayor Schewel referred to the Cultural Advisory Board for evaluation. Council also reviewed pulled consent items including the NCCU Participatory Budgeting Cycle 1 evaluation (Item 6), landfill groundwater monitoring and formerly incarcerated applicant outreach (Item 9), Equity and Inclusion Director Deborah Giles's clarification that workforce diversity is not enforced under the UBE ordinance (Item 13), and the City/County 50-slot Youth Work Internship Program (Item 23), alongside the Recreation Advisory Commission's annual report (Item 28). Council nominated appointees to the Cultural Advisory Board and Hispanic/Latino Committee, noted the Farrington Road rezoning of the former light rail facility site (Item 29), and voted 7-0 to settle the agenda and enter closed session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and City Manager's Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel called the work session to order. Council voted 7-0 to approve the City Manager's priority items: a closed session at meeting's end under NCGS 143-318.11(a)(6) regarding a personnel complaint/grievance, a packet attachment for Citizen Matter Item 31 (Marshall Botvinnik), and noting Item 33 (George O'Welch) would not appear.

agenda_items.title: Administrative Consent Agenda Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed 27 consent items including Michael Page's nomination to Discovery Durham representing NCCU (Item 4), the Triangle Bikeway Implementation Study ILA with Raleigh (Item 8), water/sewer and stormwater engineering contracts, and automated refuse collection trucks. Items 9, 13, and 23 were pulled for discussion.

agenda_items.title: Citizens Matters / Public Comment (Arts Grant Proposal and Policing)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Speakers included Chris Tiffany, a resident recounting alleged police stops and retaliation, Marshall Botvinnik proposing an $800,000 arts grant program ($15,000–$40,000 operating grants and $1,000–$15,000 project grants), and Alyssa Noble (DIDA / Anna Dance Company) highlighting sub-minimum wages in self-produced local dance. Mayor Schewel referred the arts proposal to the Cultural Advisory Board.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Items (PB Evaluation, Landfill Monitoring, Workforce Diversity, Youth Internships)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council briefly discussed the NCCU Participatory Budgeting Cycle 1 evaluation (Item 6), questioned Water Management Director Don Greeley on landfill monitoring and barriers for formerly incarcerated applicants (Item 9), heard Equity and Inclusion Director Deborah Giles clarify that workforce diversity data is collected for Council though outside the compliance ordinance (Item 13), and confirmed with OEWD's James Dickens that Durham County funds 50 youth internship slots (Item 23).

agenda_items.title: Recreation Advisory Commission 2019 Annual Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Recreation Advisory Commission chair presented its annual update, highlighting its subcommittee work and support for the Aquatic Facilities Master Plan.

agenda_items.title: Board Nominations, Farrington Road Rezoning Note, Agenda Settling, and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council nominated Lavesh Pritmani to the Cultural Advisory Board and 11 members to the Hispanic/Latino Committee. Before settling the agenda (Consent 1–27; Item 28 received; GBA public hearing Item 29), Mayor Schewel flagged Item 29 (Consolidated Item 48 on Farrington Road) as fulfilling Council's promise to rezone the former light rail maintenance facility site after light rail's cancellation, and Council voted 7-0 to enter closed session.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Oct 21, 2019 (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: At its October 21, 2019 regular meeting presided over by Mayor Steve Schewel with all seven members present, the Durham City Council proclaimed Sister Cities of Durham Week, honored Durham firefighters who built a treehouse through Jamie's Dream Team, inducted the 2019-2020 Durham Youth Commission, recognized Breast Cancer Awareness and National Arts and Humanities Month, and unanimously approved 7-0 the consent agenda. Council voted 7-0 across three motions to approve the High-Fox consolidated annexation and utility extension agreements (Item 22), and voted 7-0 to approve a partial repeal of historic landmark designation for a surface parking parcel at the Brody Duke Warehouse (Item 23), with Mayor Schewel asking the Legislative Committee to review state law capping historic tax-break clawbacks at three years. Council also voted 7-0 to adopt UDO text amendment TC1800005 strengthening tree preservation and landscaping standards (Item 24) while securing staff commitments for follow-up amendments on street trees and commercial preservation, and closed by hearing unscheduled testimony from two Durham Parks and Recreation employees regarding grievance policies, hostile workplace allegations, and camp staffing ratios.

agenda_items.title: Sister Cities Proclamation, Fire Department Recognition, Durham Youth Commission Induction, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council proclaimed Sister Cities of Durham Week, recognized Durham Fire Department personnel who partnered with Jamie's Dream Team to build a treehouse for a local child, inducted 14 members of the 2019-2020 Durham Youth Commission featuring spoken-word remarks by Leslie Gonzalez on gentrification, and heard Breast Cancer Awareness and National Arts and Humanities Month presentations from Durham Arts Council Executive Director Sherry DeVries. Council also reminded residents of early voting through November 1 ahead of the November 5 municipal election.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 1, 2, and 4-19)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Schewel read the consent agenda covering board/commission appointments (Items 2, 4), FY 2018-19 budget carryover ordinances (Item 5), a HOME loan amendment for Willard Street / Cook Road townhomes (Item 6), lift station, dam inspection, wastewater demolition, and water roof contracts (Items 7-10), Chatham County fire/rescue ILA and Duke Energy storm resiliency grant (Items 12-13), Valley Springs Park construction (Item 14), and Carpenter Fletcher and Cornwallis bike/pedestrian design amendments (Items 17, 19). Council approved the consent agenda 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Consolidated Annexation — High-Fox (1106 and 1107 High-Fox Drive)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Emily Struthers presented a voluntary annexation and utility extension request by Sean Gorman for 1.878 acres at 1106 and 1107 High-Fox Drive with exact-translation Rural Residential and Falls/Jordan Watershed Overlay District B zoning effective December 31, 2019. Gorman noted he was present for questions, no opponents spoke, and council approved the annexation/UEA ordinance, consistency statement, and zoning ordinance 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Brody Duke Warehouse Partial Repeal of Landmark Designation (LD1900001, 311 Liggett St.)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Carla Rosenberg presented a request by Measurement Inc. / Greystar (represented by George Stanziale and Brian Sherrick) to repeal historic landmark status from a subdivided 1.46-acre surface parking lot while preserving a 115-foot viewshed around the Brody Duke Warehouse, noting 6-0 Historic Preservation Commission and SHPO support and a statutory three-year back-tax recovery (~$27,000) under NCGS 105-278. Council members questioned green space and tree replacement in the Innovation District, Mayor Schewel asked the Legislative Committee to examine the state's three-year tax clawback cap, and council approved the partial repeal 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Amendment TC1800005 (Tree Coverage and Landscaping Revisions)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Scott Whiteman presented TC1800005 to expand natural project boundary buffers, increase mass-grading buffers in the suburban tier, require preservation of existing trees before replacement planting, raise urban-tier tree coverage, and require one additional lot tree at construction, noting a 10-1 Planning Commission recommendation and a planned street-tree pilot with TreesDurham. Council members sought and received staff confirmation that commercial tree preservation and right-of-way street trees would return in a follow-up text amendment by summer 2020, discussed solar access and mass grading, and approved both the consistency statement and ordinance amendment 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Parks and Recreation Employee Comments on Workplace Conditions and Grievance Policies

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel presided over the October 10, 2019 work session with all seven members present, unanimously approving (7-0) the City Manager's priority items and the City Attorney's closed session request for litigation including Darryl Howard v. City of Durham et al. The session centered on a sharp 5-2 policy disagreement over the former police headquarters / 103 South Driver developer RFP after staff sent a letter restricting which substantive proposal changes would be accepted ahead of an October 18 deadline: Mayor Steve Schewel, Mark-Anthony Middleton, Javiera Caballero, Vernetta Alston, and Jillian Johnson supported instructing staff to allow any substantive changes (to be vetted for the November 4 meeting) as reflecting Council's Monday night public intent, whereas DeDreana Freeman and Charlie Reece opposed reopening substantive changes, warning it undermined the RFP process and staff's narrower posture. Council also debated—without adopting—whether to prohibit council members from meeting privately with RFP developers after staff recommendations, with Middleton opposing any restriction on elected officials' meetings. Council voted 7-0 to settle the agenda (Consent 1, 2, 4–19; GBA public hearings 22–24) and entered closed session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Council Announcements, and Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel opened the meeting with all seven members present. DeDreana Freeman asked about bond commitments (Schewel clarified only commitments on the city's official website are official) and minority economic participation goals, while Charlie Reece announced municipal early voting (October 16–November 1). Council voted 7-0 to approve the City Manager's priority items and the City Attorney's closed session request (Darryl Howard v. City of Durham et al. and another pending litigation matter).

agenda_items.title: Minutes Corrections and Consent Agenda Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Schewel submitted corrections to the September 3 and September 5 minutes (clarifying 'the council needs to build trust with the police force' and correcting the June 30, 2019 fund balance figure to $51.2 million above the 16.7% target). Council pulled Item 8 (2019 dam inspection) and Item 12 (Chatham County Fire/Rescue ILA) and requested a bio for Item 2 (Human Relations Commission).

agenda_items.title: Discussion of Developer RFP Letter for Police Headquarters Site / 103 South Driver
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council debated whether to override staff's email limiting substantive changes from competing developers ahead of the October 18 submission deadline. By a 5-2 informal head-nod consensus (without a formal motion), Steve Schewel, Mark-Anthony Middleton, Javiera Caballero, Vernetta Alston, and Jillian Johnson directed staff to issue a new letter permitting any substantive changes that can be vetted for the November 4 meeting, over opposition from DeDreana Freeman and Charlie Reece; Middleton also opposed restricting council members' private meetings with developers.

agenda_items.title: Board Nominations, Agenda Settling, and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council re-advertised the Environmental Affairs Board vacancy and nominated Bronwyn Charlton and Brant Smith to the Durham City-County Appearance Commission. Council voted 7-0 to settle the agenda (Consent 1, 2, 4–19; GBA public hearings 22–24) and voted 7-0 to enter closed session.

votes.item_title: Approve City Manager's Priority Items (Updated Attachments Items 3-4; Supplemental Citizen Matters 27-30)
votes.discussion_detail: Approved replacement attachments for Items 3 and 4 and added supplemental Citizen Matters Items 27–30.

votes.item_title: Authorize Closed Session Request (NCGS 143-318.11(a)(3) Darryl Howard v. City of Durham et al. and Pending Litigation)
votes.discussion_detail: Approved City Attorney's request for closed session attorney-client consultation on Darryl Howard v. City of Durham et al. and another pending litigation matter.

votes.item_title: Move into Closed Session (NCGS 143-318.11(a)(3))
votes.discussion_detail: Recessed into closed session for litigation consultation.

disagreements.issue: Scope of Permitted Substantive Changes in Police Headquarters / 103 South Driver Developer RFP
disagreements.summary: Council divided 5-2 over whether to override staff's email limiting substantive developer proposal changes ahead of an October 18 deadline and instead allow any substantive changes that staff could vet for the November 4 meeting.
disagreements.side_a_position: Instruct administration to send a revised letter permitting any substantive changes by October 18 close of business for November 4 consideration.
side_a_arguments: Public interpretation and Council's expressed will on Monday night was to allow developers to bring forward any substantive changes.
Changes must still be deliverable in time for staff vetting and memo preparation before November 4.
disagreements.side_b_position: Maintain the administration's narrower posture barring substantive changes that undercut the RFP process.
side_b_arguments: Moving the date and allowing open-ended substantive revisions undermines the integrity of the RFP process and staff's technical recommendations.
The formal Monday motion did not explicitly mandate allowing sweeping substantive changes.
disagreements.resolution: Resolved by 5-2 informal head-nod consensus (without a formal motion) directing staff to send a revised letter allowing any substantive changes by October 18.

disagreements.issue: Restricting Council Member Meetings with Competing RFP Developers
disagreements.summary: Members disagreed over whether RFP stipulations should bar Council members from taking private meetings with developers during the post-recommendation window.
disagreements.side_a_position: Add RFP stipulations restricting private meetings with developers between recommendation and vote; acknowledge past meetings were a mistake.
side_a_arguments: Avoiding one-on-one developer meetings protects process fairness and avoids undermining staff.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose codifying any rule circumscribing whom elected Council members may meet with.
side_b_arguments: Elections have consequences and Council members should govern themselves rather than codifying bans on constituent or developer meetings.
No causal link existed between meeting developers and extending the RFP deadline.
disagreements.resolution: No formal policy change or vote was taken; members stated their positions for the record.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Oct 7, 2019 (Livestream)
meetings.executive_summary: Convening on October 7, 2019 with all seven members present, the Durham City Council honored the late Omega Curtis Parker, welcomed Durham Neighborhood College participants, and issued proclamations for Hispanic Heritage Month, Indigenous Peoples' Day, and World Food Day before unanimously approving the Consent Agenda 7-0 (excluding pulled Items 15, 17, and 18). On Item 14 (505 West Chapel Hill Street disposition), Charlie Reece disclosed that his family's company, Rho Inc., and competing developer Everage Group both used Joyce Fitzpatrick Communications—which City Attorney Kim Rehberg ruled was not a disqualifying financial interest—and Council voted 7-0 to reopen a staff-vetted amendment window for both Fallon and Everage until October 18 ahead of a November 4 vote. Council then passed pulled Item 15 (Center for Documentary Studies Full Frame contract) and Item 17 (HUD Fair Housing Assistance funding) 7-0, before approving Item 18 (Made in Durham youth program contract modification) by a 5-2 split vote, with Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Javiera Caballero, Mark-Anthony Middleton, and Vernetta Alston voting Aye and Charlie Reece and DeDreana Freeman voting No to support a resident's request for a delay.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Omega Curtis Parker Tribute, Proclamations, and Election Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel opened the meeting with Spanish interpretation instructions from Javiera Caballero and a moment of silent meditation honoring former school board member and DPS librarian Omega Curtis Parker. Council welcomed the 2019 Durham Neighborhood College cohort and issued proclamations for Hispanic Heritage Month (Caballero), Indigenous Peoples' Day on October 14 (DeDreana Freeman), and World Food Day / Neighbors Feeding Neighbors Day on October 16 (Mark-Anthony Middleton). Council Members Charlie Reece, DeDreana Freeman, Vernetta Alston, and Mark-Anthony Middleton offered announcements regarding the October 8 at-large primary election, grassroots anti-gun violence work by BOSS and Bull City Ceasefire, and election-day fare-free transit.

agenda_items.title: Priority Items Check and Consent Agenda Approval (Excluding Pulled Items 15, 17, and 18)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager, City Attorney, and City Clerk reported no priority items. Mayor Schewel read the Consent Agenda covering board appointments, performance audits, HUD CDBG excess program income return, DCLT loan modifications for West Park and Morehead Glenn Apartments, transit demand-response merger, election-day fare-free bus ordinance, NC State TRM agreement, Old Chapel Hill Road waterline contract, August 2019 bid report, hybrid police vehicles, American Dance Festival contract, and Summit Design land surveying amendment. Items 15, 17, and 18 were pulled, and Council approved the remaining Consent Agenda 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Updated Disposition Process for 505 West Chapel Hill Street (Former Police Headquarters)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Charlie Reece read an ethics disclosure stating that Fitzpatrick Communications worked independently for both his family's company (Rho Inc.) and developer Everage Group, and confirmed City Attorney Kim Rehberg determined no disqualifying financial interest existed so he was legally required to participate. Mayor Steve Schewel proposed giving both competing development teams (Fallon Group and Everage Group) until October 18, 2019 at close of business to submit any substantive amendments directly to staff, followed by staff vetting and a Council vote on November 4, 2019. DeDreana Freeman questioned whether accepting post-deadline submissions violated the closed June 28 RFP process, while Mark-Anthony Middleton emphasized Council had not yet voted on a developer and needed complete vetted information; Council approved the extension 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Contract with Center for Documentary Studies (Full Frame Documentary Film Festival)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DeDreana Freeman pulled Item 15 to ask General Services staff Stacey Poston about the five new evaluation criteria used with the Cultural Advisory Board and Discover Durham's Festivals and Events Committee. Freeman urged adding racial equity criteria in future funding cycles to address underfunding of Afrocentric cultural events, and Poston agreed to incorporate that feedback next year. Council approved the contract 7-0.

agenda_items.title: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development Fair Housing Assistance Program Funding
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Item 17 had been pulled by public speakers Tyrone Savage and Dennis Garrett. Mayor Schewel called both speakers' names, and neither was present in the chamber. Council moved and seconded approval of the HUD Fair Housing Assistance agreement, passing 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Made in Durham Contract Modification for Youth Program Services
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Charlie Reece pulled Item 18 after a resident emailed requesting a delay to review Made in Durham performance materials. Office of Economic and Workforce Development staffer Majora Graham-Scott and City Manager Tom Bonfield warned that a delay would create financial hardship for Made in Durham since the contract period began July 1 and work-based collaborative programming toward 600 Durham YouthWorks internships had already launched. DeDreana Freeman echoed community concerns about whether Made in Durham was reaching intended youth and supported delaying the vote, while Reece read from the resident's email criticizing deviations in service model and internship yield; Council approved the contract modification 5-2, with Reece changing his vote from not voting to No to honor the resident's delay request.

votes.item_title: Consent Agenda (Items 1-13, 16, and 19, excluding pulled Items 15, 17, and 18)
votes.discussion_detail: With Items 15, 17, and 18 pulled from the consent slate, Council approved the remaining Consent Agenda items—including appointments, performance audits, DCLT loan modifications, transit demand-response merger, general election fare-free transit, waterline and surveying contracts, and police hybrid vehicles—by a 7-0 vote.

votes.item_title: Item 14 — Extend 505 West Chapel Hill Street Proposal Submission Window to October 18 and Defer Vote to November 4, 2019
votes.discussion_detail: Following Charlie Reece's ethics disclosure and discussion of late developer communications outside the closed June 28 RFP process, Council voted 7-0 to give both Fallon and Everage until close of business on October 18, 2019 to submit any amendments to staff, direct staff to vet and brief Council, and schedule a vote for November 4, 2019.

votes.item_title: Item 15 — Approve Contract with Center for Documentary Studies (Full Frame Documentary Film Festival)
votes.discussion_detail: After DeDreana Freeman questioned General Services staff Stacey Poston about adding racial equity criteria for Afrocentric cultural events in future festival funding cycles, Council unanimously approved the contract 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 17 — Approve U.S. HUD Fair Housing Assistance Program Funding Agreement
votes.discussion_detail: Neither registered speaker (Tyrone Savage or Dennis Garrett) was present when Item 17 was called; Council moved, seconded, and approved the HUD Fair Housing Assistance agreement 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 18 — Authorize City Manager to Execute Made in Durham Contract Modification for Youth Program Services
votes.notes: Charlie Reece initially registered as not voting and asked the clerk to record his vote as No, bringing the final tally to 5-2.
votes.discussion_detail: After debate over a resident's last-minute request to delay consideration and concerns raised by DeDreana Freeman regarding target youth reach, Council approved the contract modification 5-2. The vote initially registered 5-1 with one member not voting before Charlie Reece requested changing his non-vote to No to give voice to the resident requesting a delay while noting he supported the contract.

disagreements.issue: Approval vs. Delay of Made in Durham Youth Program Contract Modification (Item 18)
disagreements.summary: Council divided 5-2 over whether to immediately authorize the Made in Durham contract modification or delay action to allow further review of a resident's critique of the organization's service model and internship outcomes.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the contract modification immediately to avoid financial hardship on an ongoing workforce partnership.
side_a_arguments: The contract period began July 1 and Made in Durham's work-based collaborative supporting 600 Durham YouthWorks internships had already launched.
Staff and the City Manager warned delaying approval would create financial hardship for the organization and noted the item had already gone through the regular work session review.
disagreements.side_b_position: Delay consideration of the contract modification to examine community concerns about outcomes and target youth reach.
side_b_arguments: A resident asked for additional time to review materials regarding Made in Durham's deviation from its original service model and limited internship yield relative to applicants.
Concerns were raised about whether the students being served matched the initial equity and program criteria.
disagreements.resolution: Motion to execute the contract modification passed 5-2; Charlie Reece noted after the vote that he supported the contract itself and voted No solely to represent the resident's request for a delay.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel presided over the September 19, 2019 work session with six members present at roll call and Council Member Mark-Anthony Middleton arriving later. Council praised the new ongoing ordinance establishing fare-free bus and ACCESS transit service on election days (Item 9) and heard public comments from local arts advocates including Omari Akil Dennis regarding The Carrack's closure and urging a Durham Arts Fellowship and indie art-space subsidies rather than out-of-town public art commissions. Council also heard competing developer presentations and conducted Q&A with staff on the downtown redevelopment RFP (including Fallon's two-phase office/residential proposal and competing single-phase financing/tax-credit structures), seeking guidance on land-payment timing and affordable housing proceeds preservation. Council nominated Chanel Frazier to the Audit Services Oversight Committee and voted unanimously (7-0) to move Item 14 to GBA and settle the agenda.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Consent Agenda Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel opened the meeting; Council Member DeDreana Freeman apologized for missing Monday's meeting after a minor medical procedure, and Mark-Anthony Middleton arrived later. Council reviewed consent items—praising Item 9 establishing ongoing fare-free bus and ACCESS service on election days—and pulled Items 5, 8 (demand-response merger), 13, 18 (Made in Durham youth program), and 19 (Summit Design surveying).

agenda_items.title: Citizens Matters / Public Comment (Policing and Local Arts Funding)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A resident criticized DPD complaint handling and background checks, followed by multiple arts advocates—including Omari Akil Dennis—highlighting the impending closure of The Carrack ($80,000 budget). Speakers criticized spending $100,000 on parking garage art, $200,000 on police murals by non-local artists, and $700,000 for the Durham Arts Council, proposing instead a Durham Arts Fellowship and subsidies for independent arts spaces.

agenda_items.title: Competing Developer Presentations and Affordable Housing Proceeds Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Developers presented competing redevelopment proposals (including Fallon's two-phase plan with office/residential buildings and a John Merrick plaza versus a single-phase competitor criticizing two-phase logistics and non-competitive 4% tax credits). Council questioned Fallon on phase-two construction timelines and upfront land payments, and directed staff (Stacy) to bring future options for using proceeds to preserve rental and single-family affordable housing.

agenda_items.title: Board Nomination and Settling the Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council nominated Chanel Frazier to the Audit Services Oversight Committee, moved Item 14 to the General Business Agenda (without a public hearing), and voted unanimously (7-0) to settle the remaining consent agenda (Items 1–13 and 15–19).

meetings.title: Durham City Council Sept 16, 2019 (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: In the livestream recording of the September 16, 2019 Durham City Council meeting, four members—Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, and Javiera Caballero—convened and voted 4-0 to grant excused absences to ill Council Members Vernetta Alston and DeDreana Freeman (with Mark-Anthony Middleton already excused). After six ceremonial proclamations including the Sibiu, Romania Sister City partnership and Neighbor Spotlight Marcella Thompson, Council voted 4-0 in open session to approve annual performance-review salaries for City Clerk Diana Schreiber ($97,335) and City Manager Tom Bonfield ($255,191). Council unanimously approved the Consent Agenda 4-0 (excluding pulled Items 19 and 20) and subsequently passed pulled Item 19 (MS4 stormwater inspections) and Item 20 (Alleyway 13 stormwater repairs) 4-0. Council then held six consolidated annexation and rezoning public hearings—New Haven Townhouses (Item 23), Magnolia Creek Phase 4 (Item 24), All Saints United Methodist Church (Item 25), 5510 Barbee Chapel Road (Item 26), Huntington Valley (Item 27), and Hopewell Academy (Item 28)—and approved every motion unanimously 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Excused Absences for Council Members Alston and Freeman
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel called the meeting to order, Charlie Reece led the Pledge of Allegiance, and roll call confirmed four members present: Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, and Javiera Caballero. Council voted 4-0 to grant excused absences to ill Council Members Vernetta Alston and DeDreana Freeman, noting Mark-Anthony Middleton's previously granted excused absence.

agenda_items.title: Sibiu Sister City Agreement, Hunger/Preparedness Proclamations, Neighbor Spotlight, and Early Voting
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council hosted a Sister City proclamation with Sibiu, Romania, recognized Senior Hunger Awareness Week, Hunger Free Durham Month, Diaper Need Awareness Week, and National Preparedness Month, heard historian Eddie Davis honor Sam Reed, and presented the Neighbor Spotlight to Marcella Thompson. Charlie Reece reminded residents that two weeks of early voting for the October 8 primary opened September 18.

agenda_items.title: Approval of City Clerk and City Manager Salaries Following Annual Performance Reviews
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Schewel announced that Council completed positive closed-session evaluations for City Clerk Diana Schreiber and City Manager Tom Bonfield and required an open-session vote on their salaries. Council voted 4-0 to approve salaries with raises of $97,335 for the City Clerk and $255,191 for the City Manager.

agenda_items.title: Priority Items Check and Consent Agenda Approval (Excluding Pulled Items 19 and 20)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager's office, City Attorney, and City Clerk reported no priority items. Charlie Reece pulled Item 19 for a brief comment under a point of order, and resident Mr. Andrews pulled Item 20. Remaining consent items covering appointments, Community Safety Task Force discussion, Affordable Housing Bond Advisory Committee report, rapid rehousing amendment, electric buses, Cornwallis Road sidewalks, and stormwater/drainage contracts passed 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Municipal Separate Storm Sewer System (MS4) Inspections Contracts (SD-2019-06 & SD-2019-07)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Charlie Reece explained that staff verified no subcontracting opportunities existed for the specialized MS4 inspections and no certified MWBE vendors in the city's database perform that work. He moved approval so critical stormwater inspections could proceed, passing 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Stormwater Infrastructure Repairs SD-2019-02 Amendment #2 (Alleyway 13)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resident Mr. Andrews spoke in support of fixing sinkholes on Alleyway 13 while urging the city to address 35 acres of impervious Duke campus runoff overwhelming the 100-year-old 24-inch pipe near Buchanan Boulevard. Public Works staffer Dana Hornkohl acknowledged legacy drainage issues and agreed to meet with Andrews regarding regional stormwater planning; Council approved the amendment 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — Consolidated Item: New Haven Townhouses (2600 Ellis Road)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jamie Sunyak presented Jared Edens's FLUM amendment and rezoning from RS-20 to PDR 6.239 for up to 55 townhouses on 9.116 acres at 2600 Ellis Road (recommended 12-1 by the Planning Commission). Edens proffered $8,250 to Durham's Affordable Housing Fund, and Council adopted the FLUM amendment, consistency statement, and UDO zoning ordinance 4-0 across three votes.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — Zoning Map Change: Magnolia Creek Phase 4 (4700 Danube Lane / 1018 Old Evergreen Drive)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jamie Sunyak presented Jared Edens's rezoning of 6.71 acres from PDR 4.90 to PDR 7.899 for up to 53 townhouse units (recommended 8-3 by the Planning Commission). Pat Young and Kim Rehberg addressed density calculation questions on the remainder tract, Edens proffered $1,000 to DPS and $7,950 to the Affordable Housing Fund, and staff confirmed to resident Giselle Feiger that a 100-foot riparian buffer would remain behind Old Evergreen Drive; Council passed the consistency statement and rezoning 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — Consolidated Annexation: All Saints United Methodist Church (116 & 120 Smallwood Drive)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jamie Sunyak presented Tim Sivers's utility extension, voluntary annexation, and Rural Residential translation for 11.27 acres owned by All Saints United Methodist Church to connect to city water. Sivers confirmed to Jillian Johnson that no expansion was planned on the vacant land; Council adopted annexation/UEA, consistency statement, and UDO zoning 4-0 across three votes.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — Consolidated Annexation: 5510 Barbee Chapel Road (International Montessori School & Soccer Club)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jamie Sunyak presented Angela Bailey's utility extension, annexation, and Rural Residential / Falls Jordan District B zoning translation for 38.51 acres at 5510 Barbee Chapel Road for an educational facility and soccer club. Following Council questions on the site's former church use and operations, Council passed annexation/UEA, consistency statement, and zoning 4-0 across three votes.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — Consolidated Annexation: Huntington Valley
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and applicant representative Robert Schunk explained the Huntington Valley annexation would allow replatting to 90 single-family lots (at the 90-lot single-access threshold) on the northern half above floodplains, targeting homes below $300,000 without rezoning or proffers. Council approved annexation, consistency statement, and UDO zoning 4-0 across three votes.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — Consolidated Annexation: Hopewell Academy (4651 Comstock Road)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jamie Sunyak presented Chad Abbott's annexation and Industrial Light zoning request for 47.707 acres at 4651 Comstock Road on behalf of RTP International Education LLC for a school building, 200-bed dormitory, and soccer field. Council questioned the relationship between nonprofit Hopewell Academy and for-profit parent RTP International Education LLC until Head of School Randy Taylor and builder Steve Hubrich clarified the lease/investment structure and $350,000–$400,000 in impact fees, while resident Aker Medina requested tuition scholarships for local students. meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel presided over the September 5, 2019 work session, opening with six members present (Council Member DeDreana Freeman joined later) and unanimously approving (6-0) an excused absence for Mark-Anthony Middleton on September 16 and the City Manager's priority items including an economic-development closed session request. Mayor Pro Tempore Jillian Johnson relayed the Race Equity Task Force's request for a six-month extension, and public commenters urged reforming Durham Arts Council funding to match peer cities. During the FY2018-19 Q4 Financial Report (Item 22), staff reported General Fund reserves above the 16.7% target alongside revenue and expense challenges in both the Transit Operating Fund (lower ridership, GoPass usage, and Durham City Transit Company overtime) and the Parking Fund (garage opening delays and street-closure meter losses), with Freeman raising equity concerns over potential residential permit fees. Council made board nominations (while an Environmental Affairs Board ballot finished 3-2-1-1 without a majority) and voted 7-0 to settle the agenda and enter closed session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Race Equity Task Force Extension Request, and Excused Absence
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel called the work session to order with six members present (DeDreana Freeman arrived later). Mayor Pro Tempore Jillian Johnson brought forward the Race Equity Task Force's request for a six-month term extension, asking the City Attorney to check amendment procedures, and Council approved an excused absence for Mark-Anthony Middleton for September 16 (Resilient Cities Summit, 6-0).

agenda_items.title: City Manager's Priority Items and Consent Agenda Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted 6-0 to accept the Manager's priority items (noting Items 29 and 31 speakers would not attend and scheduling a closed session under NCGS 143-318.11(a)(4) on business location/expansion). Council raised racial diversity concerns in board applicant pools and pulled Items 9 (Urban Ministries ESG), 10 (CIP amendment), 11 (electric bus procurement), 12 (Cornwallis Rd sidewalk/bike lane), 15 (Cultural & Public Art resolution), and 19 (MS4 stormwater).

agenda_items.title: Citizens Matters / Public Comment (Policing and Arts Council Funding)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: One speaker raised complaints regarding DPD conduct, and a member of Bulldog Ensemble Theater contrasted Durham Arts Council spending only 9% of its budget on grants ($704,000 city subsidy) with Wake County Arts Council spending 60% and Raleigh directing $1.8 million to 39 local arts groups.

agenda_items.title: FY2018-19 Fourth Quarter Financial Report (Transit and Parking Funds)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff reported General Fund balance exceeded the 16.7% target (with $2M–$4M/year allocated to paving), while Transit Operating Fund suffered lower fare revenues from GoPass/youth pass growth and missed state funds alongside higher Durham City Transit Company overtime. Interim Transportation Director Bill Judge and Thomas Leathers also addressed Parking Fund shortfalls from Morgan-Ricketts garage delays and street closures, discussing congestion pricing and residential permit fees as DeDreana Freeman urged equity protections for fixed-income residents.

agenda_items.title: Board Nominations, Agenda Settling, and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council nominated Jennifer Bell to the Human Relations Commission and Jessica Slices to the Recreation Advisory Commission, re-advertised the Appearance Commission, and tallied an inconclusive 3-2-1-1 ballot for the Environmental Affairs Board (3 Julie Malavade, 2 Karina Barnett-Lorro, 1 Walter Jenkins, 1 Anne Lazaridis). Council voted 7-0 to settle the agenda and enter closed session.

votes.discussion_detail: Granted Mark-Anthony Middleton an excused absence on September 16 to attend the Resilient Cities Summit.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Sept 3, 2019 (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: In a nearly five-hour session on September 3, 2019 with all seven members present, the Durham City Council recognized South Durham Little League champions, RBI baseball, National Recovery Month, and Hurricane Dorian emergency shelter preparations before approving the Consent Agenda 7-0 (excluding pulled Items 12 and 15). Police Chief C.J. Davis presented the 2019 Second Quarter Crime Report—noting a 16% rise in Part 1 violent crime (including 21 homicides and 312 shooting incidents), robberies targeting Hispanic residents, and a 5.8-minute Priority 1 response time—followed by Jason Schiess's traffic stop data presentation and intense public comment on gun violence and police staffing. Council then passed pulled Item 12 (Weaver Street and W.D. Hill Recreation Center renovations design) and Item 15 ($1.5M sidewalk repairs contract SW-67) 7-0. After an extensive public hearing on Item 17, Expanding Housing Choices (EHC), Council passed both the statutory consistency statement and the UDO text amendment allowing duplexes, accessory dwelling units, small-lot options, and flag lots in the urban tier by 6-1 split votes—with Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, Javiera Caballero, Mark-Anthony Middleton, and Vernetta Alston voting Aye and DeDreana Freeman voting No over source-of-income protections, unrelated-resident rules, and displacement concerns—before unanimously approving a metrics reporting resolution 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Youth Baseball & Recovery Proclamations, and Hurricane Dorian Shelter Prep
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel called the meeting to order, Charlie Reece led the Pledge of Allegiance, and all seven members answered roll call. Council honored the South Durham Little League 7–8-year-old Orange All-Star state champions, the RBI baseball program, National Recovery Month (announcing a September 14 Durham Central Park event), and local muralists, and received an emergency management briefing on Hurricane Dorian sheltering with DPD hourly presence and a Charlotte-area ambulance strike team.

agenda_items.title: Priority Items Check and Consent Agenda Approval (Excluding Pulled Items 12 and 15)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Clerk and administration presented no priority items. Mayor Schewel read the Consent Agenda covering minutes, board and Civilian Police Review Board appointments, 2020 council schedule, GoDurham transit advertising policy, Carpenter Fletcher and Hillandale sidewalk/bike-lane agreements, NLC Leadership and Community Resilience grant, and USGS rainfall/streamflow monitoring. With Items 12 and 15 pulled by Victoria Peterson, Council adopted the Consent Agenda 7-0.

agenda_items.title: 2019 Second Quarter Crime Report and Six-Month Traffic Stop Data Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief C.J. Davis reported that Q1–Q2 Part 1 violent crime rose 16% (21 homicides, 312 shooting incidents, and 44% of person robberies involving Hispanic victims, later easing in Q3), while burglaries hit a 10-year low, Priority 1 response times hit the 5.8-minute target, and sworn staffing reached 96% (98% with BLET 50). Jason Schiess presented SBI-122 traffic stop data showing 7,616 stops (+14% YoY but under half of 2010 levels), a 1.0 RTI veil-of-darkness risk ratio, higher search rates for Black drivers (8.67%) alongside no enforcement action in 61% of stops of Black drivers, and a record 51% probable-cause contraband hit rate. During public comment, Chris Tiffany, Jackie Wagstaff, Shea Ramirez, Cheryl Smith, Dennis Garrett, Rafael Zayidi, and Victoria Peterson clashed with Council over gun violence, shuttered recreation centers, and police officer funding.

agenda_items.title: Design Services Contract with Vines Architecture for Weaver Street and W.D. Hill Recreation Center Renovations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Victoria Peterson pulled Item 12 to urge Council to use fund balance reserves to reopen and expand community recreation centers and senior programming near McDougald Terrace. Council approved the Vines Architecture design services contract for Weaver Street and W.D. Hill Recreation Center renovations 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Contract SW-67 Sidewalk Repairs 2019 ($1.5 Million)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Victoria Peterson briefly commented on needing stronger zoning and property building standards after pulling Item 15. Council moved, seconded, and approved Contract SW-67 for approximately $1.5 million in sidewalk repairs 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — Unified Development Ordinance Text Amendment: Expanding Housing Choices (EHC)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Director Pat Young presented the 15-month Expanding Housing Choices (EHC) text amendment to allow duplexes across urban-tier residential districts, expand 800-sq-ft ADUs, add a 2,000-sq-ft small-lot option and narrow flag lots, remove minimum lot-width infill rules, and allow duplexes/townhouses in suburban cluster subdivisions, noting single-family zoning's redlining legacy. Following lengthy public testimony, Mark-Anthony Middleton supported EHC with a request for six-month monitoring to prevent 'gentrification on steroids,' Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Vernetta Alston, Javiera Caballero, and Charlie Reece backed immediate adoption without the Planning Commission's 12-month delay or historic-district exemption, and DeDreana Freeman opposed immediate passage citing missing source-of-income protections and unresolved unrelated-occupant rules. Council passed the consistency statement 6-1, the UDO text amendment 6-1, and a metrics monitoring resolution 7-0.

votes.item_title: Consent Agenda (Items 1-11, 13, and 14, excluding pulled Items 12 and 15)
votes.discussion_detail: With Items 12 and 15 pulled by Victoria Peterson, Council unanimously approved the remaining Consent Agenda items 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 12 — Approve Design Services Contract with Vines Architecture for Weaver Street and W.D. Hill Recreation Center Renovations
votes.discussion_detail: Following remarks by Victoria Peterson advocating additional recreation and senior facilities near McDougald Terrace, Council approved the design services contract 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 15 — Approve Contract SW-67 Sidewalk Repairs 2019 (~$1.5 Million)
votes.discussion_detail: After brief public comment from Victoria Peterson, Council unanimously approved sidewalk repair Contract SW-67 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 17 — Adopt Statutory Consistency Statement for Expanding Housing Choices (EHC) UDO Text Amendment
votes.discussion_detail: Following nearly two and a half hours of presentation, public hearing testimony, and council debate, Council adopted the consistency statement for Expanding Housing Choices 6-1, with DeDreana Freeman voting No.

votes.item_title: Item 17 — Adopt Ordinance Amending Unified Development Ordinance for Expanding Housing Choices (EHC)
votes.discussion_detail: Council adopted the Expanding Housing Choices UDO text amendment 6-1, legalizing duplexes, expanded ADUs, 2,000-sq-ft small lots, and narrow flag lots in urban-tier residential districts; DeDreana Freeman voted No.

votes.item_title: Item 17 — Adopt Resolution Regarding Development and Reporting of Metrics for Expanding Housing Choices
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted a companion resolution directing staff to develop and report monitoring metrics on the impacts of Expanding Housing Choices 7-0.

disagreements.issue: Expanding Housing Choices (EHC) UDO Text Amendment Timing, Equity Safeguards, and Displacement Risk (Item 17)
disagreements.summary: Council debated whether to immediately enact the Expanding Housing Choices UDO text amendment across all urban-tier neighborhoods or delay implementation for 12 months until the Comprehensive Plan update and stronger tenant/equity protections were in place, passing the ordinance 6-1.
disagreements.side_a_position: Adopt Expanding Housing Choices immediately across the urban tier (including historic districts) alongside ongoing metrics monitoring and the $95 million housing bond.
side_a_arguments: Single-family-only zoning perpetuates historical redlining and drives up prices in lower-income neighborhoods by restricting supply in high-demand areas.

Tear-downs for large luxury single-family homes are already occurring under existing rules; EHC enables incremental gentle density, small-lot homes, and ADUs that help market-rate filtering and homeowner equity.
Exempting local historic districts or delaying 12 months would perpetuate systemic inequity and stall needed housing supply after 15 months of community engagement.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose passing the amendment now without source-of-income voucher protections, unrelated-resident occupancy reforms, and waiting for the Comprehensive Plan.
side_b_arguments: Waiting 12 months for the Comprehensive Plan update would allow broader alignment rather than rushing a complex zoning overhaul.
The proposal lacks protections against Section 8 source-of-income discrimination and omits reforms to the three-unrelated-residents occupancy limit.
Removing single-family zoning without direct equity investments risks speculative developer activity in historic middle-class neighborhoods of color without guaranteeing affordable units.
disagreements.resolution: Both the consistency statement and EHC UDO text amendment passed 6-1 (DeDreana Freeman voting No), followed by a unanimous 7-0 vote on the metrics monitoring resolution.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel presided over the August 22, 2019 work session, opening at 1:02 PM with a unanimous vote to return to open session from closed-session performance reviews for the City Manager and City Clerk. Council discussed whether to allow board applicants to address Council during open application windows (agreeing not to do so) and considered scheduling a discussion on a Community Safety / violence task force at the next work session. During Citizens Matters, Monica Byrne presented 2016 tax filing figures for the Durham Arts Council ($189,539 or 9% in grants versus $700,000 in salaries and $704,000 in city funding) while Maeve Cohen urged immediate action on recurring neighborhood gun violence and drive-by shootings. Council also briefly reviewed the Expanding Housing Choices UDO text amendment (Item 17) and a proposed bus advertising First Amendment policy with Senior Assistant City Attorney Fred Lamar, before voting unanimously to settle the agenda (Consent 1–15; GBA Item 16; GBA public hearing Item 17) and scheduling a September 5 closed-session follow-up.

agenda_items.title: Return to Open Session, Roll Call, and Council Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted unanimously to return from closed session into open session at 1:02 PM and called the roll. Members agreed not to invite individual board applicants to present during open application periods and discussed holding a future work session conversation specifically focused on a task force addressing violence and community safety.

agenda_items.title: Citizens Matters / Public Comment (Neighborhood Safety and Arts Funding)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A speaker cited safety survey disparities (50% of minorities and 60% of non-minorities feeling safe); Monica Byrne criticized the Durham Arts Council's 9% grant ratio ($189,539 in grants vs. $700,000 in salaries and $1.4M for DPAC) and urged a 30% grant target by 2021; and Maeve Cohen recounted four recent neighborhood shootings and urged a concrete violence-reduction plan.

agenda_items.title: Expanding Housing Choices UDO Text Amendment and Bus Advertising Policy Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council briefly referenced Planning's Expanding Housing Choices text amendment (Item 17) and questioned Senior Assistant City Attorney Fred Lamar regarding First Amendment restrictions in Transportation's proposed bus advertising policy, with Mayor Schewel asking the City Attorney's office to prepare a concise First Amendment primer.

agenda_items.title: Settle the Agenda and Schedule Closed Session Follow-Up
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously settled the agenda (Consent 1–15; GBA Item 16 2019 Q2 crime report; GBA public hearing Item 17 Expanding Housing Choices) and arranged to reconvene at 10:00 AM on September 5 to finish closed-session performance evaluations for the City Manager and City Clerk.

votes.item_title: Move from Closed Session into Open Session
votes.notes: DeDreana Freeman was called in roll call without a recorded verbal response in the digest; no absences were announced.
votes.discussion_detail: Returned to open session following closed-session performance review discussions for the City Manager and City Clerk.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Aug 19, 2019 (with closed captions)
meetings.executive_summary: In the closed-captioned broadcast of the August 19, 2019 Durham City Council meeting with all seven members present, Mayor Steve Schewel opened by mourning Dr. Evelyn Schmidt and 9-year-old shooting victim Zion Person, after which Mark-Anthony Middleton and DeDreana Freeman urged Council to put the city on emergency footing and fund concrete anti-gun-violence actions. Council celebrated a Sister City partnership with Celaya, Mexico, voted 7-0 to refer the Oregon Street closing (Item 16) back to administration, viewed a new board/commission recruitment video, and adopted Consent Agenda Items 1–13 unanimously 7-0. In the sole public hearing (Item 17), Council held a quasi-judicial proceeding on Towerview Business Center's request for a 60% Major Transportation Corridor buffer reduction (100 feet to 40 feet) and associated two-story office site plan at 4804 Page Creek Lane, voting 7-0 across three motions to conduct the hearing, grant Major Special Use Permit M1800002, and approve Major Site Plan D1800246.

agenda_items.title: Tributes to Dr. Evelyn Schmidt & Zion Person, Celaya Sister City Agreement, and Gun Violence Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel mourned Lincoln Community Health Center pioneer Dr. Evelyn Schmidt and 9-year-old shooting victim Zion Person, calling for federal/state gun action and local wraparound supports. Council formalized a Sister City agreement with Celaya, Mexico, before Mark-Anthony Middleton and DeDreana Freeman urged colleagues to take immediate, funded mid-cycle action against gun violence following Zion Person's killing.

agenda_items.title: Manager's Priority Item (Refer Item 16 Back), Boards/Commissions Video, and Consent Agenda (Items 1-13)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted 7-0 to approve the City Manager's priority item referring Item 16 (Oregon Street closing) back to the administration at the petitioner's request. After viewing the Clerk's new volunteer recruitment video for boards and commissions, Council unanimously adopted Consent Agenda Items 1–13 (covering appointments, NLC fines-and-fees grant, sidewalk supplemental agreements, Twin Lakes Park easement, NRPA grant, county recycling ILA, and CityWorks upgrade) 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Quasi-Judicial Hearing — Towerview Business Center MTC-40 Buffer Reduction (MSUP M1800002 & Site Plan D1800246)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staffer Eliza Monroe presented Nelson Partners and Milestone Development LLC's application to reduce the I-40 Page Road off-ramp MTC buffer from 100 feet to 40 feet for a 12,452-sq-ft two-story office building at 4804 Page Creek Lane. Applicant attorney Neil Gosh, Carlton Midgett, engineer Bill Daniel, and appraiser Jarvis Martin presented evidence on the 1998 NCDOT condemnation, double buffer impact, off-ramp sightlines, supplemental landscaping, and comparable hotel precedent, with no opponents speaking. Council voted 7-0 to conduct the quasi-judicial hearing, 7-0 to grant MSUP M1800002, and 7-0 to approve Major Site Plan D1800246.

votes.item_title: City Manager's Priority Item — Refer Item 16 (Oregon Street Closing Public Hearing) Back to Administration
votes.discussion_detail: Council approved the City Manager's priority item referring Item 16 (Oregon Street closing) back to the administration 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 17 — Motion to Conduct Quasi-Judicial Public Hearing and Receive Evidence (Towerview Business Center M1800002)
votes.discussion_detail: Council voted 7-0 to formally open and conduct the quasi-judicial public hearing and receive evidence for MSUP M1800002.

votes.item_title: Item 17 — Grant Major Special Use Permit M1800002 (Towerview Business Center MTC 40-Foot Buffer Reduction)
votes.discussion_detail: Council granted Major Special Use Permit M1800002 reducing the MTC buffer from 100 feet to 40 feet 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 17 — Approve Major Site Plan D1800246 (Towerview Business Center)
votes.discussion_detail: Council approved Major Site Plan D1800246 for the 12,452-sq-ft two-story office building 7-0.
