meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: All seven council members opened the April 4, 2019 City Council Work Session, unanimously granting Charlie Reece (7-0) an excused absence for the April 18 work session and giving informal consensus to schedule upcoming resolutions on Malcolm X Day and LGBTQ equality legislation. Mark-Anthony Middleton delivered an extended announcement renewing his call to fund a three-year ShotSpotter gunshot-detection pilot in the upcoming budget cycle, and Council unanimously approved the City Manager's priority items (including early action on Item 22's Bimbé Festival booking contract and referring Item 5 back to staff). During an extended discussion of Item 13 (disposition of the former police headquarters at 501 W. Chapel Hill St.), Council debated whether to mandate 50-80 on-site affordable housing units under Scenario A or allow developers to submit optional Scenario B alternatives without on-site affordable housing—a flexible approach favored by Mark-Anthony Middleton in light of the upcoming $95 million housing bond, while another member objected to potentially eliminating on-site downtown affordable units. Council closed by unanimously approving the upcoming meeting agenda.

agenda_items.title: Roll Call, Excused Absence, and Announcements (Malcolm X, LGBTQ, and ShotSpotter)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: All seven council members were present at roll call and unanimously approved an excused absence for Charlie Reece for the April 18 work session. Members gave thumbs-up consensus to consider resolutions on Malcolm X Day and LGBTQ equality legislation at the next work session. Mark-Anthony Middleton renewed his call to fund a three-year ShotSpotter experiment in the FY 2019-2020 budget, urging concrete action against gun violence rather than speeches about root causes.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items (Bimbé Festival, Rental Rehab Referral, and Updates)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Tom Bonfield requested same-day action on Item 22 (Bimbé Festival headlining booking agent contract) due to a new corporate donation, referred Item 5 (Durham Community Land Trustees rental rehabilitation) back to administration, and noted attachment updates on Items 3, 4, 10, and 13 along with Durham 150 birthday events. Council unanimously approved the priority items and pulled Items 1 and 2 during consent review.

agenda_items.title: Disposition Process for Former Police Headquarters (501 W. Chapel Hill St.)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Administration recommended committing net sale proceeds from 501 W. Chapel Hill St. to affordable housing while soliciting proposals under Scenario A (mandatory on-site affordable housing) and optional Scenario B (allowing alternatives without on-site units). One speaker opposed Scenario B as undercutting transit-accessible downtown affordable housing, while Mark-Anthony Middleton argued against restricting proposals given the pending $95 million housing bond and DHA's redevelopment plans. Mayor Steve Schewel focused the scoring question on whether Scenario A requires 80 units or a 50-to-80-unit sliding scale, alongside 9% LIHTC feasibility.

agenda_items.title: Settling the Regular Meeting Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously settled the agenda for the upcoming regular meeting (Consent Items 1, 3, 4, 6-9, 11, 12, and 21; GBA Item 10; and GBA Public Hearings 14-18) before adjourning.

disagreements.issue: Mandatory On-Site Affordable Housing (Scenario A) vs. Optional Off-Site Alternatives (Scenario B) at 501 W. Chapel Hill St.
disagreements.summary: Council members differed on whether the RFP for the former police headquarters at 501 W. Chapel Hill St. should allow developers to submit optional Scenario B proposals without on-site affordable housing alongside Scenario A's 50-to-80-unit requirement.
disagreements.side_a_position: Maintain strict on-site affordable housing expectations and avoid Scenario B eliminating downtown affordable units
side_a_arguments: Allowing Scenario B to remove affordable housing from the site contradicts June council direction and strong community support
Moving units away from downtown transit hubs undermines goals of locating affordable housing in every neighborhood and reducing car dependency
disagreements.side_b_position: Permit optional Scenario B proposals alongside Scenario A's 80-unit option to evaluate full site potential
side_b_arguments: The pending $95 million housing bond and Durham Housing Authority's downtown development plans create broader context beyond a single parcel
Council should not muzzle developers from showing mixed-use, financial-return, and civic-signature options on a historic corridor
disagreements.resolution: Discussion concluded with Mayor Steve Schewel clarifying scoring scales (80 units vs. 50-80 units) for the RFP process without a formal vote.

meetings.executive_summary: Meeting on April 1, 2019, the Durham City Council recognized bilingual victim-support staff, launched Earth Month water conservation and zero-waste initiatives, celebrated Durham's first protected bike lane opening on East Main Street, and reviewed a 22-item Consent Agenda (including LED streetlight conversions, renewable energy/carbon neutrality, and Durham-Orange Light Rail review reimbursements). On pulled Items 16 and 17—Kimley-Horn design contracts for the R. agenda_items.title: Victim Support Staff, Water Pledge, Zero Waste, Farmers Market, AmeriCorps, and East Main Bike Lane
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council recognized bilingual victim-support staff, promoted the MyWaterPledge campaign, and heard Sustainability Manager Tobin Freid present the City Clerk's Zero Waste initiative. Proclamations also honored farmers markets and AmeriCorps/Senior Corps RSVP volunteers, while Council Member Charlie Reece announced the opening of Durham's first protected bike lane along East Main Street.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Reading (Items 1–22; Items 16 and 17 Pulled)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Schewel read the Consent Agenda covering FY19-20 budget guidelines, Laurel Oaks CDBG rehabilitation, LED streetlight conversion, water facility GMP amendments, the Renewable Energy and Carbon Neutrality Resolution, and GoTriangle DOLRT design review reimbursement. Items 16 and 17 were pulled by speakers; the consent vote occurred in an omitted portion of the digest.

Council voted 7-0 to approve both Item 16 and Item 17.

agenda_items.title: Public Speakers on Police Investigations, Neighborhood Safety, and Budget Partnerships

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the March 21, 2019 City Council Work Session, Council gave informal consensus for an upcoming universal health care resolution, unanimously approved the City Manager's priority items, and directed the City Clerk to place dissolution of the Passenger Vehicle for Hire Commission on a future agenda while re-advertising a board seat for greater applicant racial diversity. During consent review, Council highlighted M/WBE subcontractor outreach on Item 13 (Water Management Compliance Services Building) while noting most M/WBE firms came from outside Durham, and pulled Items 6, 7, 8, 10, 16, 17, and 18. Under Item 18, speakers and council members celebrated the Renewable Energy and Carbon Neutrality Resolution championed by Vernetta Alston and Javiera Caballero, advancing it to the April 1 consent agenda. Council also heard the Sesquicentennial Honors Commission presentation recommending an elders oral history project, unanimously settled the April 1 agenda (Consent Items 1, 2, and 4-27), and received board selections for Don Goodman and Antonio Luster before adjourning at 3:53 p.m.

agenda_items.title: Roll Call, Announcements, and City Manager Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel presided as Mark-Anthony Middleton deferred to the Racial Equity Task Force chair on an interim report and Council gave thumbs-up consent for a resolution endorsing federal universal health care legislation. Council unanimously approved City Manager Tom Bonfield's priority items updating attachments on Item 7 (FY 2019-2020 budget guidelines) and Item 11 (Passport Labs parking management software), and noting Grace Marion's absence under Item 33.

agenda_items.title: Board Appointments, Consent Review, and M/WBE Local Capacity Discussion (Item 13)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council asked the Clerk to docket consideration of whether the Passenger Vehicle for Hire Commission is still needed and to re-advertise a board seat lacking racial diversity in applicants. Items 6 (Tilarán Sister City), 7, 8, 10, 16, 17, and 18 were pulled, while Mayor Schewel and DeDreana Freeman praised Gilbane and Water Management's small-package M/WBE outreach on Item 13 while calling for a briefing on why most M/WBE subcontractors came from outside Durham. A resident also spoke under Citizens Matters about stormwater runoff threatening her house's foundation.

agenda_items.title: Renewable Energy and Carbon Neutrality Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Speakers—including youth activists referencing the global climate strike—urged Council to adopt the 100% renewable energy transition resolution. Council praised Vernetta Alston, Javiera Caballero, General Services, and the City Attorney's Office for drafting the resolution, while Mark-Anthony Middleton stressed ensuring communities of color and hourly workers are included rather than left behind. The resolution was scheduled for the April 1 consent agenda.

agenda_items.title: Settling the April 1 Agenda and Board Selection Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously settled the April 1 regular meeting agenda (Consent Items 1, 2, and 4-27, with no public hearings). meetings.title: Durham City Council Mar 18, 2019
meetings.executive_summary: Meeting on March 18, 2019 with six members present after Charlie Reece moved and Council unanimously granted Javiera Caballero an excused absence to attend a funeral in Charlotte, the Durham City Council honored Southwest Central Durham volunteer Rena Pennix and passed a 17-item Consent Agenda including utility contracts and Durham Station bus leases. Budget Director Bertha Johnson opened the FY 2019-20 budget and FY 2020-25 CIP public hearing by reporting a 20.76% countywide property value increase from the January 2019 reappraisal, followed by public speakers including Beth Brooke opposing proposed funding for 72 new police officers. Later in the evening, Council voted 6-0 across three motions to annex and rezone 301 Atkins Heights Boulevard despite neighbor objections over extending Marcy Road, voted 6-0 on Item 27 updating the Durham-Raleigh annexation and utility boundary agreement, and voted 6-0 to amend Chapter 62 allowing city acceptance of developer-built public trails.

agenda_items.title: Excused Absence for Javiera Caballero, Neighborhood Spotlight (Rena Pennix), and Meals on Wheels
agenda_items.discussion_summary: On a motion by Charlie Reece, Council unanimously granted Javiera Caballero an excused absence for the meeting while she attended a funeral in Charlotte. Council then presented the March Neighborhood Spotlight to Rena Pennix of Southwest Central Durham for food bank, community garden, and traffic-calming work, and heard an announcement encouraging Meals on Wheels volunteers.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 1–17)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With no items pulled, Council unanimously approved Consent Agenda Items 1–17 covering Planning Commission and DPAC oversight reappointments, pipeline and sewer repair contracts, cross-connection electronic filing fees, Megabus and Greyhound leases at Durham Station, and the Lodge Street Regional Stormwater amendment.

agenda_items.title: FY 2019-20 Budget and FY 2020-25 Capital Improvement Plan Public Hearing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget Director Bertha Johnson reported that the January 2019 reappraisal increased city real property assessed values by 20.76% over the current 57.8-cent tax rate. Seventeen speakers signed up; Beth Brooke urged Council to honor its 2018 'Durham Beyond Policing' resolution by rejecting funding for 72 new police officers and investing in education, affordable housing, and participatory budgeting.

agenda_items.title: Annexation and Zoning Map Change for 301 Atkins Heights Boulevard (Epcon Development)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Neighbors objected to extending Marcy Road into the proposed Epcon development due to cut-through traffic, emergency vehicle access, and paving costs, while Transportation staff Bill Judge explained the UDO mandates the street connection and allows traffic-calming review at site plan. Council approved the annexation, consistency statement, and UDO amendment 6-0 across three votes.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — Durham-Raleigh Sanitary/Water Service Areas and Annexation Boundary Agreement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff Grace Smith presented minor right-of-way alignment updates to the 1999 Durham-Raleigh annexation agreement ahead of Raleigh's April 2 hearing, and speaker Nelson Paul commented on jurisdiction along the line. Council voted 6-0 to authorize the Mayor to execute the agreement.

agenda_items.title: Ordinance Amending Chapter 62 for Acceptance of Developer-Built Public Trails
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Works representative Robert Joyner presented code changes allowing private developers to dedicate trail easements, build trails to city standards, and petition Council for public acceptance and maintenance like streets. After clarifying questions from Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson confirming public ownership, Council adopted the ordinance 6-0.

votes.item_title: Grant Excused Absence to Council Member Javiera Caballero
votes.discussion_detail: Charlie Reece moved to grant Javiera Caballero an excused absence to attend a funeral in Charlotte; the six present members approved unanimously by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Adopt Ordinance Annexing 301 Atkins Heights Boulevard
votes.notes: Mayor initially misread the vote as 4-2 before immediately correcting it to 6-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Council approved annexation of 301 Atkins Heights Boulevard for the Epcon development following public comment on Marcy Road connectivity.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement for 301 Atkins Heights Boulevard Zoning Map Change
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the comprehensive plan consistency statement for 301 Atkins Heights Boulevard.

votes.item_title: Adopt Ordinance Amending the UDO for 301 Atkins Heights Boulevard
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the UDO zoning map amendment for 301 Atkins Heights Boulevard.

votes.item_title: Adopt Ordinance Authorizing Mayor to Execute Durham-Raleigh Sanitary/Water and Annexation Boundary Agreement (Item 27)
votes.discussion_detail: Council approved updating the 1999 Durham-Raleigh annexation and utility boundary agreement to reflect finalized NCDOT rights-of-way.

votes.item_title: Adopt Ordinance Amending Chapter 62 Regarding Acceptance of Developer-Built Public Trails
votes.discussion_detail: Council adopted code revisions enabling public acceptance and maintenance of qualifying developer-built trails.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the March 7, 2019 City Council Work Session, all seven seated council members answered roll call and unanimously approved the City Manager's priority items (referring the general classification and compensation plan back to administration and adjusting the Lodge Street Regional Stormwater amendment amount from $28,850 to $24,850) as well as Interim City Attorney Kim Rehberg's closed-session request regarding Amanda Mingo v. City of Durham. Council pulled the cross-connection control electronic filing fee ordinance and the renewable energy and carbon neutrality resolution for discussion/speakers, and heard a brief public comment opposing the council's 2018 resolution on Israeli police training. Planning staff presented the Patterson Place Compact Suburban District text amendment, zoning map change, and future street network—highlighting New Hope Creek corridor protections, a proposed 200-foot Transitional Use Area, stricter steep-slope standards, and three Planning Commission review requests including a 300-foot TUA alternative—for future action in May. Council concluded by receiving board reappointment nominations, unanimously approving the settled consent and public hearing agenda, and voting unanimously to enter closed session.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items (Compensation Referral, Lodge Street Stormwater Amendment, Oregon Street Attachment, Citizens' Matters)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager's Office presented priority adjustments: referring Item 13 (General Classification and Compensation Plan recommendations) back to administration, reducing Item 17 (Lodge Street Regional Stormwater Improvements Amendment 1) from $28,850 to $24,850, replacing attachment six for Item 21 (Oregon Street closing), and noting that citizens' matters speakers Matthew Diamond (Item 29) and Heath Knight (Item 34) would not appear. Council approved the priority items by unanimous voice vote.

agenda_items.title: City Attorney Priority Item: Closed Session Request (Mingo v. City of Durham)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim City Attorney Kim Rehberg requested a closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) for attorney-client consultation concerning threatened litigation and Amanda Mingo, as Guardian ad Litem for Jayden Hyman and Jasmine Murray-Hyman, v. City of Durham. Council unanimously accepted the priority item by voice vote and welcomed Rehberg into her official role as Interim City Attorney.

agenda_items.title: Departmental Consent Review & Pulled Items (Water/Sewer Contracts, Cross-Connection Fee, Renewable Energy Resolution, ShotSpotter)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and Council reviewed departmental items including pipeline and sewer repair contracts (Items 6–7), ferric sulfate supply (Item 8), Durham Station leases for Megabus and Greyhound (Items 10–11), a utility extension at 300 Chandler Road (Item 14), City Code Chapter 70 permitting updates (Item 15), surveying contract ST-295 (Item 16), Lodge Street Stormwater Amendment 1 (Item 17), and the ShotSpotter presentation (Item 18). Council members pulled Item 9 (cross-connection control electronic filing fee) and Item 12 (renewable energy and carbon neutrality resolution, which had speakers) and praised Public Works and Water Management for advancing permitting efficiency and the Lodge Street stormwater project.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing Deferrals: Durham-Raleigh Annexation Agreement & Oregon Street Closing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Because negotiations related to a public hearing item remained ongoing, Council discussed whether to refer the item back to administration for re-advertisement or open the public hearing at the upcoming Monday business meeting and continue it. Council agreed on the less disruptive option of opening and continuing the hearing, asked speaker Nelson Paul (Morrisville) to return in 10 days for Item 27 (Durham-Raleigh annexation agreement), and inquired whether the Oregon Street closing sat within the proposed light rail footprint.

agenda_items.title: Public Comment on Resolution Regarding Police Training
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Josh Ravich of Chapel Hill addressed Council for one minute during citizens' matters to criticize Council's 2018 resolution concerning Israeli police training programs.

agenda_items.title: Presentation: Patterson Place Compact Suburban District (CSD) Text Amendment, Zoning Map Change (Z1800030) & Future Street Network
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff briefed Council on the Patterson Place Compact Neighborhood Tier design district (targeting roughly 25% of anticipated growth near proposed light rail), detailing subdistrict boundaries, heights and densities with and without affordable housing bonuses, parking rules, and environmental protections near the New Hope Creek corridor. Proposed safeguards include a 200-foot Transitional Use Area requiring a major special use permit and stricter steep-slope rules (15% slope threshold, 2,500 sq. ft. minimum area, 0% disturbance). Staff noted the Planning Commission continued the case to April to evaluate expanding the TUA to 300 feet, revising review factors, and excluding New Hope Commons, as well as pedestrian/bicycle connectivity in the US 15-501 corridor study, before returning to Council in May.

agenda_items.title: Board Nominations, Agenda Settlement & Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Clerk announced reappointment nominations for Akram Al-Turk, Brian Busby, and Cedric Johnson (Planning Commission) and Keelan Brown and Susan McClanahan (DPAC Oversight Committee), while Council chose to re-advertise the Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Commission vacancy for greater diversity. Council then unanimously approved the settled consent and public hearing agenda (with Items 3, 12, and 13 referred back or continued) and voted unanimously to enter closed session.

votes.item_title: Acceptance of City Manager Priority Items
votes.notes: Voice vote passed unanimously with all seven seated council members present at roll call; individual votes were not polled.
votes.discussion_detail: Accepted the City Manager's priority updates referring Item 13 (compensation plan) back to administration, decreasing Item 17 (Lodge Street stormwater) to $24,850, replacing Attachment 6 for Item 21 (Oregon Street closing), and noting two absent citizens' matters speakers.

votes.item_title: Acceptance of City Attorney Priority Item (Closed Session Request)
votes.notes: Voice vote passed unanimously; individual votes were not polled.
votes.discussion_detail: Accepted Interim City Attorney Kim Rehberg's priority request to hold a closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) for attorney-client consultation on threatened litigation and Amanda Mingo v. City of Durham.

votes.item_title: Approval of Settled City Council Agenda
votes.notes: Voice vote passed unanimously; individual votes were not polled.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the settled agenda for the regular meeting, placing consent items and public hearings (Items 20–28) on the docket while referring back or continuing Items 3, 12, and 13.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3))
votes.notes: Voice vote passed unanimously; individual votes were not polled.
votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) for attorney-client consultation regarding threatened litigation and the newly filed Amanda Mingo matter.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Mar 4, 2019
meetings.executive_summary: Convening on March 4, 2019 with all seven members present, the Durham City Council recognized outgoing City Attorney Patrick Baker alongside former Mayor Bill Bell, welcomed Interim City Attorney Kim Rehberg, issued Disability and Women's History/ERA proclamations, and passed the Consent Agenda 7-0. Police Chief C.J. Davis presented Item 19, the 2018 fourth-quarter and annual crime report, noting a 7% drop in Part 1 index crime, a 13% drop in violent crime, and a 6% drop in property crime. In zoning public hearings, Council denied a 30-day continuance request from an adjacent owner alleging private deed restrictions on Davis Park West and approved both the consistency statement and UDO amendment 7-0. On Item 21 (1020 Hale Street duplex rezoning), Council voted 6-1 on both the consistency statement and UDO amendment, with Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, Javiera Caballero, Mark-Anthony Middleton, and Vernetta Alston voting Aye and DeDreana Freeman voting No.

agenda_items.title: Girl Scouts Pledge, Proclamations, Tribute to City Attorney Patrick Baker, and Neighborhood Spotlight
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Ten Girl Scout troops led the Pledge of Allegiance, followed by proclamations for disability inclusion and Women's History Month/the Equal Rights Amendment and remarks from Judge Allyson Kay Duncan. Former Mayor Bill Bell joined Mayor Schewel in honoring retiring City Attorney Patrick Baker, Tony Simpson received the Neighborhood Spotlight, and Interim City Attorney Kim Rehberg was introduced.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 1–17 and Item 28)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With no priority items or pulls, Council unanimously passed the Consent Agenda 7-0, covering an RDU Airport Authority appointment, timekeeping audit, CDBG/HOME reimbursements, DOLRT plan review amendment, Hoover Road Athletic Park CMAR contract with Skanska USA Building, and a Made in Durham youth pipeline contract.

agenda_items.title: 2018 Fourth Quarter and Annual Crime Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Police Chief C.J. Davis delivered an oral 2018 annual crime report (due to Q3 slides appearing on screen), reporting that compared to 2017, Part 1 index crime declined 7%, Part 1 violent crime fell 13%, property crime fell 6%, and firearm involvement in aggravated assaults dropped from 68% to 59%.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change — Davis Park West
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Cynthia White, representing adjacent Republic Flats Apartments/Eaton Vance, sought a 30-day continuance claiming lack of notice and private commercial-only deed restrictions, which developer Craig Davis's representative rebutted with October 2018 emails and Boston meeting records. Viewing private deed covenants as outside municipal zoning authority, Council passed both the consistency statement and UDO ordinance 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change — 1020 Hale Street Duplex
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff Emily Stravitz presented Martin McFarling's request to rezone 1020 Hale Street from RU-5 to RU-5(2) for duplexes, consistent with the Medium Density Residential future land use map. Applicant Marty McFarling cited bank financing barriers for a single-family plus ADU setup, while opponent William Whitmore opposed duplex zoning; Council passed both motions 6-1 with DeDreana Freeman voting No.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement for Davis Park West Zoning Map Change
votes.discussion_detail: Council adopted the consistency statement for Davis Park West after declining an adjacent owner's 30-day continuance request.

votes.item_title: Adopt Ordinance Amending the UDO for Davis Park West
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the UDO zoning amendment ordinance for Davis Park West.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement for 1020 Hale Street Duplex Zoning Map Change (Item 21)
votes.discussion_detail: Council adopted the consistency statement for the 1020 Hale Street duplex rezoning 6-1, with DeDreana Freeman voting no.

votes.item_title: Adopt Ordinance Amending the UDO for 1020 Hale Street Duplex (Item 21)
votes.discussion_detail: Council adopted the UDO amendment rezoning 1020 Hale Street to RU-5(2) by a 6-1 vote, with DeDreana Freeman dissenting.

disagreements.summary: Council voted 6-1 to rezone 1020 Hale Street from RU-5 to RU-5(2) for duplexes, with DeDreana Freeman opposing both the consistency statement and UDO amendment following neighbor opposition and Planning Commission questions.

meetings.title: Special City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the February 21, 2019 Special City Council Work Session on affordable housing strategy and funding, Durham Housing Authority CEO Anthony Scott presented DHA's 17-phase downtown redevelopment plan utilizing HUD's Rental Assistance Demonstration (RAD) program across Oldham/Liberty, Fayette Place, Forest Hill Heights, J.J. Henderson, DHA offices, and two City-owned sites. The plan guarantees one-for-one replacement of existing public housing units within the downtown footprint alongside net new workforce and mixed-income housing, full relocation coverage, and potential community land trust townhomes at J.J. Henderson. City staff and Finance Director David Boyd then presented an anti-displacement property tax relief review and a proposed $95 million November 2019 Affordable Housing Bond referendum (part of a $157 million multi-year spending plan adding four FTEs and requiring under 2.25 cents on the tax rate). While no formal votes were taken, Council members gave informal consensus direction ('thumbs up') for the City Manager and City Attorney to prepare a formal bond referendum recommendation and ballot language alongside detailed tax-rate impact analyses.

agenda_items.title: Durham Housing Authority (DHA) Downtown & RAD Redevelopment Plan Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DHA CEO Anthony Scott presented a comprehensive 17-phase redevelopment plan (including 10 phases using 9% LIHTC credits) covering Oldham/Liberty, Fayette Place, Forest Hill Heights, J.J. Henderson, DHA's offices, and two City-owned sites. By converting public housing subsidies to Section 8 vouchers under HUD's RAD program, DHA plans one-for-one replacement within the downtown footprint, net new affordable and workforce units (up to 80% AMI, or roughly $64,000 for a family of four against Durham's >$80,000 AMI), full relocation coverage, and community land trust concepts at J.J. Henderson. Council Member Charlie Reece questioned how mixed-income rules could affect social displacement, and members expressed strong support for DHA's partnership.

agenda_items.title: Property Tax Relief & Anti-Displacement Program Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council and staff reviewed Durham's existing geographically targeted property tax relief program, noting legal constraints identified by the UNC School of Government against broad progressive property tax structures and estimating a citywide relief program could cost roughly $35 million. Members noted improved efficiency between 2016 and 2017—spending less staff time to distribute higher average grants—and asked whether partnering with community volunteers for door-to-door outreach could expand enrollment without excessive administrative costs.

agenda_items.title: Proposed $95 Million Affordable Housing Bond Referendum & Five-Year Housing Spending Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff outlined a proposed $157 million multi-year affordable housing expenditure framework anchored by a $95 million bond referendum for November 2019 and four new FY20 FTEs focused on multifamily rental preservation, homelessness, and financial management. Finance Director David Boyd explained debt would be issued incrementally rather than all at once, with an estimated tax-rate increment below 2.25 cents. Council members gave informal consensus direction ('thumbs up') for the City Manager and City Attorney to draft formal referendum recommendations and ballot language, while requesting detailed tax-rate projections given recent steep property revaluations.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the February 18, 2019 Regular City Council Meeting, Mayor Steve Schewel delivered the State of the City Address highlighting crime and policing, Durham Public Schools, immigrant sanctuary and deportation concerns, and the $2.4 million Participatory Budgeting cycle, alongside ceremonial recognitions for NCCU student activists and former State Rep. H.M. 'Mickey' Michaux. In legislative action, Council unanimously approved (7-0) both the Weaving Water Initial 2 clean-up rezoning to RS-20 and an interlocal agreement with Durham County conveying County-owned property to the City for affordable housing. Council divided over the Comstock Industrial (Page Road LandCo, LLC) annexation and Industrial Light (IL) rezoning near Duke Health System property: the annexation ordinance passed 6-1 (Ayes: Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, DeDreana Freeman, Mark-Anthony Middleton, Vernetta Alston; Nay: Javiera Caballero), while both the NCGS 160A-383 consistency statement and the UDO rezoning ordinance passed 5-2 (Ayes: Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, Mark-Anthony Middleton, Vernetta Alston; Nays: Javiera Caballero, DeDreana Freeman).

agenda_items.title: Pledge of Allegiance, Ceremonial Recognitions (24th Amendment Ratification & Rep. H.M. 'Mickey' Michaux) & State of the City Address
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Cub Scouts Pack 486 led the Pledge of Allegiance, and all seven council members answered roll call. Mayor Schewel presented ceremonial recognitions honoring NCCU students (led by student body president Tanya Robinson) and Rep. Mickey Michaux for lobbying North Carolina's 1989 retroactive ratification of the 24th Amendment, as well as a proclamation celebrating Michaux's career. Mayor Schewel then delivered the State of the City Address covering refugee and immigrant families (noting Samuel Oliver-Bruno's ICE deportation), crime and policing, public schools, and Participatory Budgeting ($2.4 million, 550 ideas, and May 1 voting for residents ages 13+), followed by the 2018 annual report video featuring 'Duramina.'

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Consolidated Annexation & Rezoning — Comstock Industrial (Page Road LandCo, LLC)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff Jamie Sunyak and applicant representative Mr. Biker presented a voluntary annexation and Industrial Light (IL) rezoning east of Page Road, west of I-540, and south of Logistics Way, adjacent to 45 acres owned by Duke Health System, noting a 10-2 Planning Commission recommendation and deferred Traffic Impact Analysis pending an end user. Council members cited written Planning Commission comments from Commissioners Baker and Miller and debated appropriate uses along the corridor near I-40. agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Zoning Map Change — Weaving Water Initial 2 (3912 & 3920 Rivermont Road)

agenda_items.title: Interlocal Agreement with Durham County for Conveyance of County-Owned Property for Affordable Housing

disagreements.issue: Comstock Industrial Consolidated Annexation and Industrial Light (IL) Rezoning (Item 13)
disagreements.summary: Council divided over annexing and rezoning the Page Road LandCo, LLC (Comstock Industrial) property to Industrial Light (IL) without a committed end user or completed Traffic Impact Analysis, echoing a 10-2 Planning Commission split reflected in Commissioners Baker and Miller's written comments.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve annexation and Industrial Light (IL) zoning as consistent with the Future Land Use Map and adjacent light-industrial/Duke Health corridor.
side_a_arguments: Consistent with the Future Land Use Map and nearby I-40 / I-540 / Page Road light-industrial development.
Provides flexibility for complementary uses (medical office, hotel, restaurant) near Duke Health System's 45-acre campus, with a TIA required at site plan once an end user is identified.
Supported by a 10-2 Planning Commission vote and Commissioner Miller's analysis, with UDO height, lighting, noise, and boundary buffer standards applying.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose the IL rezoning (and, for Caballero, the annexation) due to broad permitted IL uses and unaddressed long-term planning concerns.
side_b_arguments: Council members and staff highlighted the broad list of permitted uses in the IL district without a committed end user or pre-rezoning TIA.
Dissenters aligned with Planning Commissioner Baker's written critique cautioning against incremental rezoning decisions.
disagreements.resolution: Annexation passed 6-1 (Caballero opposed; Freeman voted Aye on annexation); both the consistency statement and UDO IL rezoning ordinance passed 5-2 (Caballero and Freeman opposed).

meetings.title: Special City Council Meeting - Legislative Breakfast with Durham Delegation
meetings.executive_summary: At the February 11, 2019 Special City Council Legislative Breakfast with the Durham state legislative delegation (including Sen. Floyd McKissick, Sen. Mike Woodard, and Rep. Zack Hawkins), Council and staff presented Durham's 2019 General Assembly priorities. Discussions focused on criminal justice reforms—specifically pre-deprivation ability-to-pay hearings and 12-month license restoration for failure-to-pay suspensions alongside expanding criminal record expunctions—as well as firearm reporting, amending state law to expand council, civilian review board, or city manager access to police body-camera footage, and electronic speed enforcement in school and high-pedestrian zones. Officials also reviewed municipal condemnation and utility relocation reimbursement authority ($30,000+ threshold), and Council Member Charlie Reece pressed for local circuit-breaker property tax relief ahead of property revaluation alongside discussion of legal hurdles to inclusionary zoning. No formal votes were taken, and Council thanked retiring City Attorney Patrick Baker for over two decades of service.

agenda_items.title: Driver's License Restoration & Criminal Record Expunction Proposals
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council and staff presented the Innovation Team's proposal for judicial pre-deprivation ability-to-pay hearings and automatic restoration after 12-month suspensions for failure to pay traffic fines, noting the need to consult DMV. Senator Floyd McKissick discussed prior bipartisan expunction legislation eliminating the lifetime cap on expunctions for dismissed or not-guilty charges, while noting Administrative Office of the Courts database limitations on older records.

agenda_items.title: Lost/Stolen Firearm Reporting & Body-Worn Camera Disclosure Reform
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Participants discussed data collection on lost or stolen firearms reported to the Sheriff, bond levels for discharging firearms or selling guns to felons, and legislative efforts with Rep. Faircloth to amend the body-camera statute. Members debated whether City Council, civilian police review boards, or the City Manager should gain statutory authority to view and release footage, balancing transparency against concerns about trying cases in the court of public opinion.

agenda_items.title: Electronic Speed Enforcement, Residential Speed Limits, Condemnation & Utility Relocation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff reviewed Item 12 (authorizing electronic speed enforcement in school and high-pedestrian priority zones) and lowering default residential speed limits below 35 mph. Staff also requested statewide or local clarity mirroring NCDOT right-of-way condemnation authority (citing Fayetteville Road) and clear authority to reimburse power and gas line relocations exceeding $30,000.

agenda_items.title: Circuit Breaker Property Tax Exemption, Inclusionary Zoning & Tribute to City Attorney Patrick Baker
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Charlie Reece renewed Durham's request for a revised circuit breaker property tax exemption in a property revaluation year to assist low-income homeowners without leaving heirs with debt, while Sen. McKissick and City Attorney Patrick Baker discussed municipal statutory limits and negative NC case law constraining inclusionary zoning (comparing Chapel Hill and Davidson local bills). Council and the delegation concluded by thanking retiring City Attorney Patrick Baker for over 20 years of service.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the February 7, 2019 City Council Work Session, Council Member Javiera Caballero reaffirmed that Durham Police do not cooperate with ICE following local detentions, and Council Member Mark-Anthony Middleton secured consensus to place ShotSpotter cost estimates and vendor Q&A (covering efficacy and Fourth Amendment questions) on the March 7 agenda. Council unanimously suspended the rules and approved two City Clerk priority travel-fund transfers ($2,591.75 from Mayor Schewel to Council Member Middleton, and $3,000 from Council Member Reece to Council Member Freeman). In pulled-item reviews, Council questioned Clark Patterson Lee's internal workforce diversity and Durham YouthWorks participation on a design contract, discussed the Institute for Sustainable Communities' Equitable Investment Fund and East Durham partnerships under the Shared Economic Prosperity plan, and received Water Management's low per-capita usage update. Council concluded by receiving board nominations and unanimously approving the settled agenda (Consent Items 1–11 and Public Hearings 12–14).

agenda_items.title: Immigration Enforcement Statement & March 7 ShotSpotter Scheduling
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Javiera Caballero noted recent ICE detentions—including a father en route to Hillside High School and 38 workers in Sanford—and affirmed that Durham Police do not cooperate with ICE. Council Member Mark-Anthony Middleton then requested per-square-mile cost figures and a ShotSpotter vendor representative at the March 7 work session to answer council questions on technology efficacy and Fourth Amendment concerns, receiving informal council concurrence.

agenda_items.title: City Clerk Priority Items: Council Travel Fund Transfers
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Clerk requested suspension of the rules and immediate approval of two travel-fund transfers: $2,591.75 from Mayor Schewel to Council Member Middleton and $3,000 from Council Member Reece to Council Member Freeman. Mayor Schewel noted Council should consult the City Attorney on whether routine transfers require formal votes in the future, and Council unanimously voted to suspend the rules and approve both transfers.

agenda_items.title: Citizens' Matters & Water Management Per-Capita Usage Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: During citizens' matters and early briefings, speakers addressed city resolutions and neighborhood redevelopment surrounding the Hayti Heritage Center (former St. Joseph's AME Church). Water Management staff reported that Durham remains one of the lowest per-capita water users in North Carolina and is incorporating climate variability analysis into water planning.

agenda_items.title: Design Services Contract with Clark Patterson Lee (Workforce Diversity & YouthWorks)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A council member pulled the Clark Patterson Lee (CPL) design services contract (General Services) to note positive M/WBE participation but raise concern over CPL's internal workforce demographics (roughly 16 African American and 11 Hispanic employees out of ~300) and the lack of Durham-based firms. CPL's representative described recruitment and STEM outreach efforts and agreed to follow up on hosting a Durham YouthWorks summer intern.

agenda_items.title: Contract with Institute for Sustainable Communities — Strategic Plan for Shared Economic Prosperity
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members discussed Item 10 (Office of Economic and Workforce Development contract with the Institute for Sustainable Communities), focusing on data gathering on minority-owned businesses, access to capital through a proposed Equitable Investment Fund, and expanding partnerships with Self-Help, Durham Community Land Trust, Latino Community Credit Union, and Habitat for Humanity beyond a single neighborhood to East Durham and citywide.

agenda_items.title: Board Nominations & Agenda Settlement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Clerk announced nominations for Brian Langloss and Beverly Thorpe (Citizens Advisory Committee), Andrew Goolsby (Architect, Historic Preservation Commission), and Kuko Nayo and Leslie Straughan-Mullen (Recreation Advisory Commission). Council unanimously approved the settled agenda comprising Consent Items 1–11 and Public Hearings 12–14.

votes.notes: Voice vote passed unanimously; individual votes were not polled.
votes.discussion_detail: Suspended the rules to take immediate action on two council travel-fund transfer requests presented by the City Clerk.

votes.item_title: Approval of Council Travel Fund Transfers (Schewel to Middleton; Reece to Freeman)
votes.notes: Voice vote passed unanimously; individual votes were not polled.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved transferring $2,591.75 from Mayor Schewel to Council Member Middleton and $3,000 from Council Member Reece to Council Member Freeman.

votes.item_title: Approval of Settled City Council Agenda
votes.notes: Voice vote passed unanimously; individual votes were not polled.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the settled regular meeting agenda with Items 1–11 on consent and Items 12–14 as public hearings.

meetings.title: City Council Meeting   Feb 4, 2019 (No Pledge of Allegiance)
meetings.executive_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel presided over the brief February 4, 2019 regular meeting of the Durham City Council, opening with a moment of silent meditation and two ceremonial proclamations. The council declared February 2019 as Together for Resilient Youth (TRY) Prevention Month—highlighting youth substance-use trends and alcohol retailer compliance—and Council Member Charlie Reece presented a proclamation recognizing January 30, 2019 as Fred Korematsu Day of Civil Liberties and the Constitution. During announcements, Council Member Mark-Anthony Middleton noted a recent staff presentation on ShotSpotter gunshot detection technology while emphasizing no decision had been made, and Council Member Javiera Caballero announced a February 24 public safety forum focused on the immigrant and Latino community. Following no priority items from staff, the council voted unanimously 7-0 to approve the five-item consent agenda before adjourning at 7:23 p.m.

agenda_items.title: Together for Resilient Youth (TRY) Prevention Month Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel called the meeting to order, led a moment of silent meditation, and read a proclamation declaring February 2019 as Together for Resilient Youth (TRY) Prevention Month, citing data from the 2017 Durham County Youth Risk Behavior Survey. Earl Boone accepted the proclamation on behalf of TRY, highlighting reductions in youth substance use outside of marijuana, praising TRY's Good Neighbor Business Network alcohol compliance efforts and CDC recognition, and warning of risks from adolescent marijuana use.

agenda_items.title: Fred Korematsu Day of Civil Liberties and the Constitution Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Charlie Reece introduced and read a proclamation declaring January 30, 2019 as Fred Korematsu Day of Civil Liberties and the Constitution, reflecting on World War II Japanese American internment under Executive Order 9066 and his own family's immigration history. Dr. Chiyoko Lord of the Japan-America Society of North Carolina accepted the proclamation and emphasized the importance of remembering civil rights struggles.

agenda_items.title: Council Announcements (ShotSpotter Briefing, Latino Public Safety Forum) and Staff Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Mark-Anthony Middleton congratulated colleagues on their LGBTQ Center benefit at Pinhook, recognized Council Member Javiera Caballero's Durham Magazine feature and Black History Month events, and thanked the City Manager for arranging a recent presentation on ShotSpotter technology while noting no decisions had been made. Council Member Charlie Reece recognized former Council Member Jackie Wagstaff in attendance, and Council Member Caballero announced a February 24 public safety forum at Immaculata featuring Police Chief Cerelyn Davis, District Attorney Satana Deberry, and Sheriff Clarence Birkhead to address crimes targeting the immigrant and Latino community. The City Manager, City Attorney Kim Rehberg, and City Clerk reported no priority items.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 1, 3, 4, 6, and 7)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Schewel read the consent agenda comprising approval of City Council minutes (Item 1), the December 2018 bid report (Item 3), a three-year renewal of the right-of-way maintenance and mowing contract (Item 4), a Building Inspections Land Development Office web portal upgrade (Item 6), and an ESRI software maintenance service agreement (Item 7). No items were pulled by council members or the public, and the council approved the consent agenda unanimously.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the January 24, 2019 City Council Work Session, six members were present and unanimously voted to excuse Council Member Charlie Reece, who was attending a funeral. Council unanimously accepted the City Manager's priority items, then suspended the rules and voted unanimously to approve both Item 2 (uniform unarmed security guard services for city parking facilities, enabling a February 1 contract start) and Item 5 (the $50,000 WIOA Finish Line Grant for emergency financial hardship aid to Durham Technical Community College students, following staff clarification of utility-payment eligibility). agenda_items.title: Excusal of Council Member Charlie Reece & Council Announcements

Mayor Schewel announced a February 21 special work session on affordable housing strategy and funding and received informal agreement to place the Environmental Affairs Board energy goals resolution on the February 7 agenda.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items (Mature Durham Presentation & Rule-Suspension Requests for Items 2 and 5)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager requested a brief Parks & Recreation briefing on the Mature Durham program and asked Council to suspend the rules to vote immediately on Item 2 (parking security guard contract, as the prior vendor ended December 31, 2018) and Item 5 ($50,000 WIOA Finish Line Grant, required before spring semester student hardship grants can be approved). agenda_items.title: Citizens' Matters: Housing Code Praise, Edison Johnson Mature Adult Class, Police Resolution & Water Billing

agenda_items.title: Uniform Unarmed Security Guard Services for City Parking Facilities
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following earlier priority review, Council unanimously voted to suspend the rules and then unanimously approved the contract for uniform unarmed security guard services at city parking facilities so coverage could begin February 1, 2019.

agenda_items.title: Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (WIOA) Finish Line Grant ($50,000)

Council unanimously voted to suspend the rules and approve acceptance of the $50,000 Finish Line Grant for Durham Technical Community College students.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Jan 22, 2019
meetings.executive_summary: At the January 22, 2019 regular meeting presided over by Mayor Steve Schewel, the Durham City Council began with ceremonial recognitions and heard from a nonprofit providing free school supplies to Durham Public Schools teachers ahead of a citywide supply drive. Following introductions from new City Attorney Kim Rehberg and no priority items, the council voted unanimously 7-0 to adopt a consent agenda covering the 2019 Long Session Legislative Agenda, bicycle lane striping, waterline and street/bridge infrastructure contracts, a HIDTA grant amendment, an MLK Jr. Commission grant, and the Durham Workers Rights Commission scope and composition. In two public hearings without public speakers, the council unanimously voted 7-0 on both the consistency statement and ordinance for UDO text amendment TC18008 allowing limited text-only development plans, and voted 7-0 to adopt amendments to the Durham Comprehensive Plan's Future Land Use Map and policies.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Ceremonial Proclamation, and Nonprofit School Supply Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel called the meeting to order and presented a proclamation recognizing a longtime community champion. Representatives from a local nonprofit also spoke about supplying free school materials to teachers across more than 50 Durham Public Schools and partnering with city departments to place donation bins throughout city facilities.

agenda_items.title: Introduction of City Attorney Kim Rehberg and Staff Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Incoming City Attorney Kim Rehberg introduced herself in place of outgoing City Attorney Patrick Baker and reported no priority items. The City Clerk also reported no priority items.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 1-7 and 14, including Legislative Agenda, Streets/Water Contracts, and Workers Rights Commission)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Schewel read the consent agenda, which included the 2019 Long Session Legislative Agenda (Item 1), a bicycle lane striping agreement TIP C-5605E (Item 2), American Tobacco District waterline replacement Amendment No. 3 (Item 3), a 2018 HIDTA grant ordinance amendment (Item 4), Contract ST-271 for 2018 Petition Streets (Item 5), Contract ST-288B for a city-maintained bridge asset management plan (Item 6), the Durham Workers Rights Commission proposed scope and composition (Item 7), and an NC Martin Luther King Jr. Commission grant (Item 14). Audience members applauded following the council's unanimous approval of the consent slate.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Amendment TC18008 (Text-Only Development Plans)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Michael Stock of the Planning Department presented text amendment TC18008, creating a limited text-only development plan option for zoning map change requests to permit proffers restricting allowed uses while broader revisions are developed. He noted prior review by the Joint City-County Planning Committee, a 12-0 Planning Commission recommendation, and January 14 approval by the Board of County Commissioners. No members of the public spoke during the hearing, a council member thanked planning staff for timely work, and the council approved both the consistency statement and the ordinance amendment 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: 2017 Evaluation and Assessment Report of the Durham Comprehensive Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Laurie Woods of the Planning Department presented proposed Future Land Use Map and policy amendments from the 2017 Comprehensive Plan Evaluation and Assessment Report, including three parcels providing a direct connection between the state park and Valley Springs Park. No members of the public spoke during the hearing; council members asked about engagement strategy and discussed Planning Commission feedback—specifically Commissioner Miller's concern about burdens on Neighborhood Protection Overlays (NPOs) and historic districts after staff removed a mandatory denial recommendation tied to affordability impacts. The council closed the hearing and adopted the resolution amending the Future Land Use Map and policies 7-0.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the January 10, 2019 City Council Work Session, six members were present and unanimously voted to excuse Council Member Mark-Anthony Middleton (who was delivering a eulogy). Council unanimously approved the City Manager's priority items, separately authorized filling a vacant Durham One Call position in the City Manager's Office as an Assistant to the Mayor, approved a closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) for a personnel matter, and suspended the rules to approve transferring $1,500 from the Mayor's travel account to supplement Council intern wages. On the 2019 Long Session Legislative Agenda (Item 1), Council unanimously adopted a motion to add raising the state minimum wage to $15 per hour after a brief debate over ad-hoc agenda additions versus strategic prioritization, and requested title clarification on the 30%/60% AMI circuit-breaker tax exemption. Council also heard an NCDOT update on staged closures of Alston Avenue, discussed 2006 street paving petitions (Item 5) and bridge asset management (Item 6), heard community advocates on the proposed Durham Workers Rights Commission (Item 7), and unanimously approved the settled agenda before entering closed session.

agenda_items.title: Excusal of Council Member Mark-Anthony Middleton & Priority Items (Assistant to the Mayor, Closed Session, Intern Wage Transfer)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted unanimously to excuse Council Member Mark-Anthony Middleton (delivering a eulogy). Council then approved the City Manager's priority items (including supplemental Item 14, an NC MLK Jr. Commission grant), voted separately to authorize filling a funded vacant Durham One Call slot as an Assistant to the Mayor, approved City Attorney Patrick Baker's request for a personnel closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6), and suspended the rules to transfer $1,500 from the Mayor's travel budget to part-time personnel for Council intern wages.

agenda_items.title: NCDOT Briefing on Alston Avenue Staged Closure
agenda_items.discussion_summary: NCDOT engineers briefed Council on closing Alston Avenue in two six-month stages (Main to Taylor, then Taylor to Liberty) to accelerate construction while maintaining property access, noting coordination with city staff and GoTriangle since March 2018 and two public meetings in April (25–30 attendees) and November (5 attendees).

agenda_items.title: 2019 Long Session Legislative Agenda ($15/Hour Minimum Wage Amendment & Circuit Breaker Clarification)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff reviewed caveats added to the 2019 legislative agenda on regular evaluation of state incentives and body-camera confidentiality agreements (Item 17). A council member moved to amend the agenda to urge raising the state minimum wage to $15/hour; after a brief exchange over whether ad-hoc additions reduce strategic effectiveness versus staking a clear policy position, Council adopted the amendment unanimously by voice vote. A member also flagged that Item 7's title omitted the 30% and 60% local AMI thresholds for the circuit-breaker property tax exemption.

agenda_items.title: Petition Streets Project (Contract ST-271-2018) & Bridge Asset Management Plan (Contract ST-28B)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: During discussion of Contract ST-271-2018 (Petition Streets Project), a council member clarified that criticism of delays on older paving petitions (such as a 2006 Castile Drive petition) was directed at City Council rather than staff and asked whether current residents still wish to pay assessments. Staff also outlined risk analysis and funding options under Contract ST-28B with Kercher Group Inc. for city-maintained bridge structures and culverts.

agenda_items.title: Formation of a Durham Workers Rights Commission (Proposed Scope & Composition)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Community advocates spoke in support of establishing a Durham Workers Rights Commission, citing North Carolina's right-to-work laws and roughly 3% union density (second lowest behind South Carolina). Council Member Vernetta Alston thanked advocates and confirmed the proposal was slated for consent approval at the Tuesday night regular meeting following MLK Day.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Settlement & Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager settled the regular meeting agenda with Consent Items 1–7 and 14 and Public Hearings 8–9. Council unanimously approved the settled agenda by voice vote and entered closed session pursuant to the earlier personnel motion.

votes.item_title: Excuse Absence of Council Member Mark-Anthony Middleton
votes.notes: Voice vote passed unanimously among the six members present (Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Vernetta Alston, Javiera Caballero, DeDreana Freeman, Charlie Reece).
votes.discussion_detail: Granted an excused absence to Council Member Mark-Anthony Middleton while delivering a eulogy.

votes.item_title: Acceptance of City Manager Priority Items
votes.notes: Voice vote passed unanimously among the six members present.
votes.discussion_detail: Accepted the City Manager's priority updates (NCDOT Alston Ave briefing, Item 1 and 7 attachments, absent speaker on Item 11, and supplemental Item 14 NC MLK Jr. Commission grant), excluding the separate Assistant to the Mayor item.

votes.item_title: Authorize City Manager to Fill Vacant Position as Assistant to the Mayor
votes.notes: Voice vote passed unanimously among the six members present.
votes.discussion_detail: Authorized the City Manager to fill an already-authorized, funded vacant Durham One Call position in the City Manager's Office with an Assistant to the Mayor.

votes.item_title: Approve City Attorney Priority Item (Closed Session for Personnel Matter)
votes.notes: Voice vote passed unanimously among the six members present.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved City Attorney Patrick Baker's priority request for a closed session at the end of the meeting under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) for a personnel matter.

votes.item_title: Suspend Rules for City Clerk Priority Item (Council Intern Wage Transfer)
votes.notes: Voice vote passed unanimously among the six members present.
votes.discussion_detail: Suspended council rules to vote immediately on transferring funds to supplement Council intern wages.

votes.item_title: Transfer $1,500 from Mayor's Travel Account to Supplement Council Intern Wages
votes.notes: Voice vote passed unanimously among the six members present.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the City Clerk's recommendation to transfer $1,500 from the Mayor's travel account to part-time personnel to supplement the Council intern's wages.

votes.item_title: Amend 2019 Legislative Agenda to Advocate Raising State Minimum Wage to $15/Hour
votes.notes: Voice vote passed unanimously among the six members present.
votes.discussion_detail: Amended the 2019 Long Session Legislative Agenda to include a state-level advocacy item raising the minimum wage to $15 per hour after brief discussion regarding legislative prioritization.

votes.item_title: Approval of Settled City Council Agenda
votes.notes: Voice vote passed unanimously among the six members present.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the settled agenda for the regular meeting comprising Consent Items 1–7 and 14 and Public Hearings 8–9.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Jan 7, 2019
meetings.executive_summary: At its first meeting of 2019 on January 7, the Durham City Council recognized Durham Parks and Recreation staff, a local international youth chess champion, Martin Luther King Jr. Day commemoration events, and January as National Mentoring Month with remarks from the Emily K Center. Council voted 7-0 to refer Agenda Item 9 (unarmed security guard services for city parking facilities) back to the City Manager's office, and City Attorney Patrick Baker read his resignation notice effective March 8, 2019 after 21 years of service to Durham. Council unanimously approved 7-0 the consent agenda (excluding Items 3, 8, and 9) covering transportation planning agreements, hazard mitigation grants, board changes, and travel policy. Following public comment from resident Victoria Peterson on Items 3 and 8 regarding youth programming, community centers, and economic development, the council voted 7-0 to approve both the Bloomberg Mayor's Challenge Grant (Item 3) and Item 8.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Silent Meditation, Pledge of Allegiance, and Roll Call
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel called the January 7, 2019 meeting to order, wished residents a happy New Year, and led a moment of silent meditation. Council Member Charlie Reece led the Pledge of Allegiance, and the City Clerk called the roll confirming the attendance of council members.

agenda_items.title: Proclamations and Recognitions (DPR, Youth Chess Champion, MLK Events, National Mentoring Month)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Schewel and the council presented proclamations and recognitions, beginning with remarks thanking Durham Parks and Recreation employees, the City Manager, and Deputy City Manager Bo Ferguson. The council honored a local youth chess champion competing internationally who discussed empowering girls in chess, announced upcoming Martin Luther King Jr. Day events including the January 21 interfaith prayer breakfast, and proclaimed January 2019 National Mentoring Month with remarks from an Emily K Center representative.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Item: Refer Agenda Item 9 (Parking Facilities Security Guard Services) Back to Administration
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Bonfield requested as a priority item that Agenda Item 9—uniformed unarmed security guard services for the city's parking facilities—be referred back to the administration. Council voted unanimously 7-0 to refer the item back to the City Manager's office.

agenda_items.title: City Attorney Patrick Baker Resignation Announcement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Reporting no priority items, City Attorney Patrick Baker requested personal privilege to read his resignation letter submitted during an earlier 6:00 p.m. closed session, giving notice effective March 8, 2019. Mayor Schewel praised Baker's 21 years of service as both City Manager and City Attorney and wished him well in his new role in Charlotte, and the City Clerk reported no priority items.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Items 3, 8, and 9)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Schewel read the consent agenda including minutes (Item 1), Historic Preservation Commission appointment (Item 2), Elected Officials Travel Authorization and Expense Reimbursement Policy (Item 4), Environmental Affairs Board expansion (Item 6), a Phase Two developer agreement and option contract (Item 7), DCHC MPO and NCDOT agreements for a Congestion Management Process web application (Item 10) and web-based TIP update (Item 11), the November 2018 bid report (Item 12), and Hazard Mitigation Grant Program items (Items 13 and 14). Items 3 and 8 were pulled by resident Victoria Peterson and Item 9 was referred back to staff; the remaining consent items passed 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 3: Bloomberg Mayor's Challenge Grant
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resident Victoria Peterson pulled Item 3 and spoke for three minutes, expressing surprise at City Attorney Baker's departure and raising concerns about youth programming and community centers. Mayor Schewel responded that the city operates many community centers open every afternoon serving hundreds of youth and will continue doing so, after which council approved Item 3 by a 7-0 vote.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 8: First-Time Homebuyer and Economic Development Program Item
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resident Victoria Peterson pulled Item 8 to critique economic development outreach and highlight violent crime concerns in the community. A council member clarified an acronym referenced during public comment, acknowledged Peterson's concerns about programming, and asked staff to follow up so she is informed about the department's first-time homebuyer and related initiatives, before council voted 7-0 to approve Item 8.

votes.item_title: Refer Agenda Item 9 (Uniformed Unarmed Security Guard Services for City Parking Facilities) Back to Administration
votes.notes: Mover and seconder were not named in the transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: City Manager Bonfield requested referring Item 9 back to the administration; council moved, seconded, and approved the referral 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 3: Bloomberg Mayor's Challenge Grant
votes.notes: Mover and seconder were not named in the transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: Following three minutes of public comment from Victoria Peterson and remarks from Mayor Schewel on afternoon youth services at city community centers, council approved Item 3 unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 8: First-Time Homebuyer and Economic Development Program Item
votes.notes: Mover and seconder were not named in the transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: Following public comment from Victoria Peterson and a council member's request for staff follow-up to share program details including first-time homebuyer offerings, council approved Item 8 unanimously 7-0.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Mayor Pro Tempore Jillian Johnson (with excused absences approved for Mayor Steve Schewel and Council Member Vernetta Alston), the December 20, 2018 City Council Work Session heard priority updates from the City Manager on NCDOT's January 2, 2019 full closure of Austin Avenue during construction and a federal lead paint abatement grant exceeding $2.6 million, and approved a closed session request for litigation matters (Friedman v. City of Durham and Ortiz v. City of Durham). Durham County Public Health and County Attorney staff briefed Council on updates to the Board of Health's no-smoking rule adding e-cigarettes and extending coverage to City- and County-owned sidewalks as an educational policy. Following a truncated middle portion of the transcript, Council reviewed parking security contract training, the Willard Street Phase 2 joint-venture 9% LIHTC affordable housing timeline and option agreement, preparations and $100,000 in community grants for the Durham 150 sesquicentennial, and equitable engagement plans for the Move Durham Central Durham transportation study. At the close of the session, Council settled the consent agenda (referring Item 5 on the Durham Workers' Rights Commission back to January 10) and nominated April Johnson to the Historic Preservation Commission by a 5-0 ballot vote.

agenda_items.title: Roll Call, Excused Absences, and Council Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Jillian Johnson opened the work session, with Council Members Javiera Caballero, Mark-Anthony Middleton, and Charlie Reece answering roll call (Council Member DeDreana Freeman did not respond at roll call, though five members later participated in the Historic Preservation Commission vote). Council approved excused absences for Mayor Steve Schewel and Council Member Vernetta Alston by unanimous voice vote. Members then thanked Parks and Recreation, Public Works, GoDurham, and Downtown Durham Inc. for organizing the holiday parade and Christmas tree lighting.

agenda_items.title: City Manager and City Attorney Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager requested moving Item 15 (Board of Health No Smoking Rule) earlier to 1:15 PM, notified Council that NCDOT would close Austin Avenue in stages beginning January 2, 2019 through December without delaying for a Council briefing, and announced a federal lead paint abatement grant of $2.6 million or more. Council unanimously accepted the manager's priority items by voice vote. The City Attorney then requested a closed session under NCGS 143-318.11(a)(3) for Friedman v. City of Durham and Ortiz v. City of Durham, which Council approved by unanimous voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Update on Durham County Board of Health No Smoking Rule
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A Durham County Public Health tobacco health education specialist reported that the 2012 Board of Health smoking rule was updated to prohibit e-cigarettes and expand coverage to all sidewalks owned, operated, or maintained by the City or County, accompanied by downtown signage. County Attorney representative Brian Wardell emphasized that the rule was framed as an educational rather than enforcement measure. A council member noted having served on the Joint City-County Committee for over a year without having heard about the sidewalk expansion before the transcript digest truncated.

agenda_items.title: Unarmed Security Guard Services and Willard Street Phase 2 Affordable Housing Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resuming after a truncated gap, Council heard details on site-specific hiring and training under the unarmed security guard contract for City parking facilities (Item 9). Staff then presented the developer agreement and option agreement for Willard Street Phase 2, explaining the joint venture would submit a 9% LIHTC application in January 2019 (with site scores in April, full applications in May, awards in August, and a December 2021 construction deadline). The agreement also funds subdivision of the Phase 2 parcel and reserves a Pettigrew Street corner affected by elevated light rail plans.

agenda_items.title: Update on Durham 150 Celebration Preparations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Beverly Thompson introduced Shelley Green to present preparations for Durham's 150th anniversary at Durham150.org. Green thanked Council for its $225,000 lead gift toward an additional $600,000 corporate and foundation fundraising target, and outlined $100,000 set aside for $500 to $2,000 neighborhood event grants opening January 2, 2019. Presenters also described coordination with the Sesquicentennial Honors Commission.

agenda_items.title: Move Durham Central Durham Transportation Study Outreach
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Transportation staff and consultant Jennifer Baldwin of Alta Planning and Design presented the public engagement strategy for the Move Durham Central Durham Transportation Study. To pilot elements of the Equitable Engagement Blueprint, the study proposed a stipend-supported Community Ambassador program partnering with local organizations, alongside outreach at Participatory Budgeting meetings and an online survey at movedurham.org.

agenda_items.title: Settling the Agenda and Historic Preservation Commission Nomination
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council settled the upcoming meeting agenda with Consent Items 1–4 and 6–14, referring Item 5 (Durham Workers' Rights Commission) back to the January 10, 2019 work session cycle. The clerk announced Council nominated April Johnson to the Historian seat on the Historic Preservation Commission by a 5-0 ballot vote. Council approved the settled agenda by voice vote, requested codifying staff follow-up with the Alliance representative on the smoking rule items, and paused briefly to locate the City Attorney for closed session statutory language.

votes.item_title: Excused Absences for Mayor Steve Schewel and Council Member Vernetta Alston
votes.notes: DeDreana Freeman did not answer roll call at 00:00:11; Schewel and Alston were excused.
votes.discussion_detail: Mayor Schewel and Council Member Alston requested excused absences prior to the meeting; the motion to excuse passed without opposition.

votes.item_title: Acceptance of City Manager's Priority Items
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote; mover not named in ASR.
votes.discussion_detail: Accepted the manager's priority items, including advancing Item 15 (Board of Health No Smoking Rule) and briefing Council on the Austin Avenue closure and federal lead abatement grant.

votes.item_title: Approval of City Attorney's Closed Session Priority Item
votes.notes: Voice vote with no opposition.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved entering closed session pursuant to NCGS 143-318.11(a)(3) regarding Friedman v. City of Durham and Ortiz v. City of Durham.

votes.item_title: Historic Preservation Commission Nomination: April Johnson (Historian)
votes.notes: Paper ballot vote tallied by the clerk at 5-0; individual ballot votes were not read into the transcript, though DeDreana Freeman must have joined the four initially present members (Johnson, Caballero, Middleton, Reece) to cast five ballots.
votes.discussion_detail: The clerk announced Council nominated April Johnson to the Historian category on the Historic Preservation Commission by a vote of 5-0.
