meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the September 20, 2018 City Council Work Session chaired by Mayor Steve Schewel, Council heard Citizen Matters from Mike Fless urging demographic weighting and racial subgroup reporting in City police satisfaction surveys, and from resident Ms. Chambers regarding illegal dumping and sex work on an unmaintained City street—prompting Mayor Pro Tempore Jillian Johnson to ask about police diversion alternatives to incarceration. Council addressed the delayed Racial Equity Task Force appointments (Item 3), voting unanimously by voice to support Judge Elaine O'Neal as chair in an informal poll, suspend the rules, and amend the task force bylaws to 17 members before selecting 16 additional members via paper ballot. Members also expressed informal support for Joseph Blocker and Michelle Gonzalez-Green on the Sesquicentennial Honors Commission (Item 4), praised Audit Services' Housing for New Hope rapid rehousing audit (Item 7), and questioned staff on MWBE subcontractor outreach and take-home police vehicle costs before unanimously settling Consent Items 1–15.

agenda_items.title: Roll Call, Announcements, and Agenda Reading
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel called the session to order, with Council announcing that the Council Procedures Committee would reconvene in mid-October to address four or five pending items from June. The City Manager noted Scott Barn would be absent for General Item 16. Council read the agenda and pulled Item 3 (Racial Equity Task Force), Item 4 (Sesquicentennial Honors Commission), and Item 7 (Housing for New Hope rapid rehousing audit).

agenda_items.title: Citizen Matters: Resident Survey Methodology and Street Dumping/Diversion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mike Fless urged Council to compare resident survey samples to Durham demographics and report police satisfaction disaggregated by race, ethnicity, and income, noting over 20% of Black and Hispanic respondents reported safety concerns with police (vs. 3% of white/Asian respondents) and 17% cited discrimination (vs. 1% of white respondents). Ms. Chambers asked to block off an unmaintained street used for dumping and sex work; NIS's Faith Gardner reported the area was cleaned, and Mayor Pro Tempore Jillian Johnson requested exploring police diversion programs rather than jail for sex workers.

agenda_items.title: Racial Equity Task Force Bylaws Amendment and Member Selection
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following small-group caucusing led by Council Member Mark-Anthony Middleton, Council held an informal unanimous voice vote supporting Judge Elaine O'Neal as Chair of the Racial Equity Task Force, then suspended the rules and unanimously amended the bylaws to establish 17 members inclusive of a mayoral-nominated chair (correcting a prior flawed selection of only 12). Resident Chris Tiffany later urged reopening applications and cited the 2016 youth-police survey. At 01:02:21, the clerk announced the 17 ballot selections: Chair Elaine O'Neal plus Tia Hall, Vanessa Hines, Corey Hogans, Jessica Ligon-Bull, Cameron Smith, David Dixon, Karen Haldeman, Anna Nunez, James Tabron, Emily Coward, Javonia Lewis, Howard McTinger, Daniel McKinney, Katie McAnglewa, Jamelmas, and Cecilia Polanco.

agenda_items.title: Sesquicentennial Honors Commission and Rapid Rehousing Audit
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council held an informal unanimous voice vote supporting Joseph Blocker and Michelle Gonzalez-Green for the Sesquicentennial Honors Commission before marking ballots for seven total seats. On Item 7, Council Member Charlie Reece praised Audit Services Director Germaine Brewington's Housing for New Hope Rapid Rehousing performance audit and requested follow-up from Community Development on the underlying program plan. Council also discussed MWBE contractor diversity and Fleet Management costs for take-home police cars before unanimously settling Consent Items 1–15 and adjourning.

votes.item_title: Informal Sense of Council: Support Nomination of Judge Elaine O'Neal as Chair of Racial Equity Task Force
votes.notes: Mayor Schewel noted for the clerk that this was an informal sense-of-the-group vote; individual present members were not polled separately.
votes.discussion_detail: Informal sense-of-the-group vote supporting Judge Elaine O'Neal as chair ahead of the regular Monday council meeting.

votes.item_title: Suspend the Rules to Amend Racial Equity Task Force Bylaws
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote; Mayor Pro Tempore Johnson, Alston, Caballero, Middleton, Reece, and Schewel answered roll call, and Freeman's presence was not audible at roll call.
votes.discussion_detail: Suspended the work-session rules to take formal immediate action amending the Racial Equity Task Force bylaws.

votes.item_title: Amend Racial Equity Task Force Bylaws to 17 Members Inclusive of Chair
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Amended the bylaws to set membership at 17 members inclusive of the chair to be nominated by the Mayor, followed by paper ballots selecting 16 additional members.

votes.item_title: Informal Sense of Council: Support Joseph Blocker and Michelle Gonzalez-Green for Sesquicentennial Honors Commission
votes.notes: Informal voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Expressed unanimous sense of the group supporting Blocker and Gonzalez-Green on the following Monday's formal agenda, alongside marking ballots for seven commission seats.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Sept 17, 2018
meetings.executive_summary: Meeting on September 17, 2018 in the wake of Hurricane Florence, the Durham City Council recognized PAC-3 neighborhood safety volunteers and commended city employees, the Hillside High School shelter, and the Emergency Operations Center for storm preparedness before approving the consent agenda 7-0. On Item 9, after hearing Bike Durham advocate James Nishimoto and Bird representative Servando Esparza regarding electric scooter regulations, Council voted 7-0 to refer the shared active transportation permitting ordinance to the Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Commission (BPAC) for input. Council unanimously passed all three motions (7-0 each) for consolidated annexation Item 17, the Southeast Regional Lift Station annexation (Item 18), and the AAA Storage annexation near Junction Road (Item 20), referred a withdrawn Christian Avenue street closing (Item 19) back to administration without a vote, and voted 7-0 to close a 330.08-foot portion of K Street needed for the Durham-Orange Light Rail right-of-way (Item 21).

agenda_items.title: PAC-3 Safety Recognition and Hurricane Florence Emergency Response Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council recognized neighborhood safety volunteers coordinating with DPD and PAC-3 and noted Constitution Week. City Manager Tom Bonfield, Mayor Schewel, Mayor Pro Tem Johnson, and Council Members Alston and Reece praised city staff, the Emergency Operations Center, and volunteers at the Hillside High School emergency shelter for their Hurricane Florence response.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Appointments, DCLT & Habitat Housing Contracts, Triangle Water Supply Partnership, Sibiu Sister City)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Schewel read consent items including minutes, Durham Housing Authority, Human Relations Commission, and Recreation Advisory Commission appointments, DCLT (1700 Merrymac St) and Habitat for Humanity housing contracts, the Triangle Water Supply Partnership MOA, Carolina Assisted Living utility extension, and the Sibiu, Romania sister city proposal. Council unanimously approved the consent agenda 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Ordinance Regulating Shared Active Transportation Companies (E-Scooters)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Bike Durham board member James Nishimoto supported the scooter permitting ordinance and called for protected bike lanes, while Bird senior manager Servando Esparza supported the ordinance while asking Council to revisit the $100-per-scooter fee and noting Bird's low-income One Bird program. Council Member Charlie Reece, joined by Vernetta Alston, requested deferring action so Durham's Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Commission (BPAC) could review the draft, and Council voted 7-0 to refer the ordinance back for BPAC input.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation and Zoning Map Change (Public Hearing)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council held a public hearing on consolidated annexation Item 17 with no registered speakers or public opposition. Council unanimously voted 7-0 on the annexation ordinance, consistency statement, and UDO zoning ordinance.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation — Southeast Regional Lift Station
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Grace Smith presented the consolidated annexation and rezoning for the Southeast Regional Lift Station. With no public speakers or council objections, Council approved the annexation ordinance, consistency statement, and UDO zoning ordinance 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Christian Avenue Street Closing (Withdrawn)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pat Young reported that the applicant withdrew the Christian Avenue street closing request late the prior week. With City Attorney concurrence, Mayor Schewel referred Item 19 back to the administration without a formal vote.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation — AAA Storage (Junction Road)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jamie Sunyak presented AAA Storage's voluntary annexation and rezoning to Industrial Light with a two-story height limit, noting the Planning Commission voted 11-0 and the project would be immediately revenue-positive. Responding to DeDreana Freeman's flooding question on Junction Road, landscape architect Pam Porter confirmed there is no floodplain on site, and Council passed all three motions 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — K Street Closing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Carla Rosenberg recommended permanently closing a 330.08-linear-foot portion of K Street to combine with adjacent properties, confirming for Council that the right-of-way lies within the planned Durham-Orange Light Rail corridor. With no public speakers, Council unanimously adopted the closure order 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 9: Refer Shared Active Transportation Permitting Ordinance to BPAC
votes.discussion_detail: Following Charlie Reece's request supported by Vernetta Alston, Council unanimously referred the shared active transportation (e-scooter) ordinance to BPAC for feedback.

votes.item_title: Item 17: Annexation Ordinance (Consolidated Item 17)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the annexation ordinance for Item 17.

votes.item_title: Item 17: Consistency Statement (Consolidated Item 17)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the consistency statement for Item 17.

votes.item_title: Item 17: Ordinance Amending the UDO (Consolidated Item 17)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously approved the UDO zoning amendment for Item 17.

votes.item_title: Item 18: Ordinance Annexing Southeast Regional Lift Station
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously approved annexing the Southeast Regional Lift Station into the City of Durham.

votes.item_title: Item 18: Consistency Statement for Southeast Regional Lift Station
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the consistency statement for the Southeast Regional Lift Station.

votes.item_title: Item 18: Ordinance Amending the UDO for Southeast Regional Lift Station
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the UDO zoning amendment for the Southeast Regional Lift Station.

votes.item_title: Item 20: Ordinance Annexing AAA Storage and Utility Extension Agreement
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously approved the voluntary annexation and utility extension agreement for AAA Storage.

votes.item_title: Item 20: Consistency Statement for AAA Storage
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the consistency statement for AAA Storage.

votes.item_title: Item 20: Ordinance Amending the UDO for AAA Storage (Industrial Light)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously approved Industrial Light zoning with a two-story limit for AAA Storage.

votes.item_title: Item 21: Order Permanently Closing a 330.08-Linear-Foot Portion of K Street
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously ordered the permanent closure of the 330.08-foot K Street segment within the planned light rail corridor.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Opening at 1:05 PM after an extended closed session, Mayor Steve Schewel presided over the September 6, 2018 City Council Work Session with Council Member Vernetta Alston on an excused absence. Council approved the City Attorney's closed-session request for Parker v. City of Durham et al. and heard urgent consideration of Item 11 (a 2018 U.S. Soccer Foundation grant converting two isolated East End Park tennis courts into a futsal pitch ahead of a September 24 contract deadline). On Item 11, a motion to suspend the work-session voting rules passed on a 5-1 split voice vote (six members present—Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, DeDreana Freeman, Mark-Anthony Middleton, and Javiera Caballero—with Vernetta Alston excused, and individual Ayes and the lone Nay not named on the voice-vote record), after which the grant itself passed unanimously. Following a truncated middle segment, staff briefed Council on residential backup options for Willard Street Phase 2 (9% LIHTC vs. mixed-income condominiums) and Police Chief C.J. Davis and Triangle HIDTA staff faced council scrutiny over task-force overtime, equitable-sharing asset forfeiture funds, and local drug data before Council settled the agenda and re-entered closed session.

agenda_items.title: Roll Call, Priority Items, and Agenda Reading
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel apologized for starting at 1:05 PM after an extended closed session and noted Council Member Vernetta Alston's excused absence. Council approved the City Manager's priority item flagging urgency for Item 11 (U.S. Soccer Foundation grant) and unanimously approved the City Attorney's request for a closed session under NCGS 143-318.11(a)(3) for Parker v. City of Durham et al. During agenda reading, a liaison raised diversity concerns on the Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Commission (Item 2) and Council pulled Items 9 and 10.

agenda_items.title: 2018 United States Soccer Foundation Grant (East End Park Futsal Conversion)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Parks and Recreation staff explained that the U.S. Soccer Foundation grant would convert two isolated, unused tennis courts behind the former Ed Nichols Recreation Center at East End Park into a futsal pitch without removing basketball courts or building a risky barrier fence. Because the grantor required a signed contract by September 24 for September 24 renovations, Council voted 5-1 by unnamed voice vote to suspend the rules (Alston excused) and then unanimously approved the grant.

agenda_items.title: Shared Active Transportation Ordinance Revision (Motorized Scooters)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Before the transcript digest truncated, a council member discussed working with Transportation staff ('Brian') on Item 9, the Shared Active Transportation Ordinance. The member highlighted an amendment replacing references to 'scooter' with 'motorized scooter' to make the regulatory language more explicit.

agenda_items.title: Willard Street Phase 2 Residential Backup Options
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resuming after a truncated gap, staff briefed Council on backup development options for Willard Street Phase 2 after determining office development was unfeasible. Preliminary modeling showed 9% LIHTC and mixed-income condominiums were viable while mixed-income rental required excessive subsidy; staff planned for Willard Street to submit a 9% LIHTC application alongside the Durham Housing Authority and withdraw if DHA scored higher or tied.

agenda_items.title: Triangle High Intensity Drug Trafficking Area (HIDTA) Briefing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DPD Chief C.J. Davis and task force presenters briefed Council on Durham's 2007 inclusion in the Atlanta-Carolinas HIDTA, outlining a $200,000+ overtime budget, a new NC prevention specialist, and federal-state-local trafficking enforcement. Council members questioned whether heavy overtime signaled understaffing, examined how asset forfeiture funds are split, deposited, audited against general-fund supplanting, and spent, and requested local drug data to evaluate program outcomes.

agenda_items.title: Settling the Agenda and Motion to Enter Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council received the clerk's tally sheets and settled the upcoming agenda with Consent Items, GBA Item 9, and GBA public hearing items by voice vote. Council then voted unanimously by voice to enter closed session for the attorney-client consultation announced by the City Attorney.

votes.item_title: Accept City Manager's Priority Item (Item 11 Urgency)
votes.notes: Voice vote; Council Member Vernetta Alston had an excused absence.
votes.discussion_detail: Accepted the manager's priority item highlighting the September 24 contract deadline for the U.S. Soccer Foundation grant.

votes.item_title: Approve City Attorney's Priority Items (Closed Session for Parker v. City of Durham et al.)
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote; Alston excused.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved closed session pursuant to NCGS 143-318.11(a)(3) for attorney-client consultation on Parker v. City of Durham et al., alongside introducing Assistant City Attorney Sophia Hernandez Atkins.

votes.item_title: Suspend the Rules for Immediate Vote on Item 11 (2018 U.S. Soccer Foundation Grant)
votes.notes: Split 5-1 voice vote among the six present members (Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, DeDreana Freeman, Mark-Anthony Middleton, and Javiera Caballero; Vernetta Alston excused). Individual Ayes and the lone Nay were not named on the record in the transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to suspend Council work-session rules to vote immediately on the U.S. Soccer Foundation grant contract at the work session.

votes.item_title: Item 11: Approve 2018 United States Soccer Foundation Grant
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote among present members (Alston excused).
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the grant contract converting two East End Park tennis courts into a futsal pitch following suspension of the rules.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session
votes.notes: Voice vote with no opposition.
votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session for the attorney-client purpose stated earlier by the City Attorney.

disagreements.issue: Suspending Work-Session Rules for Immediate Vote on Item 11 (U.S. Soccer Foundation Grant)
disagreements.summary: Council divided 5-1 on a procedural motion to suspend work-session rules and vote immediately on the U.S. Soccer Foundation grant rather than waiting for a regular televised meeting, though the grant itself subsequently passed unanimously.
disagreements.side_a_position: Suspend the rules to act immediately and meet the grantor's contract deadline.
side_a_arguments: The U.S. Soccer Foundation required the signed contract by September 24 so East End Park futsal renovations could begin on schedule.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose suspending work-session rules for immediate binding votes.
side_b_arguments: A single unnamed member voted 'No' on the procedural suspension motion before joining unanimous support for the underlying grant.
disagreements.resolution: Motion to suspend the rules passed 5-1 by unnamed voice vote (Vernetta Alston excused), and Item 11 then passed unanimously.

disagreements.issue: Scrutiny of HIDTA Overtime Staffing, Asset Forfeiture Accounting, and Local Drug Data
disagreements.summary: During the Triangle HIDTA briefing, council members questioned Police Chief C.J. Davis and task force staff over whether heavy overtime indicated insufficient base staffing, how seized asset forfeiture funds were distributed and audited, and whether local drug trend data supported ongoing participation.
disagreements.side_a_position: Scrutinize HIDTA overtime reliance, asset forfeiture incentives, and measurable local drug outcomes.
side_a_arguments: Questioned whether funding the bulk of HIDTA participation through overtime indicated inadequate regular staffing.
Probed how asset forfeiture funds are split, retained by DPD vs. City general coffers, audited, and expended.
Noted the drug crisis worsened toward opioids and sought local micro-level data showing whether HIDTA cases improved Durham outcomes.
disagreements.side_b_position: Defend HIDTA federal-local task force structure, federal audit controls, and multi-agency trafficking investigations.
side_b_arguments: Chief C.J. Davis and task force staff explained lengthy surveillance cases require overtime and that the lead investigative agency receives the larger forfeiture share.
DPD reports forfeiture expenditures annually to federal auditors to prevent general-fund supplanting and uses funds for public education and investigative tools.
disagreements.resolution: Informational briefing without a vote; staff agreed to pull additional local data on case outcomes.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Sept 4, 2018
meetings.executive_summary: At its September 4, 2018 meeting, the Durham City Council honored late civic and educational leader Dr. Phail Wynn Jr. (highlighting his work on the housing trust fund and early childhood education), proclaimed September 2018 as National Recovery Month, and announced five vacancies on the Sesquicentennial Honors Commission. Council unanimously passed the consent agenda 7-0 (excluding pulled Items 3 and 8) and passed 7-0 both motions for UDO text amendment TC18-00003 adopting revised FEMA Flood Insurance Rate Map (FIRM) panels to maintain National Flood Insurance Program eligibility. On pulled Item 3, Mark-Anthony Middleton recommended postponing the Racial Equity Task Force appointments because the proposed slate included only one African American male out of nine applicants; Vernetta Alston and DeDreana Freeman agreed, and Mayor Steve Schewel referred the item by consensus to the September 20 work session while announcing plans to nominate Judge Elaine O'Neal as chair. On pulled Item 8, Council approved 7-0 a $2.9 million Central Park waterline replacement change order (capping total contract cost at $32,008,878.42) after DeDreana Freeman questioned downtown infrastructure prioritization and pressed staff on zero-diversity contractor workforce statistics under the Equal Business Opportunity Program.

agenda_items.title: Tribute to Dr. Phail Wynn Jr., National Recovery Month Proclamation, and Sesquicentennial Honors Commission
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel and speakers paid tribute to late Dr. Phail Wynn Jr. for his housing trust fund advocacy and early childhood education leadership. Mayor Schewel proclaimed September 2018 as National Recovery Month addressing opioid and mental health stigma, and the City Clerk announced five vacancies on the Sesquicentennial Honors Commission.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Board Appointments, GARE Grant, GoDurham Gillig Buses, Rock Quarry & Morreene Parks, Unpaved Road Study)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Schewel read the consent agenda including minutes, BPAC, Environmental Affairs Board, and Board of Adjustment appointments, a Government Alliance on Race and Equity (GARE) grant, Gillig replacement buses for GoDurham, financial advisor selection, Rock Quarry Park and Morreene Road Park contracts, BizLibrary e-learning, the unpaved road study (SD-292-2018), and South Ellerbe stormwater demolition. Pulling Items 3 and 8, Council approved the consent agenda 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — UDO Text Amendment: FEMA FIRM Flood Map Updates (TC18-00003)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Michael Stock presented TC18-00003 updating Section 8.4 of the UDO to adopt revised FEMA Flood Insurance Rate Map (FIRM) panels effective October 19, 2018, a federal and state requirement to maintain Durham's participation in the National Flood Insurance Program. The Planning Commission had recommended approval 12-0, and Council passed both the consistency statement and UDO amendment 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item — Racial Equity Task Force Appointments (Deferred to Sept 20 Work Session)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Mark-Anthony Middleton (who had missed the work session selection) urged Council not to vote because the slate included only one African American male despite nine applying, calling it a systemic teachable moment for Durham's Racial Equity Task Force. Vernetta Alston and DeDreana Freeman supported postponement; Mayor Schewel referred the appointments by unanimous consensus to the September 20 work session, tasked Middleton with leading member discussions, and announced his intent to nominate Judge Elaine O'Neal as chair once membership is settled.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item — Central Park Waterline Replacement Contract Change Order No. 3
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Water Management Director Don Greeley explained the $2.9 million change order for failing cast-iron lines in the Central Park project (bringing total contract cost up to $32,008,878.42) and outlined upcoming $20 million waterline replacements in East Durham. DeDreana Freeman questioned whether downtown gentrification was driving utility prioritization and pressed Purchasing Manager Ms. Page on why many city supply/vendor contracts report zero people of color despite the Equal Business Opportunity Program ordinance; Mayor Schewel echoed concern over industry capacity gaps before Council approved the change order 7-0.

votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously approved the consent agenda excluding pulled Items 3 and 8.

votes.item_title: Item 20: Consistency Statement for UDO Text Amendment TC18-00003 (FEMA FIRM Updates)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the consistency statement for adopting revised FEMA flood insurance maps.

votes.item_title: Item 20: Ordinance Adopting UDO Text Amendment TC18-00003 (FEMA FIRM Updates)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the UDO flood map updates required to maintain NFIP eligibility.

votes.item_title: Item 8: Central Park Waterline Replacement Change Order No. 3 and Additional Contingency (Not to Exceed $32,008,878.42)
votes.discussion_detail: After discussing downtown versus East Durham waterline replacement priorities and EBOP vendor diversity tracking, Council unanimously approved Change Order No. 3.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel presided over the August 23, 2018 City Council Work Session, where Council approved an excused absence for Council Member Mark-Anthony Middleton (with DeDreana Freeman arriving after roll call) and recognized departing management analyst Mani-Sue Seemans. Council praised a Government Alliance on Race and Equity (GARE) grant for expunctions and driver's license restorations (Item 6), examined MWBE scarcity in sewer evaluation (Item 9), financial advisor fiduciary separation (Item 10), and street-paving prioritization criteria, and heard the Recreation Advisory Commission's annual presentation (Item 18). City-County Planning staff presented the Expanding Housing Choice initiative (Item 19), detailing infill zoning proposals and stormwater barriers to triplexes and quadplexes; Council Member Charlie Reece emphasized that Expanding Housing Choice targets market supply rather than mandated affordability, while Council Member DeDreana Freeman urged encouraging denser housing near light rail and bike trails. Council also reviewed corridor traffic/demographic forecasts and settled the agenda (Consent 1–16; GBA Public Hearing 20) by voice vote before adjourning at 4:02 PM.

agenda_items.title: Roll Call, Excused Absence, Staff Recognition, and Pulled Consent Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With Mayor Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Vernetta Alston, Javiera Caballero, and Charlie Reece present (and DeDreana Freeman delayed), Council unanimously excused Mark-Anthony Middleton's absence by voice vote and recognized departing analyst Mani-Sue Seemans. Council praised the GARE grant for expunctions and license restorations (Item 6) and pulled Item 9 (sewer evaluation contract, noting scarce MWBE engineering firms) and Item 10 (financial advisor selection, clarifying fiduciary independence from underwriters). Staff also discussed criteria for a street-paving prioritization budget tool.

agenda_items.title: Recreation Advisory Commission 2018 Annual Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Recreation Advisory Commission representatives (accompanied by members Frank White and March Clemons) delivered the commission's 2018 annual report. Presenters highlighted outreach presentations to local PACs and neighborhood groups, park accreditation efforts, and liaison coordination with DOST, Hillandale Golf, and BPAC.

agenda_items.title: Expanding Housing Choice Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City-County Planning staff presented draft Expanding Housing Choice infill proposals across the urban tier ahead of fall engagement and a targeted Winter/Spring 2019 review, explaining that stormwater ordinance thresholds drive up costs on triplexes and quadplexes compared to duplexes. Council Member Charlie Reece endorsed the proposal while stressing it adds housing supply rather than directly creating mandated affordable housing funded by the City's separate housing strategy. Council Member DeDreana Freeman urged also reviewing commercial-to-housing conversions and higher-density options near light rail and trails like the American Tobacco Trail.

agenda_items.title: Commission Ballots, Corridor Transportation Study, and Settling the Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The clerk read initial commission ballot counts exceeding four votes (including Tia Hall, Jessica Ligon-Bull, Cameron Smith, Elaine O'Neal, and Javonia Lewis for the Racial Equity Task Force). Staff then presented a corridor transportation study noting higher minority, Hispanic, poverty, and zero-car household rates on the Durham side, Triangle Regional Model growth projections, multi-use paths, and NCDOT funding alignment. Council settled Consent Items 1–16 and GBA Public Hearing Item 20 by voice vote before adjourning at 4:02 PM.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Aug 20, 2018
meetings.executive_summary: At its August 20, 2018 meeting, the Durham City Council recognized Freetown/Creole heritage, Neighbor Spotlight awardee Gina Chung, female judicial trailblazers for National Women's Equality Day, and members of the Durham Youth Commission, and unanimously approved the consent agenda 7-0 (including acquiring the Durham Beltline corridor, while pulling Item 18). Police Chief C.J. Davis presented the 2018 Second Quarter Crime Report showing a 13.5% overall drop in Part 1 index crime and a 28% drop in Q2 violent crime despite an increase in homicides. Council unanimously approved 7-0 three planning applications—1900 Ellendale Road II for 15 townhomes (re-voting the UDO ordinance after staff caught a misread motion), 5246 North Roxboro Street for up to 20,000 square feet of commercial space, and the Hillsborough/Cole Mill Road consolidated development with a 90-foot hotel and expanded gas station/car wash—and approved 7-0 the Durham Convention & Visitors Bureau contract for the 2019 Bull City 150 anniversary celebration after incorporating inclusive language requested by DeDreana Freeman.

agenda_items.title: Freetown Heritage, Neighbor Spotlight, Women's Equality Day Judicial Trailblazers, and Durham Youth Commission
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council recognized Freetown/Creole heritage, honored Gina Chung with the Neighbor Spotlight Award, spotlighted two Durham female judicial trailblazers for National Women's Equality Day, and welcomed incoming and returning high school members of the Durham Youth Commission. Shailia Arias was sworn in at 00:36:17.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Boards, RDU FAA Grant, Durham Beltline Acquisition, Building Inspections Online Payment)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Schewel read the consent agenda, including minutes, Carolina Theatre and Recreation Advisory appointments, an RDU Airport Authority FAA AIP grant, proposed acquisition of the Durham Beltline corridor (Item 8), and Building Inspections online payment software. DeDreana Freeman pulled Item 18 (DCVB Bull City 150 contract), and Council passed the remaining consent items 7-0.

agenda_items.title: 2018 Second Quarter Crime Report Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief C.J. Davis reported that Part 1 index crime fell 13.5% in the first half of 2018 compared to 2017, with violent crime down 28% in Q2 and double-digit decreases in rapes, robberies, aggravated assaults, larcenies, and auto thefts, though homicides increased. Resident Chris Tiffany also offered public comment before Council thanked the department.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change — 1900 Ellendale Road II
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Jacob Wiggins presented Pamela Porter's request on behalf of developer Jim Anthony to rezone 1.3 acres at 1900 Ellendale Road from RS-8 to RU-M(D) for up to 15 townhomes ($200,000-$250,000), following a 12-0 Planning Commission recommendation. Javiera Caballero and Mayor Schewel questioned why an off-site BPAC sidewalk suggestion to Dartmouth was declined (Mr. Anthony cited neighboring property owners), and Council passed the consistency statement and corrected RU-M(D) ordinance 7-0 after Wiggins flagged that Mayor Schewel initially read the Item 14 CN-D motion by mistake.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 7-0 (2 operative motions; UDO re-voted after misread)

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change — 5246 North Roxboro Street
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jacob Wiggins presented a request (engineer Jim Clark speaking for the owner) to replace a 1987 family care home restriction on 1.9 acres at 5246 North Roxboro Street with a new CN(D) development plan allowing up to 20,000 square feet of non-TIA commercial space and a transit stop. Planning Commission recommended approval 11-0, and Council passed both motions 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Items — 3578 Hillsborough Road & Cole Mill Road (Holmes Oil / Hotel)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jamie Sunyak presented Dan Jewell's (Holmes Oil) request covering 5.074 acres at Hillsborough and Cole Mill Roads to rezone 1.563 acres to CG(D) to expand an existing convenience store/gas station with a car wash and 4.141 acres to IL(D) for a 90-foot hotel creating 75-80 jobs, alongside a Future Land Use Map amendment and Christian Avenue connection. Charlie Reece questioned BPAC pedestrian access comments (Jewell cited DOT and utility-pole constraints), and Council passed all three motions 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item — Durham Convention & Visitors Bureau Contract for Bull City 150 Celebration
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pulled by DeDreana Freeman after an afternoon City Attorney memo update, Freeman thanked staff for adding language recognizing First Nations and people of color and questioned DCVB CEO Shelley Green on living wages for hourly event workers and marketing coordination with Parks and Recreation. Mayor Schewel praised the grassroots '150 organizations' approach kicking off at the holiday parade, and Council approved the contract 7-0.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: With all seven council members present, the August 9, 2018 City Council Work Session opened with City Manager Tom Bonfield briefing Council on a tragic officer-involved shooting the previous night and introducing new Emergency Communications Director Randy. Council unanimously accepted the manager's priority items (Items 6, 7, 17, and 18) and the City Attorney's closed-session request, and noted corrections to prior June 7 minutes clarifying that Council Member Mark-Anthony Middleton had opposed rather than supported Mayor Pro Tempore Jillian Johnson chairing the Racial Equity Commission. Expressing general reluctance to suspend work-session rules for transparency reasons, Council nonetheless voted unanimously to suspend the rules and accept Item 6 (the CHAMPS Cities Combating Hunger grant), and also acted during the session on Items 7 (free GoDurham bus rides for youth 18 and under and 19–21 GED students), 11, and 17 (three fire trucks). Following a truncated middle gap, Transportation staff reviewed the dockless bike-share pilot, emerging e-scooter regulations, vendor response requirements for resident complaints, and returning docked bike-share CMAQ funds in favor of more equitable dockless service before Council settled the agenda, recorded Recreation Advisory Commission ballot appointments for David Fellerath and Charles Hill, and entered closed session.

agenda_items.title: Roll Call, Officer-Involved Shooting Briefing, and Staff Introduction
agenda_items.discussion_summary: All seven council members answered roll call. At the Mayor's request, City Manager Tom Bonfield updated Council on a tragic officer-involved shooting from the prior night, noting an overnight press release and ongoing Police Department reporting protocols while facts are verified. The manager also introduced new Emergency Communications Director Randy, hired from Cumberland County.

agenda_items.title: Priority Items and Minutes Corrections (June 7 Racial Equity Record)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously accepted four City Manager priority items—adding Item 18 (Durham 150 contract with DCVB) and requesting rule suspensions to act on Item 6 (CHAMPS grant), Item 7 (free GoDurham transit for youth and GED students), and Item 17 (three fire trucks)—and unanimously approved a closed session under NCGS 143-318.11(a)(3). Members also requested corrections to May and June minutes, notably correcting June 7 minutes that erroneously claimed Mark-Anthony Middleton supported Jillian Johnson chairing the Racial Equity Commission.

agenda_items.title: CHAMPS Cities Combating Hunger Grant and Youth Free Transit (Items 6 & 7)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A council member stated she generally opposes suspending rules at work sessions due to public transparency concerns, but moved to suspend the rules for Item 6 because of grant cohort deadlines. Council voted unanimously to suspend the rules and accept the CHAMPS grant (crediting Peter Skillern of Reinvestment Partners). Council then introduced Item 7, expanding free GoDurham rides to youth 18 and under and 19–21 GED students, before the transcript truncated.

agenda_items.title: Shared Active Transportation Pilot Update: Dockless Bikes and E-Scooters
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resuming after a truncated gap, Transportation staff reviewed the dockless bike-share year (500 bikes each from three vendors), legal uncertainty in Raleigh and Charlotte over motorized scooters versus mopeds, sidewalk riding prohibitions, and proposed permit updates adding e-bikes/e-scooters, seven-day idle-bike dashboards, and direct vendor responsiveness to resident complaints. Staff recommended returning federal CMAQ funds for a docked bike-share program because dockless bike-share proved far more geographically equitable across Durham.

agenda_items.title: Settling the Agenda, Commission Ballots, and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council settled the upcoming agenda (Consent 1, 2, 4, 5, 8–10, 18; GBA 12; GBA Public Hearings 13–16; Disposed 6, 7, 11, 17; Referred back 3) by voice vote. The clerk announced ballot appointments of David Fellerath ('Felleroff') and Charles Hill to the Recreation Advisory Commission. Council then voted unanimously by voice to enter closed session.

votes.notes: All seven council members present.
votes.discussion_detail: Accepted manager's priority items covering Durham 150 and urgent rule-suspension requests for Items 6, 7, and 17.

votes.notes: All seven council members present.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved entering closed session at the end of the meeting for attorney-client communication pursuant to NCGS 143-318.11(a)(3).

votes.notes: All seven council members present.
votes.discussion_detail: Suspended work-session rules to accept the CHAMPS grant immediately despite general transparency reservations noted by the mover.

votes.item_title: Item 6: Accept CHAMPS Cities Combating Hunger Grant Project Ordinance
votes.notes: All seven council members present; Items 7, 11, and 17 were also listed as disposed at 01:29:25 during the truncated middle portion.

votes.notes: All seven council members present.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Aug 6, 2018
meetings.executive_summary: In a nearly five-hour meeting on August 6, 2018, the Durham City Council passed the consent agenda 7-0 (including the CEDAW resolution) and unanimously approved the 15-member Participatory Budgeting Steering Committee and an Audit Services Oversight Committee appointment 7-0. In a major 2-5 split vote on Item 23, Council rejected $20 million in tax-exempt conduit bonds for Excelsior Classical Academy—with Mark-Anthony Middleton and DeDreana Freeman voting Aye and Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, Javiera Caballero, and Vernetta Alston voting Nay—over charter school funding impacts on Durham Public Schools and TeamCFA governance ties. Council approved 5123 Chin Page Road (Item 24), Garrett Road consolidated annexation (Item 33), and pulled bike/Beltline agreements (Items 10 and 12) 7-0, while passing the Boone Street closing (Item 25), K Street closing (Item 26), and both motions for the Rolling Dale rezoning (Item 27, despite troubling conflict-of-interest concerns) 6-1 with DeDreana Freeman dissenting on each. Finally, Council adopted the Durham Beltline Trail Master Plan (Item 28) while directing staff to return in 90 days with an engagement roadmap for a racial equity plan by a 6-1 vote, with Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, DeDreana Freeman, Mark-Anthony Middleton, and Vernetta Alston voting Aye and Javiera Caballero voting Nay in favor of an immediate pause.

agenda_items.title: Breastfeeding & CEDAW Resolutions, City Ranking, Consent Agenda, and Committee Appointments (Items 2 & 5)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council presented a Breastfeeding Coalition proclamation, Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson read the CEDAW resolution supporting women's human rights, and Council celebrated Durham ranking seventh among 150 cities nationally. Council approved the consent agenda 7-0 (pulling Items 10 and 12), approved the 15-member Participatory Budgeting Steering Committee slate 7-0 (after holding slots for DeDreana Freeman and Mark-Anthony Middleton), and approved an Audit Services Oversight Committee appointment 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — $20M Education Revenue Bonds for Excelsior Classical Academy (Public Finance Authority)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Finance Director David Boyd and bond counsel Mary Nash Rusher presented a TEFRA hearing for up to $20 million in tax-exempt conduit bonds via Wisconsin's Public Finance Authority (chosen for a 40-year maturity) with no city financial liability. Five council members (Charlie Reece, Vernetta Alston, Jillian Johnson, Javiera Caballero, and Steve Schewel) opposed lending the City's tax-exempt financing stamp to a charter school affiliated with TeamCFA and diverting students/funding from Durham Public Schools, while Mark-Anthony Middleton and DeDreana Freeman argued denying tax-exempt refinancing harmed current Durham students; the resolution failed 2-5.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Failed 2-5 (Middleton & Freeman Aye; Schewel, Johnson, Reece, Caballero, Alston Nay)

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change — 5123 Chin Page Road
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jacob Wiggins presented Charlie Yokley's request to rezone one acre at 5123 Chin Page Road from Rural Residential (RR) to Industrial Light (IL) without a development plan to match adjacent properties, following an 11-0 Planning Commission recommendation. DeDreana Freeman questioned tree preservation and the trend of speculative rezonings without development plans before Council passed both motions 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — Boone Street Closing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jamie Sunyak presented Mark and Madison Marvelli's request to permanently close 296 linear feet of unbuilt Boone Street right-of-way between Latta/Lassiter and Dixon Streets containing an existing concrete driveway encroachment. Jillian Johnson and DeDreana Freeman questioned how unpermitted surface and underground encroachments occur in public rights-of-way, and Council passed the closure order 6-1 with Freeman voting Nay.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — K Street Closing (Duke University Adjacent)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jacob Wiggins presented Ronald Carpenter's request to close 766.81 linear feet of K Street surrounded by Duke University parcels while retaining a sanitary sewer easement. DeDreana Freeman questioned sewer line access enforcement, and Mayor Schewel criticized Duke for leaving the adjacent former city soccer field vacant for a decade while still backing the closure; moved by Mark-Anthony Middleton, the order passed 6-1 with Freeman voting Nay (announced by the clerk as '6-0 with Council Member Freeman voting no').

agenda_items.title: Resumed Public Hearing — Rolling Dale Zoning Map Change (602 & 606 West NC 54)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resuming a continued public hearing on a 6.65-acre rezoning from RS-20 to PDR 3.94 for 25 townhomes with added 40-foot tree conservation, 70-foot southern setback, and double silt fencing, Council heard the City Attorney report that Durham County's Attorney found no county ethics violation when a Planning Commissioner who voted on the case later represented the applicant. While Mayor Schewel, Charlie Reece, and Vernetta Alston expressed concern that the process appeared tainted, six members judged the proffered buffers superior to by-right development; DeDreana Freeman dissented on both votes (6-1), arguing PDR rezoning is discretionary and threatens waterways.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — Durham Beltline Trail Master Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dale McKeel and Transportation Director Terry Bellamy presented the TIGER-funded Durham Beltline Trail Master Plan after extensive public comment on displacement and equity. Council debated community calls to pause adoption until an equity plan was completed: six members supported adopting the conceptual plan while directing staff to return in 90 days with a community engagement roadmap for a racial equity plan (with Mark-Anthony Middleton clarifying an engagement plan vs. year-long task force work and DeDreana Freeman emphasizing jobs planning), whereas Javiera Caballero voted Nay to honor DOST advocates' call for a pause.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation — Garrett Road
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jamie Sunyak presented the Garrett Road consolidated annexation and rezoning (including a $2,500 proffer to Durham Public Schools and an 11-0 Planning Commission recommendation). Council discussed traffic signal and sidewalk needs along Garrett Road before approving all three motions 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Items — Neighborhood Bicycle Routes Design (C-5605I) and Durham Beltline Supplemental Agreement (EB-5504)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council approved Item 10 (neighborhood bicycle routes design contract, pulled by Adela Ortiz) 7-0. On Item 12 (Durham Beltline supplemental municipal agreement), speakers including Ms. Ortiz urged ensuring 'super-excluded' residents are included and protected from displacement before Council approved the agreement 7-0.

votes.item_title: Consent Agenda (Items 1, 6-9, 11, 14-21, excluding pulled Items 10 and 12)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously approved the consent agenda including the CEDAW resolution and DHA pre-development grant, excluding pulled Items 10 and 12.

votes.item_title: Item 2: Participatory Budgeting Steering Committee Appointments (15 Members)
votes.discussion_detail: After holding votes open for Freeman and Middleton to participate, Council unanimously approved the 15-member slate (five from each ward).

votes.item_title: Item 5: Audit Services Oversight Committee Appointment
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously approved the Audit Services Oversight Committee appointment 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 23: Resolution Approving Public Finance Authority Education Revenue Bonds (Excelsior Classical Academy, up to $20M)
votes.notes: Clerk announced 'fails by a vote of 5 to 2 with Council Member Middleton and Council Member Freeman voting in the affirmative.'
votes.discussion_detail: Following an intense 50-minute policy debate on charter schools, DPS per-pupil funding, and TeamCFA, the bond resolution failed 2-5 with Mark-Anthony Middleton and DeDreana Freeman voting Aye and the remaining five members voting Nay.

votes.item_title: Item 24: Consistency Statement for 5123 Chin Page Road
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the consistency statement for 5123 Chin Page Road.

votes.item_title: Item 24: Ordinance Amending the UDO for 5123 Chin Page Road (RR to IL)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously rezoned one acre at 5123 Chin Page Road from Rural Residential to Industrial Light.

votes.item_title: Item 25: Order Permanently Closing a 296-Linear-Foot Portion of Boone Street
votes.discussion_detail: After questions about unpermitted right-of-way driveway encroachments and enforcement, Council passed the Boone Street closure order 6-1 with DeDreana Freeman voting Nay.

votes.item_title: Item 26: Order Permanently Closing a 766.81-Linear-Foot Portion of K Street
votes.notes: Clerk misspoke '6-0 with Council Member Freeman voting no' while all 7 members were present and voting (6 Ayes, 1 Nay).
votes.discussion_detail: Moved by Mark-Anthony Middleton following questions on sewer easement enforcement and Duke University's adjacent unused field, the K Street closing order passed with DeDreana Freeman voting Nay.

votes.item_title: Item 27: Consistency Statement for Rolling Dale (602 & 606 W. NC 54)
votes.discussion_detail: Council adopted the consistency statement for Rolling Dale 6-1 with DeDreana Freeman voting Nay.

votes.item_title: Item 27: Ordinance Amending the UDO for Rolling Dale (RS-20 to PDR 3.94)
votes.discussion_detail: Council approved rezoning 6.65 acres at 602 and 606 W. NC 54 to PDR 3.94 for up to 25 townhomes 6-1 with DeDreana Freeman voting Nay.

votes.discussion_detail: Following debate over pausing the master plan for racial equity planning, Council passed the master plan paired with a 90-day staff directive for a community engagement roadmap toward a racial equity plan, with Javiera Caballero voting Nay.

votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the consistency statement for Garrett Road.

votes.item_title: Item 10: Contract for Neighborhood Bicycle Routes Design (TIP C-5605I)
votes.discussion_detail: Following comments from speaker Adela Ortiz, Council unanimously approved the neighborhood bicycle routes design contract 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 12: Durham Beltline Supplemental Municipal Agreement (EB-5504)
votes.discussion_detail: Following community appeals to center historically excluded residents in Beltline planning, Council unanimously approved the supplemental municipal agreement 7-0.

disagreements.issue: Tax-Exempt Conduit Bond Approval for Excelsior Classical Academy Charter School (Item 23)
disagreements.summary: Council split 2-5 on approving a TEFRA resolution enabling Excelsior Classical Academy to issue up to $20 million in tax-exempt conduit bonds via Wisconsin's Public Finance Authority.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the conduit bond resolution because the City bears no financial liability and denying tax-exempt refinancing penalizes Durham students already attending the school.
side_a_arguments: The school already holds a state charter and owns the building on an interim loan; denying tax-exempt bonds will not prevent expansion and only forces taxable debt that pulls operating funds away from students.
Municipal TEFRA hearings should not be used as a philosophical foil against charter schools when the City contributes zero public dollars and has no jurisdiction over education policy.
Withholding financing leaves the school more financially vulnerable to outside management lender TeamCFA.
disagreements.side_b_position: Deny the conduit bond resolution because the City should exercise its discretion not to lend a municipal financing tool to charter school expansion.
side_b_arguments: Charter school expansion diverts per-pupil tax dollars and families away from Durham Public Schools, which serve the majority of low-income and Black and brown students.
Excelsior has ongoing financial ties (forgivable loans and a voting board seat) to TeamCFA, whose state takeover politics threaten local public schools.
The school has alternative taxable or governmental financing options without Durham City Council's official stamp of approval.
disagreements.resolution: Motion failed 2-5 at 01:16:26.

disagreements.issue: Boone Street and K Street Right-of-Way Closings and Encroachment Enforcement (Items 25 & 26)
disagreements.summary: Council voted 6-1 on both street closing orders (Boone Street and K Street), with DeDreana Freeman dissenting over right-of-way encroachment enforcement and utility/drainage oversight.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the permanent street closures because both met UDO standards, raised no agency objections, and retained required sewer easements.
side_a_arguments: Boone Street was an unbuilt paper street where closing legally remedies an existing driveway encroachment.
On K Street, the City retains a full sanitary sewer easement ensuring maintenance access even though Duke University's adjacent field has sat vacant.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose closing the public rights-of-way due to weak proactive enforcement against surface and underground encroachments.
side_b_arguments: Allowing unpermitted driveways and drainage/underground encroachments to be cured only retroactively via street closures reflects inadequate right-of-way patrol and enforcement.
disagreements.resolution: Both Boone Street and K Street closure orders passed 6-1.

disagreements.issue: Rolling Dale Zoning Map Change (RS-20 to PDR 3.94) and Process Ethics Concerns (Item 27)
disagreements.summary: Following a County Attorney review finding no formal ethics violation when a Planning Commissioner who voted on Rolling Dale later represented the developer, Council split 6-1 in approving the rezoning.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve PDR 3.94 rezoning on its merits despite process concerns because proffered tree buffers, setbacks, and double silt fencing protect neighbors better than by-right single-family development.
side_a_arguments: The County Attorney confirmed no county ethics violation occurred and Council could decide impartially on the merits.
Proffered 40-foot southern tree conservation, 70-foot setbacks, 34% impervious cap, and double silt fencing offer stronger protections than by-right RS-20 single-family construction.
disagreements.side_b_position: Deny the rezoning to PDR 3.94 and keep existing RS-20 zoning to protect waterways and neighborhood stability.
side_b_arguments: Moving from RS-20 to PDR 3.94 is a discretionary legislative action, not a by-right entitlement.
Higher density and grading pose avoidable stormwater and waterway risks to the surrounding community.
disagreements.resolution: Both the consistency statement and zoning ordinance passed 6-1.

disagreements.issue: Durham Beltline Trail Master Plan — Immediate Adoption with 90-Day Engagement Directive vs. Pause for Equity Planning (Item 28)
disagreements.summary: Council voted 6-1 to adopt the conceptual Durham Beltline Trail Master Plan while directing staff to return in 90 days with an engagement process for a racial equity plan, with Javiera Caballero voting Nay in favor of pausing adoption.
disagreements.side_a_position: Adopt the conceptual master plan now while directing staff to return within 90 days with a community engagement roadmap to build a racial equity plan before design/construction.
side_a_arguments: Construction is 1.5 to 2 years away, leaving ample time to co-create an equity plan covering affordable housing, local hiring, and corridor engagement before asphalt is laid.

Gentrification is already accelerating citywide regardless of the trail; adopting the master plan preserves federal TIGER/transportation momentum while committing Council to anti-displacement measures.
disagreements.side_b_position: Pause approval of the master plan in deference to community and DOST advocates calling for equity planning first.
side_b_arguments: As a former Durham Open Space and Trails (DOST) commissioner and trail advocate, felt compelled to honor residents and DOST members requesting an explicit pause before adoption.
disagreements.resolution: Motion passed 6-1 at 04:31:15.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Returning from summer recess on July 26, 2018, Mayor Steve Schewel presided over the City Council Work Session with five members present (Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Vernetta Alston, Javiera Caballero, and Charlie Reece) and unanimously excused DeDreana Freeman and Mark-Anthony Middleton, who were traveling. Council introduced new Deputy Clerk Ashley Wyatt, heard Mayor Schewel's tribute to a deceased community leader and report on a Bloomberg Foundation/Harvard mayors' training, and unanimously accepted City Manager priority items for the Algal Flowway presentation (Item 18), Durham Beltline Trail Master Plan public hearing (Item 28), and Garrett Road annexation (Item 33). Members also discussed board diversity and re-advertising vacancies on the Board of Adjustment, Participatory Budgeting Steering Committee, and Homeless Services Advisory Committee, and requested Excelsior Classical Academy representatives attend Monday's bond hearing (Item 23). Following a truncated middle segment, Transportation staff presented the 2017–18 Downtown Parking Study recommending shared parking, smart meters, curbside management, satellite shuttles, and updated parking maximums instead of building a new deck, and Council settled the agenda and reported ballot votes appointing Ian Kipp to the Board of Adjustment (4 votes) and Regina D. King to the Homeless Services Advisory Committee (5 votes) before adjourning at 3:56 PM.

agenda_items.title: Roll Call, Excused Absences, Announcements, and Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With five members present, Council unanimously approved excused absences for DeDreana Freeman and Mark-Anthony Middleton. The City Clerk introduced new Deputy Clerk Ashley Wyatt, and Mayor Schewel mourned the passing of a close friend and Durham Tech Community Foundation colleague (transcribed in ASR as 'Fail win') and reported on a Bloomberg Foundation/Harvard training for 40 mayors. Council unanimously accepted City Manager priority items for Items 18, 28, and Supplemental Item 33.

agenda_items.title: Board Appointments and Agenda Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed board vacancies, agreeing to appoint one Board of Adjustment member while re-advertising two seats, noting a lack of consensus to re-advertise the Participatory Budgeting Steering Committee disability seat, and placing an appointment on GBA for Germaine Brewington's input due to gender diversity concerns. Members pulled Items 9 (DHA downtown planning grant) and 18 (Algal Flowway), thanked staff for the Miracle League utility extension (Item 20), and asked Finance to have Excelsior Classical Academy representatives attend Monday's Item 23 revenue bond hearing.

agenda_items.title: 2017–18 Downtown Parking Study Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resuming after a truncated middle segment, Transportation staff presented the 2017–18 Downtown Parking Study amid more than 80,000 square feet of retail/restaurant and one million square feet of office construction. Recommendations included standardized signage, smart meters and pay-by-phone upgrades, curbside and EV management, bringing parking operations in-house, shared church and private-deck agreements, satellite shuttle parking, public-private partnerships, and revising maximum parking code rules. Mayor Schewel and council members welcomed optimizing existing capacity rather than building another parking garage.

agenda_items.title: Settling the Agenda and Commission Ballot Results
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously settled the agenda with Consent Items 1, 6–12, and 14–21, GBA Items 2 and 5, and GBA Public Hearing Items 23–28 and 33. The clerk announced ballot selections of Ian Kipp as regular member of the Board of Adjustment (4 votes) and Regina D. King to the Homeless Services Advisory Committee (5 votes), while Participatory Budgeting Steering Committee ballots yielded eight candidates with 4 votes and six with 3 votes (carried to GBA). After noting Phil's funeral time on Monday, Mayor Schewel adjourned at 3:56 PM.

meetings.title: Durham City Council June 18, 2018
meetings.executive_summary: With Council Member Javiera Caballero excused absent, the six present Durham City Council members approved the consent agenda 6-0 (including the FY 2018-19 budget, CIP, and fire consolidation with Bethesda and Parkwood) and later passed pulled Item 16 establishing the Racial Equity Task Force 6-0. On Item 31, Council voted 4-2 to remove loose tire mulch at East Durham Park using $20,000 from the General Fund balance rather than delaying Piney Wood soccer field repairs, with Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, DeDreana Freeman, and Vernetta Alston voting Aye and Mark-Anthony Middleton and Steve Schewel voting Nay. Council approved street closings for Sycamore Street (Item 44) and Bush Drive (Item 52) by identical 5-1 votes—Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, Mark-Anthony Middleton, and Vernetta Alston in favor, and DeDreana Freeman opposed—while approving Drake Avenue and Sarvis Street closings (Item 51), FY 2018-19 capital facility fees (Item 46), and annexations for 3112 Blue Hill Lane (Item 42) and J.C. Electric (Item 43) unanimously 6-0. Council also kept the public hearing open and continued the Rolling Dale rezoning (Item 45) to August 2018 to obtain a City Attorney ethics review regarding a Planning Commissioner representing the applicant.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, Excused Absence, Neighbor Spotlight, and History Lesson
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m., and Council voted 6-0 to grant an excused absence to Council Member Javiera Caballero, who was traveling. Ceremonial items included presenting the Neighbor Spotlight Award to Estella Bell, recognizing the Duke University baseball coaching and support staff, and hearing a local history presentation from public historian Eddie on the 1933 Durham Post Office and Federal Courthouse and the Epps v. Carmichael desegregation case.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 1–39, Excluding Item 16, Item 31, and Public Hearings)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Schewel read the consent agenda, noting Item 11 (Housing Appeals Board at-large alternate vacancy) was referred back to the City Clerk's office and Item 16 (Racial Equity Task Force) was pulled by a resident for separate consideration. Major items approved on consent included the FY 2018-19 budget, FY 2019-24 Capital Improvement Plan, Council Code of Ethics amendment, sidewalk and utility infrastructure contracts, Durham City-County fire consolidation, and future police headquarters site disposition. Council approved the remaining consent slate 6-0.

agenda_items.title: East Durham Park Tire Mulch Report and Funding Source
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Community speakers Lenora Smith and Kristen Henry thanked Council for addressing East Durham Park's tire mulch but criticized Durham Parks and Recreation (DPR) for recommending removal of only the loose tire mulch without consulting residents about remaining bonded tire mulch, urging a systemwide moratorium on recycled tire products. DPR Assistant Director Tom Dawson explained why staff recommended delaying Piney Wood soccer field repairs (a playability rather than safety issue) to pay for removal, which Mark-Anthony Middleton and Steve Schewel supported to protect the General Fund balance. A majority of Council instead backed appropriating $20,000 from fund balance to avoid pitting neighborhoods against one another, passing the motion 4-2.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation for 3112 Blue Hill Lane
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented a voluntary annexation and utility extension request for 3112 Blue Hill Lane to allow construction of a city-maintained public street connecting a residential development along Enders Chapel Road to the satellite-annexed Yancy parcel. Applicant representative Charlie Yokley of the McAdams Company attended to answer questions, with no opposition speakers. Council approved the annexation, consistency statement, and initial residential rural zoning in three consecutive 6-0 votes.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation for J.C. Electric Initial (4915 Hillsborough Road)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented a voluntary annexation, utility extension agreement, and initial Industrial Light (IL) zoning request for a 9.9-acre parcel split between Orange and Durham counties under an interlocal annexation agreement with Orange County, intended for an outdoor recreation facility requiring a Board of Adjustment minor special use permit. Council Member Charlie Reece expressed strong frustration with cross-county annexations and assigning IL zoning adjacent to a residential neighborhood, though he voted in favor because of a state-imposed stream buffer. Council approved all three motions 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Sycamore Street Permanent Street Closing (TROSA)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented a request by Kimley-Horn on behalf of TROSA to permanently close 465.60 linear feet of an unbuilt, unmaintained paper street segment of Sycamore Street surrounded entirely by TROSA-owned parcels. Proponent representatives Ed Hallberg and Dan Jewell noted the closure is a first step toward future site planning, and opponent Freeman Ledbetter departed after staff addressed his questions before the hearing. Council approved the street closing order 5-1, with DeDreana Freeman voting against.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change for Rolling Dale (602 and 606 West NC Highway 54)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented a rezoning request from RS-20 to Planned Development Residential 3.940 for up to 25 townhomes on 6.65 acres, which Planning Commission had recommended approving 9-5. Following extensive public comment and Council questioning over tree buffers and the appearance of conflict from Planning Commissioner Neel Ghosh now representing the developer, Council Members DeDreana Freeman, Charlie Reece, and Mark-Anthony Middleton debated ethics rules and public perception. Per City Attorney guidance that no vote was required, Mayor Schewel kept the public hearing open and continued the item to August 2018 for an ethics review and further developer-neighborhood talks on tree preservation.

agenda_items.title: Ordinance Revising Capital Facility Fees for FY 2018-19
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Don Greeley of the Department of Water Management presented the annual revision to water and sewer capital facility fees (system development fees) prepared with consultant Raftelis to conform to North Carolina General Statutes Chapter 162A Article 8 by the July 1, 2018 statutory deadline. No members of the public spoke during the newly mandated public hearing. Council adopted the fee ordinance 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Drake Avenue and Sarvis Street Permanent Street Closings
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented a request associated with Hillandale Partners LLC and adjoining residential property owners to permanently close 157 linear feet of Drake Avenue and 143 linear feet of Sarvis Street (unbuilt paper streets west of Tampa Avenue traversed by a perennial tributary of Ellerbe Creek). Watts Hospital-Hillandale Neighborhood Association representatives Jamie Greener and Tom Miller urged approval to protect the stream topography and coordinate adjacent development off Hillandale Road. Council adopted the permanent closing order 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Bush Drive Permanent Street Closing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented a request by Edens Land to permanently close 874 linear feet of unbuilt public right-of-way on Bush Drive as required by a zoning text commitment (Z170014) and site plan condition. Council Member DeDreana Freeman questioned the high number of street closings on the agenda and noted there were several at one meeting. Council passed the closing order 5-1, with DeDreana Freeman voting Nay.

agenda_items.title: Establishment of the City of Durham Racial Equity Task Force (Pulled from Consent)

disagreements.issue: East Durham Park Tire Mulch Removal Funding Source (General Fund Balance vs. Delaying Piney Wood Soccer Field Repairs)
disagreements.summary: Council split 4-2 over whether to pay $20,000 to remove loose tire mulch at East Durham Park by drawing from the General Fund balance or by following staff's recommendation to delay planned half-penny Parks & Trails repairs to the Piney Wood soccer field for one year.
disagreements.side_a_position: Appropriate $20,000 from General Fund balance so East Durham Park is remediated without delaying Piney Wood or pitting neighborhoods against each other
side_a_arguments: Residents urged not pitting East Durham against another neighborhood's park project
Vernetta Alston noted initial reservations about tapping fund balance but voted Yes to support Council majority for the $20,000 appropriation
disagreements.side_b_position: Follow staff recommendation to delay the Piney Wood soccer field repair by one year instead of tapping General Fund balance
side_b_arguments: Mark-Anthony Middleton argued Piney Wood was a playability/rentability issue rather than a safety hazard and would not be denied, only delayed 12 months
Middleton compared the General Fund balance to a household savings account that should not be raided for a $20,000 project to demonstrate fiscal discipline to taxpayers
disagreements.resolution: Motion to fund loose tire mulch removal via a $20,000 General Fund balance appropriation passed 4-2.

disagreements.issue: Sycamore Street and Bush Drive Permanent Street Closings
disagreements.summary: DeDreana Freeman dissented 5-1 on two permanent street-closing orders (Item 44 Sycamore Street and Item 52 Bush Drive), questioning the high volume of public right-of-way closures coming before Council.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve permanent street-closing orders for unbuilt paper rights-of-way consistent with staff recommendations and prior zoning commitments
side_a_arguments: Both rights-of-way were unbuilt and unmaintained by the city
Staff confirmed Bush Drive closure was required by prior zoning case Z170014 and Sycamore Street was surrounded by TROSA parcels with no agency objections
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose permanent right-of-way closures amid high volume of street closings
side_b_arguments: DeDreana Freeman questioned the unusually large number of street closings appearing on the agenda and voted against closing Sycamore Street and Bush Drive
disagreements.resolution: Both street-closing orders passed 5-1.

disagreements.issue: Rolling Dale Rezoning Ethics Question and Tree Buffer Continuance
disagreements.summary: Council debated whether Planning Commissioner Neel Ghosh representing the Rolling Dale developer after previously participating at the Planning Commission posed a conflict of interest or public perception concern, and how to balance fairness to the attorney with ethics clarity.
disagreements.side_a_position: Continue the public hearing to August 2018 so the City Attorney can review the Code of Ethics facts and the developer can work with neighbors on tree preservation
side_a_arguments: Charlie Reece stated that while he did not believe Mr. Ghosh had improper intent, public perception suffers when a Planning Commissioner later represents an applicant before Council
DeDreana Freeman suggested continuing the item and Steve Schewel proposed keeping the public hearing open until August so clear ethics guidance could be obtained
disagreements.side_b_position: Ensure fairness to Mr. Ghosh by clarifying whether any rule actually barred his appearance rather than leaving innuendo
side_b_arguments: Mark-Anthony Middleton pressed the City Attorney for a definitive statement on whether anything was improper and noted uncertainty over whether existing rules even covered the situation
disagreements.resolution: Without objection, Mayor Schewel kept the public hearing open and continued Item 45 to August 2018 for City Attorney ethics review and further developer-neighborhood talks.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the June 7, 2018 City Council Work Session (presided over by Mayor Steve Schewel with all seven council members present), Council unanimously approved the City Manager's priority items (7-0)—referring a Chatham County fire-response interlocal agreement back to administration and adding four supplemental items, including a performance-evaluation software contract and street closings—and the City Clerk's priority item (7-0) adding the April 16, 2018 draft minutes to the June 18 agenda. Members reviewed and pulled multiple items from the FY 2018-19 budget, Capital Improvement Plan, and departmental agenda, noting new planning fee schedules supporting nine positions and high per-mile sidewalk construction costs ($1.3 million per mile on NC-751/NC-54). During Citizens Matters, speakers advocated on the proposed Durham Beltline ($2.39 million in the proposed budget), and following a truncated middle portion of the transcript, staff presented updates on Bloomberg Mayor's Challenge / Innovation Team prototypes—including a 'Welcome Home' prototype and a $250,000 court-based Expunction and Restoration office targeting 10,000+ residents with suspended licenses. Council concluded by reviewing board and commission ballot appointments (noting a split ballot tally on the Cultural Advisory Board where Valerie Gillespie passed with four votes and an unnamed member switched a vote to Candace Smith) and unanimously settling the agenda before adjourning at 4:42 PM.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Priority Items (City Manager and City Clerk)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel called the work session to order with all seven council members present. City Manager Tom Bonfield apologized for frequent agenda updates and outlined priority items: an example fee schedule for nine new planning positions under Item 13 (FY 2018-19 Budget and FY 2019-24 CIP), referral of Item 27 (Chatham County fire-response interlocal agreement) back to administration, and supplemental Items 50-53 (citizens matter, Drake Avenue/Sovereign Street and Bush Street closings, and employee performance evaluation software). Council approved both the Manager's priority items and the Clerk's request to schedule April 16, 2018 draft minutes for June 18 approval, followed by a farewell recognition of retiring staff member Terry Capers.

agenda_items.title: Review of Departmental, Presentation, Public Hearing, and Supplemental Agenda Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members read through the agenda and flagged items for discussion or clarification, holding Items 14, 15, 16, 18, 23, 24, 26, 28, 29, 30, and 31. On Item 13 (FY 2018-19 Budget and CIP), a member requested an email before Monday explaining why certain ordinances were attached, while on Item 19 (NCDOT U-4726HJ NC-751/NC-54 sidewalk project) and Guess Road, members noted sidewalk construction costs of $1.3 million and $1.0 million per mile respectively. Members also flagged Item 15 (City Council Code of Ethics amendments), Item 16 (Racial Equity Task Force), Item 18 (mortgage loan servicing contract), and Item 37/minority business capacity challenges.

agenda_items.title: Citizens Matters: Proposed Durham Beltline
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Savannah Colbreath and a colleague addressed Council during Citizens Matters at 1:00 PM regarding the proposed Durham Beltline project. They noted that $2.39 million is allotted to the project in the upcoming fiscal year budget and began presenting community requests prior to construction before the transcript digest truncated.

agenda_items.title: Bloomberg Mayor's Challenge / Innovation Team Prototypes (Expunction, Driver's License Restoration & Welcome Home)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resuming after a truncated gap, Innovation Team staff presented on the 'Welcome Home' and 'Expunction and Restoration' prototypes slated to launch by late July/August using the City's existing $400,000 grant match without requesting new funds. The proposed expunction and driver's license restoration office—staffed by two full-time attorneys, a legal assistant, and a community outreach coordinator (preferably formerly justice-involved individuals)—would operate partly in the courthouse via a judicial referral system championed by Judge Amanda Maris, alongside regional coordination with Wake and Orange County district attorneys after AOC data showed over 10,000 Durham residents with suspended/revoked licenses and 45% carrying charges in surrounding counties. Staff estimated the prototype cost at $250,000 and planned to pursue Durham County and partner support while circulating a detailed memo.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments and Agenda Settlement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Clerk read ballot results for Citizens Advisory Committee (PAC1-PAC4), Housing Appeals Board (Maria Perry and Elizabeth Wiener, plus re-advertising an at-large seat), and Human Relations Commission appointments (Jeffrey King, Brian Kennedy II, Brandon Washington, Andrea Hudson, D.A. Porter, and Natalie Santos). On the Cultural Advisory Board, Valerie Gillespie passed with four votes while Marcus Hawley (1), Bernetta Rivers (2), Vivian Slade (1), and Jamie Tyndall (1) split remaining ballots, leading an unnamed council member to switch a second vote from Bernetta Rivers to Candace Smith. Council then unanimously settled the consent and public hearing agenda for the upcoming regular meeting and adjourned at 4:42 PM.
