meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the January 4, 2018 City Council Work Session presided over by Mayor Steve Schewel, the six seated Council members (with the At-Large seat vacated by Schewel's election as Mayor still open prior to Javiera Caballero's later appointment) unanimously approved the City Manager's priority items referring a transit amenities contract back to staff and scheduling a street-repaving presentation. Council reviewed affordable housing and land trust funding items—noting permanent affordability tradeoffs—alongside HR's 2018–2021 Aetna Whole Health employee benefit savings and Public Works' $6.6 million FY18 pavement preservation program shifting from worst-first paving to a PCI-65 lifecycle approach, where members raised equity concerns about public perception in historically neglected neighborhoods. After a truncated middle section, Council engaged in an extended procedural debate over how to vote on the vacant At-Large Council seat: Mayor Pro Tempore Jillian Johnson demonstrated ranked-choice voting while Charlie Reece questioned electing a finalist with three votes and Mark-Anthony Middleton favored live deliberation between rounds under a traditional majority-vote ballot. Following an unresolved ranked-choice motion, the six seated members voted 4-2 by unattributed voice vote to adopt the majority-vote ballot system over ranked-choice voting (the transcript did not record a roll call naming which four of Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, DeDreana Freeman, Mark-Anthony Middleton, and Vernetta Alston voted Aye and which two voted Nay).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Vacancy Applicant Residency Inquiry, and Manager's Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel called the work session to order with the six seated members (Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, DeDreana Freeman, Mark-Anthony Middleton, and Vernetta Alston; one At-Large seat vacant). A member requested the City Clerk verify whether At-Large Council vacancy applicant Andrea Small lived within city limits before members finalized shortlists. Council then unanimously approved the City Manager's priority items to refer Item 6 (transit amenities repair and installation contract) back to staff and hear a presentation on Item 10 (Contract ST-285 street repairs and repaving).
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed (Unanimous voice vote on Manager's priority items)

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Affordable Housing / Land Trust Cost Tradeoffs
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff read agenda items including HR's 2018–2021 employee benefits recommendations (Item 7), a Police Department HIDTA grant amendment (Item 8), ESRI software maintenance (Item 11), and a public hearing item (Item 12). During review of Items 3 and 4, one member noted the high cost of the projects while another highlighted that community land trust units remain permanently affordable rather than expiring after 15, 20, or 30 years, which alters cost comparisons.

agenda_items.title: 2018–2021 Employee Benefits Recommendations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Human Resources staff briefed Council on recommended 2018–2021 health plan changes transitioning employees from existing basic and core plans to Aetna Whole Health options. Staff reported that every participating employee switching to the new plans would save on premiums, deductibles, and out-of-pocket costs—averaging roughly $57 per month, and saving up to $250 per pay period for families moving from the core plan to the low option.

agenda_items.title: Contract ST-285: 2018 Street Repairs, Repaving, and Pavement Preservation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Works staff presented Durham's transition from a 'worst-first' paving strategy to a scientific pavement preservation approach aimed at maintaining residential streets at a Pavement Condition Index (PCI) of 65 using $6.6 million in FY18 funds (up from $3 million in FY17) plus prior-contract contingency funds. Members asked how soon cost savings would reach the worst roads, cautioned that residents in historically under-maintained neighborhoods could perceive treating moderate roads first as a new excuse for delay, requested advance street lists for PAC-1 communication, and asked about pothole response prioritization and prior work in Stone Hill Estates before the transcript truncated.

agenda_items.title: City Council Vacancy Selection Procedure: Ranked-Choice vs. Majority-Vote Ballot
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resuming after a truncated middle section, the six seated Council members debated two methods for selecting an appointee from seven finalists to fill the vacant At-Large Council seat. Mayor Pro Tempore Jillian Johnson walked through ranked-choice voting mechanics and argued it offered a fairer model that could help educate the public, while Charlie Reece voiced concern about potentially appointing someone with only three votes, and Mark-Anthony Middleton and others argued ranked-choice would confuse the public, depart from Council precedent, and eliminate substantive live debate between rounds. After an earlier ranked-choice motion was interrupted by prolonged debate, a member stated they would vote for majority vote to avoid further delay, and Council passed the majority-vote ballot process 4-2 by unattributed voice vote prior to adjournment.

votes.item_title: Approve City Manager's Priority Items
votes.notes: Voice vote declared passed without opposition among the six seated members (Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, DeDreana Freeman, Mark-Anthony Middleton, and Vernetta Alston; 7th At-Large seat vacant).
votes.discussion_detail: Referred Item 6 (transit amenities repair and installation contract) back to the administration and scheduled a presentation for Item 10 (Contract ST-285 street repairs and repaving).

votes.item_title: Adopt Majority-Vote Ballot Process for City Council At-Large Vacancy Selection
votes.notes: Split voice vote passed 4-2 among the six seated members present (Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, DeDreana Freeman, Mark-Anthony Middleton, and Vernetta Alston; Javiera Caballero had not yet been appointed to the vacant At-Large seat). No roll call of individual Aye and Nay voters was recorded in the transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted a multi-round majority-vote paper ballot process (taking the top two candidates if no majority emerges on the first ballot, or discussing if tied) rather than ranked-choice voting for filling the vacant At-Large Council seat. An earlier motion on ranked-choice voting at 02:12:00 was followed by extended debate rather than a finalized count before this 4-2 vote.

disagreements.issue: Voting Method for Filling City Council At-Large Vacancy (Ranked-Choice vs. Majority Ballot)
disagreements.summary: The six seated Council members split 4-2 over whether to select the At-Large Council vacancy appointee using a ranked-choice instant-runoff ballot demonstrated by Mayor Pro Tempore Jillian Johnson or a traditional multi-round majority-vote paper ballot.
disagreements.side_a_position: Use a multi-round majority-vote ballot requiring a candidate to win a majority of votes, with live Council discussion between rounds if needed.
side_a_arguments: Charlie Reece raised concerns about ranked-choice potentially appointing a candidate with only three votes and ballot exhaustion.

Mark-Anthony Middleton and colleagues argued ranked-choice was needlessly exotic and confusing to the public compared to Council's prior template, and valued live debate between rounds when candidates are eliminated rather than pre-set automatic second-choice transfers.
disagreements.side_b_position: Use a ranked-choice voting ballot for the seven vacancy finalists.
side_b_arguments: Mayor Pro Tempore Jillian Johnson demonstrated ranked-choice mechanics and supporters viewed it as a fairer system.
Proponents noted it offered Council an opportunity to educate themselves and model ranked-choice voting for the public in the future.
disagreements.resolution: Passed 4-2 by unattributed voice vote at 02:29:46 in favor of the majority-vote ballot method after extended debate and one member agreeing to support majority vote to avoid further delay; individual Aye/Nay votes were not called by roll.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Jan 2, 2018
meetings.executive_summary: At its first regular meeting of 2018 on January 2, the six-member Durham City Council issued ceremonial proclamations recognizing January 2018 as National Mentoring Month and honoring the life and legacy of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. During announcements, Council Member Mark-Anthony Middleton reflected on attending a Bull City United Week of Peace vigil and urged residents to bring proactive gun-violence prevention ideas to Council chambers. Council unanimously approved 6-0 the consent agenda (excluding pulled Item 7), covering the FY 2018-19 budget schedule, HUD grant amendments, Jackson-Pettigrew Street affordable housing financing, bicycle facility design, hydrant meter rates, and the November 2017 bid report. After Transportation Director Terry Bellamy answered a question confirming that federal minority- and women-owned business rules governed pulled Item 7, Council unanimously passed 6-0 the NCDOT grant project ordinance for the downtown transportation study.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Pledge of Allegiance, and Roll Call
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. and led a moment of silent meditation, followed by Boy Scout Troop 461 leading the Pledge of Allegiance at the invitation of Council Member Charlie Reece. The Clerk called the roll, confirming all six seated council members were present.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation Declaring January 2018 as National Mentoring Month
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Charlie Reece read a proclamation signed by Mayor Schewel designating January 2018 as National Mentoring Month in Durham. Doran Langley of the Charles Hamilton Houston Foundation accepted the proclamation alongside representatives of My Brother's Keeper Durham, Movement of Youth / Mentors Carolina, and Men of Vision in McDougald Terrace.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation Honoring the Life of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson read a proclamation honoring Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. and recalling his visits to Durham between 1960 and 1964. Pastor William Lucas, Chair of the Durham Martin Luther King Jr. Steering Committee, accepted the proclamation and noted the 50th anniversary of Dr. King's assassination and upcoming MLK commemorative events.

agenda_items.title: Council Announcements: Gun Violence Vigil and Community Advocacy
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Mark-Anthony Middleton recognized Bull City United for hosting a Week of Peace vigil for gunfire victims and acknowledged Durham's progress on homicides while stressing continuing challenges with gunfire. He urged activists and residents to come to Council chambers with concrete recommendations to prevent gun violence rather than waiting until after tragedies occur.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Minutes, Records Retention, FY18-19 Budget Schedule, HUD Grants, Jackson-Pettigrew Housing, Bike Design, Hydrant Rates, Bid Report)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Schewel read the consent agenda, including council minutes, municipal record retention schedule amendments, the FY 18-19 budget development schedule, FY 2017-18 HUD grant amendments (CDBG, HOME, ESG, and HOPWA), subordinate financing for the Jackson-Pettigrew Street development with Self-Help Ventures Fund and DHIC, Inc., a bicycle facility design master agreement, Chapter 15 hydrant meter deposit and rental rate amendments, and the November 2017 bid report. Item 7 was pulled at a council member's request, and the remaining consent items passed 6-0.

agenda_items.title: City of Durham and NCDOT Grant Project Ordinance for Downtown Transportation Study
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pulled from the consent agenda for clarification, a council member asked why the agenda memo stated the agreement was not reviewed for compliance with Durham's Equal Business Opportunity ordinance. Transportation Director Terry Bellamy explained that because the study uses federal funding, it follows federal minority- and women-owned business regulations rather than the local ordinance, and clarified that an RFQ panel was reviewing submittals while this ordinance simply established grant funding authority; Council approved the item 6-0.

votes.item_title: Adoption of Consent Agenda (Items 1, 3-6, 8-10, excluding pulled Item 7)
votes.notes: Six seated members present prior to filling the vacant At-Large seat.
votes.discussion_detail: After reading the consent agenda and pulling Item 7 at a council member's request, Mayor Schewel entertained a motion to approve the remaining consent items (Items 1, 3-6, and 8-10), which was moved, seconded, and passed unanimously 6-0.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Mayor Steve Schewel during the outgoing City Clerk's final work session, the Durham City Council unanimously approved the City Manager's priority items—referring an electronics recycling contract with Powerhouse Recycling Inc. back to administration and suspending the rules to pass a $4,000 close-out contract extension with Mid-Atlantic Associates Inc. for a 2014–2017 EPA brownfield assessment grant. During agenda review and discussion, Council examined periodic amendments to the 2013 Records Retention Manual, $400,000 in combined funding (with a $30,000 City share) for a Downtown Transportation Study with NCDOT, and the FY 2018–19 budget outreach schedule balancing large community conversations with PAC 1 and PAC 2 requests to retain neighborhood meetings. Public speakers addressed Eno River Association updates and livestreaming/decorum rules for work sessions. Council concluded with an extended debate over the procedures for filling its vacant At-Large seat—agreeing on a strict January 2, 2018, 5:00 PM submission deadline without a mailbox rule and an iterative ranked-choice ballot ranking the top three of seven finalists, while differing on whether to hold public comment on January 2 for all 22 applicants or on January 4 after narrowing the field to seven.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and City Manager Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel acknowledged the outgoing City Clerk's final work session and called roll with Mayor Pro Tempore Jillian Johnson and Council Members Vernetta Alston, Mark-Anthony Middleton, and Charlie Reece recorded as answering present. The City Manager requested suspending the rules to vote on Item 11 (Mid-Atlantic Associates brownfield grant close-out) and referring Item 12 (Powerhouse Recycling electronic equipment agreement) back to administration.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review: HUD Grants, Downtown Transportation Study, and Capital Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Members pulled Item 3 (Records Retention Manual), Item 4 (FY 2018–19 budget schedule), Item 5 (FY 2017–18 HUD CDBG/HOME/ESG/HOPWA grant amendments), and Item 7 (City/NCDOT Downtown Transportation Study). Council highlighted that NCDOT is covering most of the $400,000 Downtown Transportation Study, leaving only a $30,000 City match.

agenda_items.title: Item 11: Mid-Atlantic Associates Inc. EPA Brownfield Assessment Grant Amendment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Charlie Reece noted his general practice of opposing official votes at work sessions but moved to suspend the rules because the $4,000 extension was needed to close out the 2014–2017 EPA grant by year-end and keep Durham's 2018 grant application competitive. Council unanimously suspended the rules and approved the contract amendment.

agenda_items.title: Citizens Matters: Eno River Association and Public Meeting Livestreaming/Decorum
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Robin Jacobs (Executive Director of the Eno River Association) and board Vice President Milo Pyne addressed Council during Citizens Matters. Speaker Chris Tiffany urged Council to revise public meeting decorum rules, stop using the term 'citizen' restrictively, and install permanent cameras to livestream all work sessions and public meetings so officials' behavior is visible to the public.

agenda_items.title: Item 3: Amendments to City Records Retention Manual
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff explained that the North Carolina Division of Archives and History periodically issues minimum retention schedule amendments that must be incorporated into Durham's January 2013 Records Retention Manual. Council asked clarifying questions about the state process and periodic updates.

agenda_items.title: Item 4: FY 2018–19 Budget Development Schedule and PAC Outreach
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff explained outreach negotiations with Durham's Partners Against Crime (PAC) districts after PAC 1 and PAC 2 declined to replace 'Coffees with Council' entirely with three large community conversations. As a middle ground, budget presentations would occur at the three broader community conversations while PAC meetings remain on the schedule for new Council members to introduce themselves and share priorities.

agenda_items.title: City Council At-Large Vacancy Appointment Process and Ranked-Choice Voting
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resuming in the afternoon, Council confirmed that questionnaire attachments must arrive in the Clerk's Office by 5:00 PM on January 2, 2018 with no 'mailbox rule,' and discussed an iterative ranked-choice voting method where members rank their top three of seven finalists with lowest vote-getters eliminated until a majority is reached. Members also debated whether to open public comment on January 2 for all 22 applicants or on January 4 after narrowing to seven finalists before adjourning without a formal vote on the comment schedule.

votes.item_title: Approval of City Manager's Priority Items (Suspend Rules on Item 11; Refer Item 12 Back)
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote; individual member names for mover and seconder were not identified in the transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: Accepted City Manager's request to take up Item 11 for immediate vote and refer Item 12 (Powerhouse Recycling electronic equipment agreement) back to administration.

votes.item_title: Suspend the Rules to Vote on Item 11 (EPA Brownfield Grant Amendment)
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote; seconder was not identified by name.
votes.discussion_detail: Charlie Reece moved to suspend the rules so Council could act at the work session to close out the 2014–2017 EPA grant before year-end.

votes.item_title: Approve Item 11: Mid-Atlantic Associates Inc. Brownfield Grant Contract Amendment
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote; mover and seconder were not identified by name.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved $4,000 contract extension with Mid-Atlantic Associates Inc. to complete close-out tasks for the 2014–2017 US EPA Community-wide Brownfield Assessment Grant.

disagreements.issue: Timing and Format of Public Comment for City Council Vacancy Applicants
disagreements.summary: Council members disagreed on whether and when to schedule dedicated public comment on candidates applying for the vacant At-Large Council seat prior to the January 16 selection.
disagreements.side_a_position: Hold a public comment period on January 2 covering the 22 applicants (e.g., capped at an hour total) so residents and civic groups can weigh in early.
side_a_arguments: January 2 has a light agenda and gives residents without social media access an in-person forum like budget public hearings.
January 16 is too late in the process for public input to influence Council's narrowing and selection.
disagreements.side_b_position: Wait until after narrowing the pool to seven finalists (or limit to six minutes per finalist at the January 4 work session) rather than taking comment on 22 applicants.
side_b_arguments: Allocating six minutes per candidate across 22 applicants is unmanageable.
Some Council members questioned whether supporter speeches would alter evaluations already based on written applications and interviews.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote was taken before Mayor Schewel adjourned the work session at 02:55:04.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Dec 18, 2017
meetings.executive_summary: The six-member Durham City Council unanimously approved 6-0 the consent agenda—including GoDurham replacement buses, HOPWA and Enterprise Community Partners contract amendments, and multiple pedestrian and waterline projects—while receiving public comment on the FY 2018-19 Annual Action Plan amid questions from Council Members Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, Mark-Anthony Middleton, and DeDreana Freeman over shifting CDBG and ESG homelessness dollars toward rapid rehousing and future Dedicated Housing Fund allocations. Council also voted 6-0 on all land-use items, re-designating land around the Venable Center as a local historic landmark, rezoning 5275 North Roxboro Street to Commercial General with a Development Plan, and approving the 93-acre Sagewood and Nichols Farm consolidated annexation. Additionally, Council unanimously adopted 6-0 a resolution supporting the federal Temporary Protected Status (TPS) program and approved 6-0 the timeline, candidate questionnaire, and interview procedures to fill the vacant At-Large Council seat.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Pledge of Allegiance, Recognitions, and NC Commission of Inquiry on Torture Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Troop 451 led the Pledge of Allegiance, and the City Clerk called the roll with all six seated council members present. Mayor Steve Schewel recognized neighborhood health and GirlTrek volunteers and read a proclamation for NC Stop Torture Now regarding the North Carolina Commission of Inquiry on Torture (NCCIT) findings on rendition flights at Johnston County and Global TransPark.

agenda_items.title: City Manager, City Attorney, and City Clerk Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager and City Clerk reported no priority items. City Attorney Patrick Baker notified Council and the public that three documents produced at the December 13 Council Procedures Subcommittee meeting were added to General Business Agenda Item 2 regarding the City Council vacancy.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Duke Energy Intervention, HOPWA Amendment, GoDurham Buses, Water/Sewer & Pedestrian Contracts)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Schewel read the consent agenda titles covering intervention in Duke Energy case E-7 Sub 1146, the Appearance Commission interlocal renewal, a HOPWA contract amendment, Enterprise Community Partners Phase 2, GoDurham replacement buses, Southeast Regional Lift Station engineering, a 2-inch waterline replacement contract, Neighborhood Compass management, North Duke Street/NC 54/South Street pedestrian improvements, and Odyssey Drive and Alpine Road culvert replacements.

agenda_items.title: FY 2018-19 Annual Action Plan Needs Public Hearing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Moved first on the General Business Agenda, Community Development Director Reginald Johnson and Federal Programs Coordinator Wilma Conaway-Jans (ph.) outlined projected HUD entitlements ($1.8M CDBG, $800k HOME, $160k ESG, and $328k HOPWA) ahead of the May 15, 2018 submission. Homeless service providers including Urban Ministries of Durham, Families Moving Forward, and Outstretched Hands—along with Council Members Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, Mark-Anthony Middleton, DeDreana Freeman, and Mayor Steve Schewel—questioned eliminating ~$130,000 in CDBG homelessness funding and dedicating ESG entirely to rapid rehousing prior to Council review of the Focus Strategies report and Dedicated Housing Fund budget proposals.

agenda_items.title: Venable Center Local Historic Landmark Designation (LD170001)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Karla Rosenberg presented Case LD170001 to re-designate land associated with the Venable Center at South Roxboro and East Pettigrew Streets after a 2016 subdivision/recombination inadvertently stripped landmark status from the front courtyard and small annex parking lot, estimating $3,287 in annual city tax revenue impact ($7,650 combined city-county). Applicant representative Charlie Yokely of the McAdams Company confirmed the omission was an unintended clerical overlap.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change — 5275 North Roxboro Street
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Jamie Sunyak presented a request to rezone 1.31 acres (a vacant Burger King site) in the Eno River Basin Overlay from Commercial Neighborhood to Commercial General with a Development Plan capping floor area at 10,000 sq ft and committing to a bus pullout shelter and TIP U-516 right-of-way dedication, unanimously recommended 12-0 by the Planning Commission. Applicant engineer Tim Sivers and owner Dale Reynolds described plans for a water-conserving express car wash paying at least $11/hour plus benefits and employing people with disabilities, while Council Member DeDreana Freeman flagged potential competition with nearby car washes.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation — Sagewood and Nichols Farm
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Jacob Wiggins presented Highland Falls Raleigh LLC's request for utility extension agreements, voluntary annexation effective December 31, 2017, and exact-translation Rural Residential (RR) initial zoning for two contiguous parcels totaling ~93 acres along Doc Nichols Road. Staff noted water/sewer capacity and positive fiscal buildout impact, and confirmed in response to Mark-Anthony Middleton that including Doc Nichols Road right-of-way creates donut holes because an intervening property owner declined annexation.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Supporting the Federal Temporary Protected Status (TPS) Program
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson introduced and read a resolution urging the U.S. Department of Homeland Security to renew TPS for Nicaragua and Haiti and continue protections for the estimated 320,000 national and 13,000 North Carolina TPS holders. Eliazar Posada of El Centro Hispano and Jose Fidel Campos-Sorto of the North Carolina Salvadoran Association thanked Council while urging continued concrete local support.

agenda_items.title: City Council At-Large Vacancy Timeline, Questionnaire, and Interview Rules
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Attorney Patrick Baker reviewed the Procedures Subcommittee recommendations to adopt the vacancy timeline, revised candidate questionnaire (with formatting additions noted by Council Member Vernetta Alston), and applicant interview rules and procedures. On Council Member Charlie Reece's recommendation, Council deferred choosing the final voting/selection method to Thursday's work session.

votes.item_title: Receive Public Comments on FY 2018-19 Annual Action Plan Needs Public Hearing (Item 18)
votes.notes: No funding allocations were adopted at this first needs hearing.
votes.discussion_detail: Following an extended public hearing on CDBG and ESG homelessness service funding allocations, Director Reginald Johnson reminded Mayor Schewel that Council needed to formally vote to receive the public comments. A motion and second passed 6-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Ordinance Designating Venable Center Land as a Local Historic Landmark (LD170001, Item 15)
votes.discussion_detail: After staff and applicant testimony clarified that only the historic building parcel's front courtyard and annex lot—not the rear redevelopment parking lot—were being re-designated, Council closed the hearing and voted 6-0 to adopt the landmark ordinance.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement for 5275 North Roxboro Street Zoning Map Change (Item 16)
votes.discussion_detail: Following questions from Council Member DeDreana Freeman regarding local competition and wage/disability hiring commitments from applicant Dale Reynolds, Council closed the public hearing and unanimously adopted the consistency statement 6-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Ordinance Amending UDO Zoning Map for 5275 North Roxboro Street (Item 16)
votes.discussion_detail: Council adopted the zoning map change from CN to CG(D) with a 10,000 sq ft maximum floor area on a 6-0 vote.

votes.item_title: Adopt Annexation Ordinances and Authorize Utility Extension Agreements for Sagewood and Nichols Farm (Item 17)
votes.discussion_detail: After staff answered Mark-Anthony Middleton's question about donut holes along Doc Nichols Road, Council closed the public hearing and approved the consolidated motion to adopt the annexation ordinances and authorize utility extension agreements 6-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement for Sagewood and Nichols Farm Initial Zoning (Item 17)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the comprehensive plan consistency statement 6-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Initial Zoning Ordinance (RR) for Sagewood and Nichols Farm (Item 17)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the UDO amendment establishing Rural Residential (RR) initial zoning for the 93-acre annexation 6-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Resolution Supporting the Temporary Protected Status (TPS) Program (Item 23)
votes.discussion_detail: Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson read and moved the resolution supporting TPS renewal, with public speakers from El Centro Hispano and the NC Salvadoran Association endorsing the measure. Council passed the resolution 6-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt City Council At-Large Vacancy Timeline, Candidate Questionnaire, and Interview Rules and Procedures (Item 2)
votes.notes: Final vote administered by the retiring City Clerk after 33 years of service.
votes.discussion_detail: After confirming with City Attorney Patrick Baker that all three Procedures Subcommittee attachments (including Vernetta Alston's nominal formatting updates to the questionnaire) could be adopted together while deferring the selection voting method to Thursday's work session, Council approved the motion 6-0.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At his first work session as Mayor, Steve Schewel presided over unanimous procedural votes to launch the City Council At-Large vacancy appointment process—suspending the rules to direct the City Clerk to publish the notice of vacancy, approve the initial application form, and set a December 19, 2017, 5:00 PM filing deadline. Council also heard a resolution circulated for the December 18 meeting supporting the federal Temporary Protected Status (TPS) program for immigrants from Nicaragua, Haiti, Honduras, and El Salvador, and reviewed pulled items including intervening in a Duke Energy rate case, the DataWorks Neighborhood Compass contract, and pedestrian improvement contracts on North Duke Street and Raynor Street. During Citizens Matters, Northeast Central Durham Leadership Council Director Lenore Smith urged Council to remove tire mulch from local playgrounds over lead and cadmium exposure concerns and adopt racial and income equity surfacing criteria, prompting Council to request an equity report on playground surfacing. All votes taken at the work session were unanimous.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and TPS Support Resolution Announcement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel called the meeting to order; roll call recorded Mayor Pro Tempore Jillian Johnson and Council Members Vernetta Alston, Mark-Anthony Middleton, and Charlie Reece present, with Council Member DeDreana Freeman delayed traveling back to town. A Council member announced a draft resolution supporting the federal Temporary Protected Status (TPS) program for immigrants from Nicaragua, Haiti, Honduras, and El Salvador for consideration at the December 18 business meeting.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Item and Agenda Pulled Items Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager noted minor administrative refinements coming for Item 9 (DataWorks contract), which Council approved unanimously. Council reviewed departmental and public hearing items—covering GoDurham replacement buses, HOPWA, Enterprise Community Partners, water management, and annexations—and pulled Items 1, 2, 9, 10, and 13 for discussion.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed (Unanimous voice vote on Manager's item)

agenda_items.title: Citizens Matters: Solicitation Permits and Tire Mulch Playground Equity
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Scott Barnet spoke on solicitation permitting and speed-zone concerns. Lenore Smith (Northeast Central Durham Leadership Council) presented a four-point resolution calling for removing tire mulch at local playgrounds due to lead and cadmium cluster concerns and adopting racial and income equity criteria; Deputy City Manager Bo Ferguson and Assistant Director Tom Dawson addressed product cost and reliability, and Council requested a brief report on playground surfacing equity.

agenda_items.title: Items 1 & 9: Duke Energy Rate Case Intervention and DataWorks Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Charlie Reece questioned the implications of the City becoming an intervening party in the Duke Energy rate case (Item 1). Council also reviewed Item 9 regarding Neighborhood Improvement Services' contract with DataWorks to operate the City's Neighborhood Compass outside City staffing.

agenda_items.title: Items 10 & 13: Pedestrian Improvement Contracts and Contractor Workforce Diversity
agenda_items.discussion_summary: On Item 10 (North Duke Street pedestrian improvements), Deputy City Manager Bo Ferguson and Transportation staff explained long federal project delivery lifecycles, short sidewalk gap construction under 500 feet, and sharing the Durham Bike+Walk Plan's 150 prioritized projects with new Council members. On Item 13 (Raynor Street pedestrian improvements), members discussed employment demographics and the availability of African American civil engineers at contractor Ramey Kemp & Associates.

agenda_items.title: Item 2: City Council At-Large Vacancy Notice and Application Schedule
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council confirmed that the City Charter requires attempting to fill the vacant At-Large seat rather than bypassing directly to a special election. Council Member Charlie Reece moved to suspend the rules in accordance with the procedures manual, and Council unanimously directed the City Clerk to publish the vacancy notice, approved Attachment 6 as the initial application form, and set a December 19, 2017, 5:00 PM deadline.

agenda_items.title: Clerk Search Scheduling, Committee Assignments, and Agenda Adoption
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council coordinated schedules for a December 13 closed session with HR on the City Clerk search, distributed draft Council committee assignments, and unanimously adopted the December 18 business meeting agenda (Consent 1, 3–14; GBA 2; GBA Public Hearings 15–18).

votes.item_title: Approval of City Manager's Priority Item (Item 9 DataWorks Contract Refinements)
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote; mover and seconder were not identified by name.
votes.discussion_detail: Accepted City Manager's notice of minor non-substantive administrative refinements to Item 9 prior to final action.

votes.item_title: Suspend the Rules to Act on City Council Vacancy Process (Item 2)
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote; seconder was not identified by name.
votes.discussion_detail: Charlie Reece moved to suspend the rules to take official action at the work session to initiate the vacancy timeline under the procedures manual.

votes.item_title: Issue Vacancy Notice, Approve Application Form, and Set December 19 Deadline
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote; mover and seconder were not identified by name.
votes.discussion_detail: Directed the City Clerk to publish the notice of vacancy, approved the initial application form (Attachment 6), and set Tuesday, December 19, 2017 at 5:00 PM as the filing deadline.

votes.item_title: Adopt December 18, 2017 City Council Meeting Agenda
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote; mover and seconder were not identified by name.
votes.discussion_detail: Set Consent items 1 and 3–14, General Business Agenda item 2, and GBA Public Hearings 15–18.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Dec 4, 2017
meetings.executive_summary: The December 4, 2017 Durham City Council organizational meeting began with certification of the 2017 municipal election results and farewell tributes to outgoing Mayor Bill Bell, Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden, and Council Members Eddie Davis and Don Moffitt. Newly elected Mayor Steve Schewel and Council Members Mark-Anthony Middleton, Vernetta Alston, and DeDreana Freeman took the oath of office, after which the six-member council unanimously elected Jillian Johnson as Mayor Pro Tempore 6-0. Following a brief recess, Council passed the consent agenda 6-0 and unanimously voted 6-0 after a public hearing to approve Public Finance Authority multifamily housing revenue bonds for the Lynn Haven Apartments affordable housing project.

agenda_items.title: Election Certification and Farewells for Outgoing Mayor and Council Members
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Outgoing Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order and received certified 2017 municipal election results. Council and staff honored outgoing members Don Moffitt, Eddie Davis, Cora Cole-McFadden, and Mayor Bill Bell with plaques and reflections on their tenure covering affordable housing, transit, and financial stewardship.

agenda_items.title: Swearing-In of Newly Elected Mayor and Council Members and Inaugural Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Newly elected Council Members Mark-Anthony Middleton, Vernetta Alston, and DeDreana Freeman, along with Mayor Steve Schewel, took their oaths of office and delivered inaugural remarks thanking outgoing leaders, families, and voters while outlining their shared vision for Durham.

agenda_items.title: Election and Swearing-In of Mayor Pro Tempore
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Charlie Reece moved to designate Council Member Jillian Johnson as Mayor Pro Tempore for the City of Durham. Council approved the designation 6-0, and Johnson took the oath of office surrounded by her family.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (DPAC Oversight, DHA Reappointment, FY17 CAFR, Water Audit, Housing & BPAC Agreements)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a 10-minute recess, Mayor Schewel read consent items covering a DPAC Oversight Committee appointment, Durham Housing Authority Board reappointment, the FY 2017 Comprehensive Annual Financial Report, a Water Management meter disconnect/reconnect audit, a county revenue-reimbursement interlocal agreement, Piedmont-Reynolds loan amendments with Durham Community Land Trustees, BPAC reauthorization, water deposit ordinance updates, the October 2017 bid report, and a Davis Park East median sign license.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing and Resolution Approving Multifamily Housing Revenue Bonds — Lynn Haven Apartments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Community Development Director Reginald Johnson presented a resolution approving the Public Finance Authority's issuance of multifamily housing revenue bonds for the Lynn Haven Apartments affordable housing project. In response to Mayor Schewel's inquiry, developer legal counsel Eric Prostell addressed accompanying housing tax credits, and with no public speakers, Council unanimously adopted the bond resolution 6-0.

votes.item_title: Designate Council Member Jillian Johnson as Mayor Pro Tempore
votes.notes: Mayor Schewel's vacated At-Large seat remained vacant pending the council appointment process.
votes.discussion_detail: At Mayor Schewel's invitation, Council Member Charlie Reece moved to designate Jillian Johnson as Mayor Pro Tempore, which was seconded and approved 6-0.

votes.item_title: Resolution Approving Issuance of Multifamily Housing Revenue Bonds for Lynn Haven Apartments (Item 14)
votes.discussion_detail: Following Community Development Director Reginald Johnson's staff report and developer counsel Eric Prostell's response regarding tax credits, no members of the public signed up to speak; Council closed the hearing and unanimously adopted the resolution 6-0.
